sessions.title: Broken tablets
sessions.desc: After Moses broke the first set of tablets containing the Ten Commandments, what happened to the shattered pieces? The Torah never tells us. The rabbis explored what role the broken tablets continued to play after Moses received a second, unbroken set. Exploring these teachings, we discover that both the whole and the broken were considered sacred.

sessions.title: ‘It Don’t Mean a Thing…’: adventures in Ta’amei Hamikra
sessions.desc: Do you teach Torah and/or read Torah in shul? Discover a revolutionary graphical method of textual analysis (developed by a great 20th-century Tanachist/musicologist, Mechel Perlman) that will take your Torah insight and leyning to a new level. Your approach to Torah will never be the same.

sessions.title: Deck the halls: Shabbat edition
sessions.desc: Get stuck in and help us transform the space for Shabbat! A fun, creative session to make decorations, get crafty and bring a bit of colour and personality to the weekend. Come along, make something, meet people and help us get the space Shabbat-ready.

sessions.title: Write your Jewish story
sessions.desc: A Jewish story can be anything you want it to be – something that you experienced, or imagined. You can define Jewish, and yourself, in any way you want. We will write short pieces and share our writings within our group. This is a free-flowing chance to get creative with your thoughts and words.

sessions.title: Beyond Golda: the women who built Israel
sessions.desc: When thinking about Israel’s early years, we often think of those who declared the state or led governments, but it was also shaped in quieter ways. Women were at the forefront of culture, education and medicine. What they created became part of Israeli society, while their names faded from history. This session uncovers a few of their stories.

sessions.title: Family Havdalah crafts
sessions.desc: Make your own unique besamim (spice) blend, make a paper Havdalah candle and decorate a little becher (Kiddush cup). You can bring these to show to everyone else at Limmud Havdalah!

sessions.title: Welcome to Limmud! (1 of 2)
sessions.desc: From first-timers to long-term Limmudniks, pop by the Wellbeing Hub for a lowdown on this year's festival!

sessions.title: Through a veil: translating the Bible, 1: into Greek – the Septuagint (1 of 4)
sessions.desc: The very first translation of the Bible was made about 300 BCE, in Greek. We'll explore the historical background, including some miracle stories, and find out why some rabbis compared it to the Golden Calf. On the way we'll rediscover a lost Jewish community. No Greek necessary – sample texts in English!

sessions.title: False gods, real cravings: the spiritual wisdom of the second commandment
sessions.desc: 'You shall have no other gods before Me.' Is idolatry a relic of the ancient world, or is it still alive and well? Drawing on Torah, contemporary thinkers and insights from addiction recovery, we'll explore the second commandment as a living text about desire, loyalty and spiritual hunger. All are welcome; no background in Jewish text is needed.

sessions.title: Kabbalat Shabbat – a very successful innovation
sessions.desc: Kabbalat Shabbat was an innovation of 16th-century kabbalists. We'll see how it spread through beautiful booklets, still preserved; what it meant to kabbalists; why Prague welcomed the Shabbat bride with musical instruments, and why other communities resisted this.

sessions.title: Beyond resilience: wisdom from shipwrecked rabbis
sessions.desc: What do we do when the world feels unsteady and so much lies beyond our control? Through rabbinic texts and contemporary voices, we’ll explore different ways of meeting uncertainty and disruption, asking what it means to endure difficult moments, where resilience comes from, and whether upheaval can open up new ways of living.

sessions.title: Now what happens?
sessions.desc: Are you a Jew by choice? Come and share your experiences of integrating into Jewish life after the beit din (rabbinical court), good and bad. Help us understand how the community can help you settle in, what you need to grow your Jewish life and how you can help others. Run by the founder of LISHMAH, a new organisation supporting Jews by choice.

sessions.title: Seeking the story of Psalm 23
sessions.desc: Why is this psalm traditionally sung on Shabbat afternoon? And why is it recited ‘for someone who is ill’? Using a multifaceted literary approach, we will study this passionate little six-verse psalm, and uncover its dramatic undertones. Where is the ‘Valley of the Shadow of Death’ today? And how do we survive it? Join our flock to find out…

sessions.title: Friday night delight
sessions.desc: Come and join Caroline for stories and songs especially for Erev Shabbat (Friday evening). If you’re tired after your journey up to Birmingham please join us to relax and listen, and if you are full of energy, there’s plenty of chance to join in with singing and acting. All welcome, but especially suitable for families with young children.

sessions.title: Sinai’s fine print: when breaking the law is the law
sessions.desc: Tehilim (Psalms) says: ‘Et la’asot la’Shem, heferu Toratecha’ (it is a time to act for G-d; they have violated your Torah). Everyone agrees on the words, but no one agrees on what the sentence means. This paradoxical verse is the one halachic decisors cite to start a revolution – one that stays inside tradition (that’s what we Jews do).

sessions.title: Jews and alphabets
sessions.desc: The alphabet is perhaps the most sophisticated and influential technology you have never thought about. It has played a central role in Jewish culture from earliest times. We will consider the birth of the alphabet, alphabetical structures, why the Hebrew alphabet is not really an alphabet at all, and what all this means in a digital age.

sessions.title: Assassin's Creed – four assassinations that shaped Zionism/Israel
sessions.desc: Assassination as a tool of politics can be shocking and divisive but certainly changes the course of history. Zionism and Israel have had their share. The 1995 murder of Yitzhak Rabin is the arch-example, but in this session we’ll explore four other assassinations that altered the course of Zionism and Israel – from the Yishuv to the modern state.

sessions.title: Chassidishe tisch
sessions.desc: Come join a Chassidish-style tisch run by Limmud’s very own Avi Grant. You do not need to know the songs to join; come along and learn as we go or just enjoy some tunes. This will be an upbeat non-instrumental session.

sessions.title: Oneg
sessions.desc: Looking for a place to hang out, meet new people and make friends? Join us for a relaxed oneg (Shabbat social gathering) with games, good company, snacks and drinks. Come along, get to know others and enjoy a fun, informal way to start the festival over Shabbat together!

sessions.title: Things that go bump in the shtetl
sessions.desc: Come hear some of the strangest, spookiest and most intriguing ghost stories from Jewish folklore and tradition. From dybbuks (malevolent spirits) and wandering souls to haunted homes and supernatural encounters, we'll explore what Jewish stories can tell us about death, memory, belief and the things that linger.

sessions.title: Zemer tune-swap
sessions.desc: ‘I have this wonderful Yah Ribon I’ve never heard anyone else sing.’ We’re blessed with a wide array of tunes for zemirot (Shabbat table songs) – let's circulate them! Want the confidence to start singing, or new tunes to sing? Want to spread a niche tune to Shabbat tables far and wide? All levels of familiarity with texts and tunes warmly welcome.

sessions.title: Serah bat Asher: memory and redemption
sessions.desc: Serah bat Asher is a mysterious figure: from gently delivering news of Joseph's survival to her presence at the Exodus and beyond, she bridges past and future, loss and hope. What can Serah teach us about the power of remembrance in shaping redemption? Join us to uncover the wisdom of this overlooked female figure and her enduring relevance.

sessions.title: The ascents of Jewish peoplehood – a new educational approach
sessions.desc: Beit midrash-style workshop introducing ‘The Ascents of Jewish Peoplehood’, a new educational model from ANU – Museum of the Jewish People for exploring Jewish identity and belonging. Through chavruta study and source sheets, participants will examine core aspects of Jewish identity and reflect on their own connection to the Jewish story.

sessions.title: Family Shabbat morning
sessions.desc: Join us for a joyful Shabbat morning of singing, learning and connecting. Together we’ll discover this week’s Torah portion and reflect on the theme of blessings for our families through thoughtful, creative activities.

sessions.title: What do we say about the dead when the living are still arguing?
sessions.desc: When someone dies, the stories we tell about their life can bring comfort, but can also be contested. Drawing on Jewish mourning and the experience of accompanying people through loss, this session explores how we honour grief without simplifying a person’s life or telling others how to mourn – whether in a family, a community or the public eye.

sessions.title: Caught, not taught: what the next generation learns by watching us
sessions.desc: Every Friday night, parents put their hands on their children’s heads and bless them to be like Ephraim and Menashe. Few of us learned that from a book. We caught it. Drawing on Vayechi and Haym Soloveitchik’s 'Rupture and Reconstruction', let’s discuss what happens when that chain breaks, and what Judaism our children are catching from us.

sessions.title: Are we hastening or delaying the coming of the Messiah?
sessions.desc: 'Meshiach' (the Messiah) is more on the agenda of the Jewish world today than it’s been for a while. We’ll look at the sources to learn how we should deal with this fascinating yet mysterious theological issue.

sessions.title: Vayechi: when the truth won't set you free
sessions.desc: Explore today's Torah reading through the lens of midrash. We'll learn what midrash is as we unpack a striking midrash on this week's reading, asking: what facts do we want to know, and what truths might be better left unknown? L'ilui nishmat Shaul Ben Yehuda Arieh / In loving memory of Shaul Berkowitz z"l.

sessions.title: Niggun workshop: singing without words
sessions.desc: A playful, welcoming introduction to niggunim: Jewish melodies sung without words. We’ll learn and sing a few niggunim together, explore how melody can create connection without language, and experiment with listening, repetition and harmony. No musical experience or singing ability required.

sessions.title: Off the derech, finding our way
sessions.desc: This session is for anyone who grew up Modern Orthodox and no longer is. I'm a ‘cultural Jew’ – engaged with Judaism as a Jewish cultural worker, and still feel spiritually homeless. We'll discuss the communities we've found since, where we feel at home and where we don't, and what a strict halachic upbringing leaves you to work out on your own.

sessions.title: Finding hope: Talmudic lessons of resilience
sessions.desc: The Jewish community is living through some difficult times. Of course, this is not new for us as a people. The rabbis of the Talmud knew a thing or two about difficult times and still told stories of people who refused to despair. We turn to these texts to ask how they understand hope: not as waiting for better days, but as a roadmap for action.

sessions.title: A breath of fresh air
sessions.desc: Grab a hot drink and wrap up warm for some fresh air and an amble around the hotel grounds! The walk will take place along a wheelchair-accessible route.

sessions.title: Progressive Jewish approaches to obligation
sessions.desc: How might Progressive Jews articulate an approach to commandments, rituals and obligations? If you take religious Judaism seriously but don’t accept the predicates of Orthodoxy, what kind of language can be used to express a theology of commitment? Michael Marmur suggests a way of grappling with this persistent and crucial question.

sessions.title: Esther: explored
sessions.desc: Does the book of Esther pass the Bechdel test? And other important questions.

sessions.title: Parashat Vayechi – the passing of an era
sessions.desc: As the book of Genesis draws to a close, Jacob and Joseph look back at their lives – and forward to the future of the Jewish people. What can we learn from the successes and the broken dreams, the triumphs and regrets of our ancestors?

sessions.title: Old (and Young) Jews telling jokes!
sessions.desc: We all love those traditional, Jewish jokes, and nothing brings us together more than laughter. This is an opportunity to share our favourites, discuss why they tickle our kosher funny bones, and explore the themes that flow through our humour. We’re the funniest people in the world!

sessions.title: The genocidaire as a moral person
sessions.desc: Genocide perpetrators are often seen as fundamentally immoral. Yet comparative research shows they are often guided by specific moral concerns. This finding enables a better understanding of the crime, and therefore facilitates prevention. Training in moral autonomy seems especially promising in furthering resistance to genocide.

sessions.title: Family singalong
sessions.desc: Join the Families Team for a lively, interactive singalong for all ages! Share favourite songs, discover new tunes, and enjoy making music together in a warm and welcoming environment.

sessions.title: Shabbat mindfulness
sessions.desc: Discover Shabbat as a time to pause, breathe, and simply be. Through gentle mindfulness practices rooted in Jewish tradition, we’ll explore gratitude, presence, and ways to bring Shabbat’s stillness into the rest of the week.

sessions.title: Leading from the middle
sessions.desc: Especially in liberal Judaism, tefillah experiences are so often offered in a hyper-frontal, presentational manner – think: clergy on the raised bimah, congregants watching from the rows/pews. Come learn the philosophy and best practices to change this dynamic, leading instead from the middle to facilitate broader and better group engagement.

sessions.title: Seuda Shlishit
sessions.desc: Join us for Seuda Shlishit (third meal)! Come wash, grab a bite, and enjoy some food and conversation with the community. Drop in whenever you can – there’s no need to miss any sessions. Pop by, eat, chat and carry on with your Shabbat.

sessions.title: How music impacted on the Abayudaya youth
sessions.desc: We will explore how, following the fall of dictator Idi Amin, the introduction of new niggunim (traditional Jewish melodies) transformed the tefillah experience, revitalised synagogue worship, and attracted the younger generation back to the synagogue, contributing to significant growth in the community.

sessions.title: Who knows six? I know six!
sessions.desc: Six are the sections of the Mishnah. But hold on… what exactly are the ‘shisha sidrei mishna’? Learn about each section by studying its opening mishnah and think about how the Mishnah, the very first written collection of oral traditions, is organised and what it contains. Next seder night, we will finally be able to sing truthfully, ‘I know six’!

sessions.title: Tikkun Am: what does it mean to heal a nation?
sessions.desc: Come along for a discursive session about Jewish peoplehood and building bridges within the Jewish community, looking primarily at the modern concept of Tikkun Am, 'repairing the nation'. We will learn where this concept comes from, think openly about how we might work towards it, and interrogate whether it is even a worthy goal.

sessions.title: The ant, the lizard and the locust
sessions.desc: Actionable personal and professional development lessons from our smallest teachers. How does scripture use the natural world to teach topics including strategy, alignment, and resilience?

sessions.title: From parchment to pixels: 900 years in the evolution of education
sessions.desc: Ever wondered how page design changes how we learn? No Talmud background required for this visual journey across nine centuries! Using rare National Library of Israel sources, we’ll see how texts evolved from medieval parchment to print to smartphone apps, and how ever-changing page layouts opened ancient books to new audiences in each generation.

sessions.title: ‘A twisted candle with many lights’ – ease into Havdalah b’yachad
sessions.desc: As our blissful Shabbat Limmud draws to a close, let’s ease into Havdalah b’yachad (together). Come and join Caroline for some Havdalah songs and stories. Suitable for all – especially those families with young children.

sessions.title: Board games
sessions.desc: Don't be bored! Come and play some games! Solo Limmudniks encouraged to attend.

sessions.title: Communal Havdalah
sessions.desc: A special moment at Limmud. Havdalah (meaning ‘separation’) is how we say farewell to Shabbat for another week. We bring the whole Limmud community together to sing, dance and look ahead to the rest of Limmud Festival.

sessions.title: Why I'm right and you're wrong
sessions.desc: A funny, practical guide to one of the most vital skills we need right now: disagreeing without deciding everyone else is an idiot. Drawing on new research from More in Common and University College London, this session explores why disagreement feels so hostile, what we get wrong about each other, and how to argue better. No compulsory group hug.

sessions.title: Too much information? The evil eye and social media
sessions.desc: From curated Instagram feeds to LinkedIn humblebrags, modern life encourages us to make ourselves visible and invite the gaze of others. This discussion explores the Jewish concept of Ayin Hara (the Evil Eye) and asks what happens when ancient warnings against flaunting success collide with a culture of self-promotion and constant public exposure.

sessions.title: Ireland, IRA and antisemitism – how Ireland's politics got caught up in the Israeli-Palestinian conflict
sessions.desc: Ireland is portrayed in the media as the most antisemitic country in Europe. But is it? Learn about the curious projection of the independence struggle on the Israeli-Palestinian conflict, the Irish connections with the Nazis and the PLO, and the only Irish pogrom.

sessions.title: Who gets to belong? Building queer Jewish community in Europe
sessions.desc: Ariel Heller was helping build Keshet Europe from scratch when Italy Pride put Jewish belonging in the headlines – and him in the spotlight. What’s it like to become a public voice for an identity people are arguing about? Ariel shares what he learned about visibility, pressure and building a community when the story suddenly gets bigger than you.

sessions.title: Speak, stay silent or choose your cause? Public figures and injustice
sessions.desc: When global injustice dominates the news, public figures face pressure to respond. Does a platform create responsibility to speak, even without expertise? Or can speaking oversimplify, while silence leaves others unheard? Is choosing one cause principled, selective, or both? This session tests the arguments without assuming one right answer.

sessions.title: How to covertly join the Rabbanut
sessions.desc: Preceded by a whistle-stop tour of the oral Torah, learn an excerpt of the surprising laws of meat and milk through paired and group textual study of the Shulchan Aruch. Suitable for all levels, no Hebrew knowledge required. Be a part of the conversations our ancestors have passed down through the generations, as my father passed them down to me. L’ilui nishmat Tuvia Gershon ben Shmuel Chaim / In loving memory of Keith Jeremy Posner.

sessions.title: Finding your voice: music, authenticity, and the courage to be heard
sessions.desc: We all have a voice, whether or not we consider ourselves singers. Through music, storytelling, reflection, and interactive exercises, we'll explore what it means to express ourselves authentically. Together, we'll discover how finding our unique voice can deepen our relationships and inspire others. No musical experience is necessary.

sessions.title: Non-Zionist listening and processing circle
sessions.desc: A quiet space for anyone who feels uncomfortable with uncritical support for Israel. Each participant can speak and be heard without argument, judgement or condemnation. This is not a debating forum, but a safe and accepting space where we can express our feelings and emotions honestly and listen to each other with compassion and respect.

sessions.title: Three questions about Israel: belonging, complexity and responsibility
sessions.desc: Can we belong without agreeing? Can we embrace Israel’s complexity and stay connected? Join me to explore three questions in Israel education: belonging and criticism, complexity and simple answers, and personal identity and collective responsibility. We won’t solve Israel’s complexities in an hour, but we can make room to explore them together.

sessions.title: 'It is a tree of life to those who hold fast to it...' (Proverbs 3:18)
sessions.desc: Holding fast to the 'Tree of Life' means ensuring Liberal Jewish values aren't taught in isolation. Serving as a school rabbi across all ages offers a unique lens on guiding students from early childhood to graduation, shaping them into compassionate, engaged Jewish adults.

sessions.title: Listening circle: how are we, really?
sessions.desc: What has it felt like to be part of the Jewish community recently? This is a space to say how it’s been for you and hear others’ experiences. We’ll each have uninterrupted time to speak, listening without judgement, response or comment. We hope to leave feeling heard, more connected and with a little more space to think. (Maximum ten participants.)

sessions.title: Magnified? Sanctified? Learn Aramaic through Kaddish
sessions.desc: What are we actually saying when we say kaddish, and does it matter? Why is one of the more iconic prayers in our tradition in a language so few of us understand? Let’s find out by working through the grammar and vocabulary of the text and discussing contemporary liturgical translations.

sessions.title: Make a salad
sessions.desc: Inspired by a 1962 performance art piece by Alison Knowles, Limmud will be making salad. Become part of a living salad machine to create, consume, and contemplate. We will be exploring themes of community, nourishment, and participatory performance by making and then eating a big. fat. salad.

sessions.title: Nova, Brooklyn, Tijuana: the hidden Jewish psychedelic care network
sessions.desc: Over the past decade, Jewish communities in the US and Israel have quietly built their own psychedelic care networks where mainstream medicine fell short. Through three real journeys (a Nova festival survivor, a Hasidic man in Brooklyn facing opioid addiction, and an IDF reservist with PTSD), discover who is filling the gaps, and how.

sessions.title: ADHD, rejection sensitive dysphoria and more!
sessions.desc: ADHD is a joy... some of the time. Paul will take you on a journey through an ADHD coaching lens, tackling topics as varied as rejection sensitive dysphoria, reasonable adjustments in the workplace, job hunting, and the different priorities that an ADHDer may experience in comparison to neurotypical folk. There will be time for questions.

sessions.title: When Anger Finds a Rhythm
sessions.desc: An interactive workshop on turning protest, anger and personal experience into spoken word. Spoken-word artist Yossi Zabari shares some of his own work, breaks down how it was built, and guides participants through shaping an idea, finding its rhythm, and creating a short piece of their own.

sessions.title: Sharks before Shark Tank: the Limmud pitch den
sessions.desc: Israel's Dragons' Den first called investors 'sharks'. Got a startup, social or community idea? Bring a two-minute pitch! Slots are first come, first served. A panel of experienced Limmud founders and investors will give direct, constructive feedback, Israeli-style. Top pitches win mentoring. Or just come to listen, learn and vote!

sessions.title: Let me be Qallir – a brief introduction to the world of piyyut
sessions.desc: For centuries, the most prominent form of new Jewish liturgy was the piyyuṭ, or liturgical poem. Dozens of varieties of unique piyyuṭim are still found among the many rites of Judaism. But we used to recite many more than we do now. Where did they fit in, where did they go, and can we bring them back? Let's dive into the piyyuṭ world together.

sessions.title: Humperdinck's Hansel and Gretel – antisemitism lying beneath the beloved fairy tale?
sessions.desc: Is there antisemitism lurking beneath Hansel and Gretel? This illustrated talk with music and photos investigates the darker side of the opera in the context of nineteenth-century German antisemitism, exploring the evidence, its modern interpretations, and whether it changes the way we hear a work we thought we knew. With live singing.

sessions.title: Stamford Hell
sessions.desc: Join Charlie on their journey out of an insular Charedi community, told through visual art and illustrations from their (unpublished) graphic novel.

sessions.title: Build it up – see it fall and UNO challenge
sessions.desc: Come along and chill out with a game of Jenga. A game of skill and dexterity. Build it up and see who can move the most bricks before moving the one that makes it fall. Play UNO, the card game loved all over the world by all ages. Or you can bring your own and introduce us to your favourite game. It's a great opportunity to relax and have some fun.

sessions.title: Jews and the printing press – a 15th-century tech revolution
sessions.desc: In 1444 a Jew in Avignon was among the first to learn the art of 'Artificial Writing'. Printing enabled international projects like the Shulchan Aruch, made by Jews in Safed, Venice and Egypt working together. We'll meet young girls who typeset prayer books and tell of their plight, and see how Christian Bible chapters suddenly enter Jewish books.

sessions.title: Russian-speaking Jewry: 21st-century luftmenschen or an integral part of Jewish peoplehood?
sessions.desc: Who are the people we have come to call ‘Russian-speaking Jews’? How did this distinctive group emerge, and how do its members define their identity today? We will explore the formation and evolution of Russian-speaking Jewry, with a particular focus on the profound changes it has undergone since the beginning of Russia’s war against Ukraine.

sessions.title: Limmud's great big gameshow!
sessions.desc: Bits of your favourite panel and game shows have been given some Limmud sparkle. Join us to find out what points make, your starter for ten, and what you could have won. It’ll be super, smashing, great!

sessions.title: What it was like in Chelm 200 years ago, and what it's like today. Celebrating yom tovim, beating extreme cold and exchanging idiocies
sessions.desc: Hear some stories about Chelm, the 'village of idiots', in Eddie's own shaggy-dog style – some clever, comical, pathetic, poignant and idiotic. Some of the stories are legends, but many are made up and set in present-day Chelm, now a pleasant tourist centre. Try to complete the limerick: 'There was a young man from Chell-em' and bring it with you!

sessions.title: Through a veil: translating the Bible, 2: into Aramaic – the Targums (2 of 4)
sessions.desc: When Jews started speaking Aramaic, they had to start translating the Bible. We’ll explore how these translations developed into a special type of Jewish literature still used today, and how their unique style still influences some modern translations. No Aramaic needed – sample texts in English, from sedate to baroque!

sessions.title: Radical amazement: the essence of spirituality within intergenerational relationships
sessions.desc: Drawing on her work and recent chapter in the 'International Handbook of the Religious, Moral and Spiritual Dimensions in Education', Judith seeks to ignite that sense of belonging and harmony, with others, with nature, with the divine, and with oneself, that gives life meaning and purpose. Is this the magic formula for living in radical amazement?

sessions.title: Israeli Jewry vs Diaspora Jewry
sessions.desc: Am Yisrael (the Jewish people) is such a small people, but with a big division. There is a certain lack of connection between Israeli and Diaspora Jewry, and it has been like that for a long time. However, today we are living through an even rougher time in terms of that division, and each one of the worlds has been impacted by 7 October.

sessions.title: A woman's voice is indecent?
sessions.desc: The Orthodox prohibition against listening to women singing is not as simple as it seems. The lecture will explore the history of women's song from biblical times to modern-day rabbis who deal with the paradox that many observant Jews regularly listen to vocal concerts and even participate in mixed choirs – occasionally even in synagogues!

sessions.title: The joy of making music together
sessions.desc: An interactive musical experience where the audience becomes part of the music. Inspired by the Jewish tradition of singing together, and drawing on melodies from different musical worlds, we'll create a shared musical experience full of energy, joy and connection.

sessions.title: Mensch or machine
sessions.desc: Four hundred years ago, Rabbi Loew shaped a protector from Vltava clay and gave it a word to live by. Tonight the golem wakes again, built from code, and asks questions. Who wrote its rules? Can it refuse? An audio-visual retelling of the Prague legend for the age of AI.

sessions.title: Vayarutz vayomer: he ran and he talked – or run and chat (1 of 4)
sessions.desc: If you fancy a chance to stretch your legs as well as your minds then do join us for this outdoor run. We can meet new people and discuss Jewish topics, Limmud sessions, running schedules or just enjoy being outside. Be prepared to run for an hour and maybe get muddy.

sessions.title: Good morning, Limmud!
sessions.desc: Limmud Festival meets breakfast TV! Join our studio audience every morning for an insider’s scoop on the events of the previous day, hot takes from some of your favourite Limmud presenters, a forecast of the day’s highlights and lots of silliness and shtick.

sessions.title: Liberal Zionism – it's an oxymoron, right?
sessions.desc: Many people like to describe themselves as liberal (or even socialist) Zionists. But can you be both a liberal-progressive and a Zionist? Or is it an oxymoron, like military intelligence? We'll delve into the writings of Hannah Arendt, Martin Buber and some others to see what they thought of Jewish nationalism.

sessions.title: The boy who drew Auschwitz
sessions.desc: Thomas Geve was deported to Auschwitz as a 13-year-old Jewish boy from Berlin and survived 22 months in various camps. Upon liberation, he depicted his experiences in over 80 detailed drawings. After the war, he lived in London then Haifa. The story will be told by his sister, with clips of Thomas Geve and the projection of some of his drawings.

sessions.title: How ChatGPT could make your synagogue £50,000
sessions.desc: What happens when you apply AI to the boring stuff? Drawing on experience with the Jewish Community of Stockholm, we’ll explore how AI can transform synagogue admin, websites, calendars, communications and fundraising – and the security, governance and cultural barriers that can stop it happening.

sessions.title: Hop on, hop off: a Jewish campus tour
sessions.desc: Hop on for a campus tour with no flights required. From Tel Aviv to Manchester, Haifa to Leeds and Jerusalem to Birmingham, we’ll meet students navigating identity, belonging, activism and community. Through real-life dilemmas and conversation, we’ll explore what Jewish student life looks like in Israel and the UK.

sessions.title: Considering the work of Achille Mbembe I (1 of 2)
sessions.desc: We’ll read selected passages from Mbembe's books about the human condition in this technological moment, and take note of his route to a thinkable future via an unflinching look at moral and environmental breakdown. We’ll enjoy some of his poetic prose on dark things where it’s difficult to identify who and what is acting and how we are implicated.

sessions.title: Mindfulness for Jews | part 1: between the itch and the scratch (1 of 3)
sessions.desc: The world is loud, fast and demands our endless attention. Our tradition builds in pauses, but do we take them? This session invites us to slow down and discover something that's been available to us all along. Drawing on ancient wisdom and modern neuroscience, we'll explore what's possible, and try it for ourselves. All are welcome.

sessions.title: Anxiety and hope: a Progressive rabbi in Israel
sessions.desc: The categories of anxiety and hope are key engines of Jewish creativity. Relating to both, we will ask: What are the prospects for Israel to be a decent society? Can one speak of Israel today as ‘the first flowering of our redemption’? Michael Marmur will suggest some ways of navigating this political and ethical minefield.

sessions.title: Wake up your body and soul!
sessions.desc: Fusing the best early morning practices with ancient Jewish wisdom, this will be a shacharit that will set us all off to a great new day at Limmud. Expect the familiar, alongside the creative and the new. Everybody welcome.

sessions.title: Darchei shalom: balancing personal religious observance and relationship with others · Limmud's Beit Midrash (1 of 4)
sessions.desc: Talmud in the original in three groups (beginners, intermediate and advanced), each with a skilled teacher. Learn the structure of a passage, its arguments, literary power and relevance for building diverse communities today. Begin with an intro from Rahel. More on the Beit Midrash in the handbook/app – or just come for one day or stay all week.

sessions.title: 'Israel in Song' – a video presentation
sessions.desc: An hour of the early traditional songs of Israel from the times of the pioneers who built the towns and villages and tilled the soil. Songs of Israel's War of Independence, the paratroopers who liberated East Jerusalem in the Six-Day War and soldiers who defended Israel in the Yom Kippur War with a backdrop of breathtaking scenery.

sessions.title: Shiru! Two parts, three parts, no pressure...
sessions.desc: Fancy a sing? Join our scratch choir! Together, we'll learn a selection of texts in multiple parts, all by ear. No auditions, no sheet music, no previous experience needed. If you enjoy singing and are happy to hold a tune, simply bring your voice, your enthusiasm, and a willingness to listen! We'll sing simply for the joy of making music together.

sessions.title: Hidden treasures of the London School of Jewish Studies
sessions.desc: When was the earliest UK Hebrew machzor (festival prayer book) printed? Who wrote the first British Jewish cookbook? Discover treasures from Jewish history – the first Hebrew concordance (1523), 1820s pamphlets, Nazi revisionist history, post-war restitution, and the Survivor’s Talmud – a journey through the London School of Jewish Studies library.

sessions.title: Talmud Digest – 20 rabbinic stories in pocket-sized comics
sessions.desc: 'Talmud Digest: Pocket-Sized Comics' is an accessible, illustrated introduction to selected Talmudic stories and ideas. Combining humour, storytelling, and visual design, it makes complex Jewish texts engaging and approachable for contemporary readers, both beginners and experienced learners.

sessions.title: Nightmares of a posek: when an angel amended the Shulchan Aruch
sessions.desc: A great decisor of Jewish law needs rock-solid logic and airtight arguments. That is, unless an angel – the Mishnah personified – appears in a dream to make you reverse your halachic decision. No, don't worry, this didn’t happen to me. It happened to the greatest halacha hero of all time, Rabbi Yossef Karo, author of the Shulchan Aruch.

sessions.title: Jewish students, in their own words: campus, community and everything in between
sessions.desc: 80 university Jewish societies. 10,000 Jewish students. One union. Countless opinions. Every kind of Jewish student comes and the Union of Jewish Students (UJS) represents them all. How does that work? Put your questions, hot takes and curveballs to UJS president Raphi Leon and students from across the UK. Attendance optional, questions compulsory.

sessions.title: The hidden Torah of Leonard Cohen: one song
sessions.desc: Leonard Cohen wasn’t just a singer-songwriter – he was a mysterious midrashic excavator, weaving Jewish ideas and texts into hauntingly beautiful poetry and music. We’ll listen to one of his songs and then dig deep into his reimagining of a familiar story. A session for devoted fans or those new to his work.

sessions.title: Protected, yet restricted: disability and religious participation in Jewish texts
sessions.desc: Leviticus forbids insulting a deaf person (19:14), yet bars priests with a mum (‘blemish’) from some Temple duties (21:16–23). Can someone be protected by the law while denied authority within it? With Mishnah Chagigah 1:1, we separate protection, exemption and permission, then turn to synagogues today. No Hebrew needed.

sessions.title: Our very own Lashon HaKodesh: prayer book Jewish English
sessions.desc: What is Prayer Book Jewish English and is it a sacred language? Hear about and discuss Sarah's research on the multifaceted linguistic landscape of Hebrew-English siddurim. We'll debate how the divine name should be represented, how to spell C(h)/xan(n)uk/ca(h), what our prayer books say about us as English-speaking Jews, and more.

sessions.title: When the promise survives: cruel optimism and biblical kingship
sessions.desc: Why do we stay attached to a job, relationship or political order when what we rely on to make life better is also wearing us down? Berlant calls this cruel optimism. Biblical kingship lets us follow that bind across centuries. Reading 1 Samuel, Sanhedrin 20b and the Ishbitzer Rebbe, we ask how promises of the good life survive and change.

sessions.title: Desert Island Discs, live at Limmud: Castaway with Sarah Sackman
sessions.desc: In the spirit of the BBC classic, [a guest castaway] shares the eight pieces of music, the book and the luxury item they'd take to a desert island, and the stories behind them. Woven through are the threads of Jewish life, identity and memory that connect us as a community. Expect warmth, surprise and insight.

sessions.title: The Valkyries don't ride to Tel Aviv – why Israel 'cancelled' Wagner (1 of 2)
sessions.desc: 25 years ago, Daniel Barenboim conducted Wagner in Israel, challenging a decades-old taboo and sparking a firestorm of controversy. Why was (and is) Wagner effectively ‘cancelled’ in the Jewish state? Is refusing to play an antisemitic composer an act of Holocaust memory, sensitivity to survivors or an anachronistic denial of cultural freedom?

sessions.title: Do not destroy: ecology art through a Jewish lens
sessions.desc: An illustrated talk on how Jewish thought and artists have viewed the living world, and what that tradition asks of us now. No art background needed. From Genesis’s call to till and guard the earth, the land’s rest year, and the New Year of the Trees, to repairing the world as care for creation, we will discover Jewish ecology pioneers and artists.

sessions.title: A psychotherapist and a rabba walk into a session – take two
sessions.desc: We're back! First launched at Festival in 2022, this session on love, psychology, Torah, and where they overlap will be led by Shimmy Feintuch, a professional psychotherapist, and Yaffa Epstein, an Orthodox rabba. Join us for a text-based, psychologically insightful, and fun conversation.

sessions.title: Lake walk
sessions.desc: Escape cabin fever and come stretch your legs for a refreshing nature walk around the beautiful iconic industrial park lake. Solo Limmudniks encouraged to attend.

sessions.title: Sketch and stretch
sessions.desc: Join us for a relaxed outdoor drawing session where we'll sketch what we see on our walk around Pendigo Lake! No prior drawing experience necessary and materials will be provided.

sessions.title: From fringe to force: the new far right in Europe and the UK
sessions.desc: From Brussels to Bucharest, Tbilisi to the UK, how is the far right moving from fringe to force? Leon Saltiel, Alina Bricman, Teona Dalakishvili and Amos Schonfield bring perspectives from the UN, EU affairs and Jewish communal life to examine the movements, rhetoric and political shifts reshaping Europe – and how communities can respond.

sessions.title: Can you use maths to model tikkun olam?
sessions.desc: Tikkun olam asks us to work to repair the world, but the systems we live in are complicated, interconnected, and full of surprises. We will explore how mathematical models help us think about such systems: ecosystems, social networks, and communities, and target intervention where it might actually help. No maths background is needed.

sessions.title: Healing beyond the border: from Tijuana to Tel Aviv – psychedelic healing for IDF veterans
sessions.desc: Israeli veterans with PTSD are finding psychedelic healing abroad, from Or Haim in Tijuana to Nevut's work with lone soldier veterans in Colorado. Explore the Diaspora networks making this possible, and how Israeli clinicians are preparing to bring these treatments home.

sessions.title: Group singing workshop
sessions.desc: Join Ariella Zeitlin for a group workshop. Think Kululam-style (mass group singing): I lead the room through simple, repeatable melodies until the whole space is singing together, layering harmonies as people find their footing. It's less concert, more communal exhale: the point isn't to sound good, it's to feel connected.

sessions.title: Relational communities: what it actually *tachlis* means to build communities full of people who do the work
sessions.desc: This is for folks in community leadership who want to find and develop other people to actually participate in the work, which Ron Wolfson describes as 'how to transform the model of twentieth-century Jewish institutions into twenty-first-century relational communities offering meaning and purpose, belonging and blessing.'

sessions.title: Intro to Mahloket Matters: the Jewish value of constructive disagreement (1 of 3)
sessions.desc: In this session, come learn the building blocks of the Pardes Institute of Jewish Studies' curriculum on constructive disagreement. This curriculum features Jewish text, social science, and practical skills for encountering people and ideas that are different from us.

sessions.title: 18 Dimensions of Jewish Life in Europe
sessions.desc: Do you oversee, run or manage a communal organisation in the UK or Europe? Do you deal with Jewish education? Can you define your core goal and purpose? This workshop will introduce 18 Dimensions of Jewish Life: a European interpretation of an innovative framework built by M2 in the USA to guide and assist your strategy, direction and mission.

sessions.title: Through a veil: translating the Bible, 3: into European languages – the politics of translation during the Reformation (3 of 4)
sessions.desc: The Protestant Reformation brought an explosion of Bible translations in its wake. Some of the most intense battles for control of Bible translation were fought in England, and we’ll explore the politics of the King James Version and the lessons it can teach us for translations today.

sessions.title: The power of Jewish stories
sessions.desc: In this interactive session, participants will explore the psychology of storytelling: how stories move us, connect us, and help us think more deeply. Together, we will examine how personal and communal Jewish stories can be used as powerful tools for meaningful education.

sessions.title: From grief to political awakening
sessions.desc: ‘Ask me about it’, says Yonatan Zeigen. After losing his mother, peace activist Vivian Silver, he was jolted out of what he calls a political coma. This is a candid conversation about grief, the questions it leaves behind and the moment personal loss becomes a demand to act.

sessions.title: How to be the archivist of your own family story
sessions.desc: In this workshop we’ll explore how curating your family’s stories, recipes, photographs, heirlooms and rituals can make you feel more anchored and connected. This session is suitable for anyone who wants to know more about their family story and preserve it.

sessions.title: The hardest question: organ donation, Jewish law and family choice in the midst of grief
sessions.desc: When my father died, my family faced organ donation in the midst of shock, pain and grief. Three people later received his organs. Today, more than 8,500 people are waiting for a transplant and hundreds die each year without one. Through one family's story, Jewish law and stark realities, we ask: how do we choose when time and life are running out?

sessions.title: Black, Jewish and ‘Not Enough’
sessions.desc: Blackness and Jewishness can each be questioned, policed or misunderstood, and holding both can mean being told you don’t fully belong in either space. Through personal stories and her reporting on race and Jewish life, Nadine examines the everyday encounters that make identity feel conditional, and asks what would make belonging real.

sessions.title: From Torah to action! Be a light!
sessions.desc: Explore 18 key Jewish values from the Torah. Choose a well-known statement of one value, commit to acting on it weekly for six months, and put it into action! The session begins with interactive study of the values. Anyone interested can then make a six-month commitment and talk about what they chose, why, and what they hope to do with it.

sessions.title: Getting jiggy(saw puzzle) with it
sessions.desc: Meet new people and uncover beautiful images. Solo Limmudniks encouraged to attend.

sessions.title: Is joy Jewish? What the rabbis of the Talmud have to teach us about finding joy in uncertain times · The Open Beit Midrash
sessions.desc: Positive psychologist Tal Ben-Shahar calls happiness the ultimate currency by which we measure our lives. But how do we find it? Join us for a journey through three rabbinic stories exploring joy: where it comes from, where we can find it, and whether it holds up in an uncertain world. Session open to all, whatever your experience with Jewish text.

sessions.title: The magic of Hasidic storytelling
sessions.desc: Why tell stories? Following the Hasidic idea that tales should 'awaken' people, I explore storytelling's spiritual role. Using my book 'The Wagon Tale' as a springboard, I examine how Hasidic parables spark personal transformation, bridge tradition and modern growth, and offer timeless wisdom for today. This session is presented in partnership with the Jewish Literary Foundation.

sessions.title: More than walls: the architecture and symbolism of Jewish museums
sessions.desc: How do you build a home for thousands of years of history, celebration, and profound loss? In this session, we explore how the world’s most significant Jewish museums use avant-garde design and deep historical symbolism to turn raw materials into memory. Discover how architecture can be a physical manifestation of memory itself.

sessions.title: Why should Jews care about Jewish prisoners?
sessions.desc: What happens to our responsibility for another Jew when the prison door closes? Drawing on Jewish ideas of community, responsibility and teshuvah alongside criminology and lived experience, we’ll explore Jewish life in prison, punishment, stigma and whether imprisonment changes who we consider part of our community.

sessions.title: Jewish artists need a rest
sessions.desc: It is a tough time to be a Jew in the arts. Personally I want to hide under a rock… This session is a place for creatives to come together and explore how to bring rest and relaxation into our artistic practices.

sessions.title: The sound of belonging: building Jewish community through song
sessions.desc: Music has the power to transform a room of individuals into a community. Through stories, interactive singing, and practical ideas drawn from years of leading congregations and communities, we'll explore how music creates belonging, strengthens relationships, and invites meaningful participation.

sessions.title: How to Jew: the questions your colleagues are afraid to ask
sessions.desc: ‘Another Jewish holiday?’ ‘Why do you leave early on Friday?’ ‘Is it true about the hole in the sheet?’ Yosef wrote 'How to Jew', a plain guide to Judaism for non-Jewish colleagues. A funny talk on the questions people are too embarrassed to ask, the answers that build bridges, and how to be the office Jew without burning out.

sessions.title: Can climate cooperation survive and prevent a war?
sessions.desc: Climate risks cross borders, but cooperation happens amid unequal power and unresolved conflict. Drawing on regional work on water, energy and renewables, Tareq explores whether dialogue and practical climate projects can build trust, who sets priorities and benefits, and where cooperation reaches its limits.

sessions.title: Making space for Jewish life: what we keep, what we let go, and how our homes shape the way we live
sessions.desc: Our homes hold more than stuff: they hold memories, traditions and Jewish life. In this interactive session, we’ll explore what we keep and let go, how to bring meaningful objects into everyday life, and practical ways to organise our homes around the lives we actually live. Come with a challenge; leave with ideas to use at home.

sessions.title: Antisemitism: do we know too much?
sessions.desc: Since 7 October 2023, there has been a massive increase in research on antisemitism. In this session I will draw on unpublished data to show how we know less and less about other Jewish issues as antisemitism has become 'the' issue. Are we in danger of becoming ignorant about anything other than the threats against us?

sessions.title: Antisemitism, Burnham, and conflict in the Middle East – an ABC of Jewish public policy in 2026 and 2027
sessions.desc: President of the Board of Deputies Phil Rosenberg reviews 2026 from the perspective of the Jewish community. He will give an insight into what the Board of Deputies is expecting in 2027. Audience views, perspectives, and questions welcome.

sessions.title: Reading the results: what Israeli and Palestinian voters told us
sessions.desc: Two months after the Israeli and Palestinian parliamentary elections, Dahlia Scheindlin looks at what the results reveal – and what they leave unclear – about public opinion. Drawing on decades of polling and campaign work, she asks what voters were responding to, and what an election can tell us about a society’s deeper divisions and hopes.

sessions.title: An Anglo-Jewish history of broigus
sessions.desc: The history of Jewish communities, it is said, is the same everywhere: fights erupt and splinter congregations form. Discover historic bickering and quarrels across Britain, from brawls in shuls to kosher rivalries. How did British Jews disagree in the past and what can we gain when we embrace it as part of our shared communal history?

sessions.title: Crafts and conversations (1 of 2)
sessions.desc: Everybody's so creative! Bring your latest craft project, and work alongside other crafty people in a low-pressure social environment. Come with friends or make some new ones: everybody's welcome!

sessions.title: Chopping onions on my heart: losing the Iraqi Jewish language
sessions.desc: Judeo-Iraqi Arabic is going extinct. Samantha, a daughter of Jews who left Baghdad in 1951 and 1971, explores the story of one of the biggest and oldest Mizrahi communities, and the efforts to preserve and keep Iraqi Jewish language and culture going.

sessions.title: From Birmingham to Birmingham: an exploration of American social justice texts
sessions.desc: We will compare Dr. Martin Luther King's 'Letter from a Birmingham Jail' and Rabbi Eugene Borowitz's letter from the St. Augustine jail, 'Why We Came'. Together we will explore what these texts from the 1960s civil rights movement urge us to do in response to the urgent justice needs in the world today.

sessions.title: Marching for the living
sessions.desc: Reflecting on the first March of the Living in 1988, a third-generation survivor explores how being physically present at Auschwitz compares with life today, and how hope and community support can build everyday resilience.

sessions.title: Ancient wisdom, modern teaching: exploring pedagogy through Jewish texts
sessions.desc: Discover the pedagogical study group model developed at the Leo Baeck Education Center. This session highlights how collaborative study of Jewish texts in a teachers' beit midrash enriches pedagogical thinking, fosters professional reflection, and offers fresh insights for everyday teaching.

sessions.title: Open mic
sessions.desc: Poets, acrobats, instrumentalists, ventriloquists, yodellers. We want you all! Come and perform your special skill for a room full of other skilled individuals.

sessions.title: Two Jewish women who changed Progressive Judaism – and the world!
sessions.desc: Lily Montagu and Jerusha Jhirad met in London before the First World War. From there to India and beyond, both founded Jewish institutions. But that wasn’t their main job. One was a magistrate, youth and social worker and more; the other a pioneering doctor and campaigner. Come and be inspired by how one person can make a difference.

sessions.title: Fantastical Jewish worlds
sessions.desc: Forget 'Fourth Wing' or 'Game of Thrones': where are the Jewish worlds in modern fantasy stories? In this session, sci-fi and fantasy-obsessed Sam will outline Jewish-inspired stories and worlds in modern western fantasy. Part talk, part 'to be read' list generator, we'll explore how Jewish history, myths, and religion inspire imagined worlds.

sessions.title: Sinai, sacraments or just a trip? Psychedelics and the future of Jewish spirituality
sessions.desc: Could psychedelics help renew Jewish spiritual life, or are they a distraction from the real work? Adriana Kertzer, Jessica Roda, Marc Frank and Micah Gold share what they've seen, where they disagree and what comes next. Bring your curiosity, your scepticism and your questions.

sessions.title: From Beis Yaakov to biophysics
sessions.desc: I will talk about my journey from growing up as a Beis Yaakov (ultra-Orthodox girls' school) girl, and the eldest of seven siblings, in the frum (religiously observant) community of Broughton Park, to becoming a professor of biophysics who investigates the tiny machinery that collaborates to maintain health inside each of our thirty trillion cells.

sessions.title: ‘Oh, I’ll just use AI’ – are chatbots helping or hindering our ability to learn?
sessions.desc: We’re all using AI more and more. Hear seasoned educators discuss the pros and cons of these new tech assistants. While some are excited about the potential and possibilities, others have stark warnings about the very real dangers. Will AI take us one step further on our Jewish journey, or two steps back? Come and find out…

sessions.title: The future of jobs, skills and the Jewish workplace
sessions.desc: AI, automation and demographic change are rewriting the world of work. Drawing on the World Economic Forum’s 'Future of Jobs' research, we’ll explore the skills shaping 2030. Then we turn the lens on years of data from thousands of Jewish nonprofit employees, uncover surprising connections – and ask: are Jewish organisations great places to work?

sessions.title: Israel, UK and Diaspora relations post the 27 October Israeli election
sessions.desc: The Israeli election of 27 October was billed as one of the most consequential in Israel’s history. President of the Board of Deputies Phil Rosenberg discusses the impact of the results and Israeli politics on UK-Israel bilateral relations and on Israel-Diaspora relations. Audience views welcome.

sessions.title: Sephardi vs Ashkenazi: we're more similar than you think
sessions.desc: Cholent or chamin (the Sephardi equivalent)? Sephardi or Ashkenazi? Explore the fascinating similarities and differences between two major Jewish traditions, from prayer and pronunciation to food, customs and halacha. Expect a fun, interactive session, plenty of surprises, and a chance to discover traditions beyond your own. L’ilui nishmat Tuvia Gershon ben Shmuel Chaim / In loving memory of Keith Jeremy Posner z"l.

sessions.title: Lovely lamentable humanity · The Open Beit Midrash
sessions.desc: What does it mean that we are in the image of G-d? Does this apply to those who do awful things and if so, what do such acts do to the divine image? We'll explore some of the most inspiring teachings, biblical and rabbinic, on our potential, and some of the most honest descriptions of our limitations – considering G-d's and our responsibilities.

sessions.title: Eliyahu Goldratt: a life in Goals and Constraints
sessions.desc: How did a religious, Israeli scientist become a globally important, successful and best-selling business guru? How did he not only transform the workings of many manufacturing plants and other companies worldwide, but also create a whole new way of thinking and approaching commercial and other organisational problems?

sessions.title: Welcome to Limmud! (2 of 2)
sessions.desc: From first-timers to long-term Limmudniks, pop by the Wellbeing Hub for a lowdown on this year's festival!

sessions.title: Dead enough? Does Judaism allow organ donation from patients on NRP (artificial circulation)?
sessions.desc: A new transplantation protocol aims to improve the outcomes for recipients by keeping the donor's organs oxygenated. But is the donor truly dead when their vital organs are removed? On what basis? We will consider halachic arguments for and against this controversial procedure.

sessions.title: Impact evaluation 101 for trustees and charity leaders
sessions.desc: For-profit companies measure success through the bottom line, but charities measure it through impact. Measuring and proving this is now expected of all UK charities, but Jewish charities are often behind the curve. By the end of this workshop, you'll have a draft impact model for your organisation. Suitable for trustees and communal professionals.

sessions.title: From Jonah to Yona: immigration, identity and reinvention through art
sessions.desc: This session traces the presenter’s journey from the Netherlands to New York and from one cultural and spiritual identity to another. Through paintings, installations, and personal stories, Verwer explores migration, conversion, belonging, Jewish identity, and ecological displacement, revealing how crossing boundaries has shaped her life and art.

sessions.title: Quilting Jewish London's future
sessions.desc: Share anything from old camp T-shirts to personal rituals: positive reflections of being Jewish that you want to pass on to future generations. We will collage/embroider fabrics, and discuss individual stories while contributing to a collective public art quilt for JW3.

sessions.title: Heartburn: the back story
sessions.desc: We will read together a midrash so outrageous that you have probably never seen it, which offers a way into thinking about human responses to extreme situations. Michael Marmur suggests that the theme of indigestion and heartburn, familiar to many of us, may provide a useful metaphor in thinking about the contemporary crisis of Jewish life.

sessions.title: The space between
sessions.desc: A chance to pause, take a breath and make sense of your Limmud Festival experience. Come to share what’s on your mind, listen to others, or simply sit with whatever you’re feeling. No agenda, no pressure and no need to have the answers – just a welcoming space to reflect, connect and process together.

sessions.title: From crisis to capacity: a leadership lab for community resilience
sessions.desc: What role can you play when your community faces uncertainty, disruption, or crisis? This interactive workshop combines practical emergency preparedness concepts with leadership development. Explore scenarios alongside community members and leadership from across the globe and uncover opportunities for local and international collaboration.

sessions.title: Yeshiva University and the Pride Alliance
sessions.desc: They wanted a club with pizza and movie nights. Instead the Yeshiva University Pride Alliance faces a possible Supreme Court case against its own university. Using court filings, students' writing and scenes from Alliance, the film I'm producing, we explore how a club became a national test of religious freedom against queer inclusion.

sessions.title: Who gets to decide what Jewish words mean?
sessions.desc: Words such as antisemitism, Zionism, memory and solidarity are used, challenged and sometimes weaponised in public debate. Drawing on Jewish texts and ideas, we’ll explore how their meanings have shifted, what Jewish tradition can add to the conversation, and how we can disagree about them without losing one another.

sessions.title: Unity versus uniformity: Rabbi Uziel and Sephardi halacha
sessions.desc: Rabbi Uziel and Rabbi Kook disagreed over prayer rites. Can unity be built without blurring identity, and who paid the price in Israeli society? Through Rabbi Uziel's life and writings, we will explore Sephardi-Ashkenazi relations then and now, and today's revival of Mizrahi traditional identity. In loving memory of Brenda and Russell Smith z"l.

sessions.title: Israel in the headlines: what’s the bigger story?
sessions.desc: A dramatic headline can dominate a day, but what does it reveal about where the Middle East is heading? From Iran’s regional ambitions to Israel’s ties with Arab states and American power, Daniel Schwammenthal looks beyond the daily news at the forces reshaping the region. Which stories deserve more attention, and what are British readers missing?

sessions.title: UK Jewish Film's short film selection
sessions.desc: Four short films showing the range of Jewish life on screen: That’s How You Make a Torah, about the first two women scribes; Butterfly, a stunning, hand-painted animation about Olympic swimmer Alfred Nakache; Parents, a gentle film about grief and family; and Rubinstein's, starring Anton Lesser, Allan Corduner and Rachel Adedeji.

sessions.title: Trans Jewish stories: identity, belonging and joy
sessions.desc: What does it mean to be transgender and Jewish? Hear from trans Jews as they share their own stories of identity, faith, community and belonging. Through personal storytelling and conversation, we’ll explore the diversity of trans Jewish life, from its challenges to its moments of connection, celebration and joy.

sessions.title: Ethics of empathy: beyond us and them · The Open Beit Midrash
sessions.desc: Biblical stories remind us that struggles over belonging are enduring. Through Genesis 16 and 21, we’ll explore the tangled relationships between Sarah, Abraham, Hagar, and G-d – and what they reveal about belonging, empathy, and responsibility, drawing on close reading and feminist biblical scholarship.

sessions.title: Question Time with Young Limmud
sessions.desc: Sarah Sackman, MP for Finchley and Golders Green, and Gershom Sizomu, former Chief Rabbi of Uganda, face questions from Jewish primary school children. No topic is off limits. Only members of Young Limmud will be asking questions, but all are invited to come and watch.

sessions.title: A breath of fresh air
sessions.desc: Grab a hot drink and wrap up warm for some fresh air and an amble around the hotel grounds! The walk will take place along a wheelchair-accessible route.

sessions.title: Noah's ark scavenger hunt
sessions.desc: Feeling intrepid? Love puzzles? Fan of things that come in pairs? Pick up your Hunt Guide from the session location and get going. But you better hurry! We hear there's a high chance of rain...

sessions.title: Piyyut around the world workshop
sessions.desc: Join me on a journey that brings our Jewish story to life, opening our hearts in a vibrant musical 'Ingathering of the Exiles'. We'll explore piyyutim (liturgical poems) from diverse traditions and the stories behind them, learn the tunes and sing them together. Whether you sing in the shower or are a stage professional – come and sing with us!

sessions.title: Deep listening 1: transform your relationships with family, friends and foes (1 of 2)
sessions.desc: How well do we listen, especially to people we disagree with? This double session is a chance to learn from Emily Kasriel, creator of the Deep Listening approach. Explore its eight steps, practise them, and experience how listening deeply can create understanding and connection across difference. Come ready to listen, speak, experiment and learn.

sessions.title: Speed Mishnah: learn Rosh Hashanah! · The Open Beit Midrash (1 of 4)
sessions.desc: Have you ever wanted to learn Mishnah but didn't know where to start? Come along and learn an entire masechet (tractate), and celebrate with a siyum (completion party) on Wednesday morning! A range of presenters will teach every single mishnah in Tractate Rosh Hashanah over four days. No previous knowledge or Hebrew required.

sessions.title: What do I say? Talking to children about the hard stuff
sessions.desc: Where did Grandma go? Why do people hate Jews? Can I have a phone like everyone else? Write down the conversation you're dreading, anonymously if you'd rather. A team of experts will answer your hardest questions, staying out of politics and focusing on the day-to-day challenges of raising children in 2026. Practical, specific and no judgement.

sessions.title: Why I built a Jewish psychedelic retreat company: culturally competent care
sessions.desc: After facing antisemitism and tension after 7 October while working for a psychedelic retreat company in Sweden, psychotherapist Hanna Radomski set out to build something different: Ketter Retreats, offering legal psilocybin retreats inspired by Jewish spirituality. Hear her story of courage, community and healing, then bring your questions.

sessions.title: Bagels and beholders – Jewish roleplaying games and their sources
sessions.desc: Dungeons and Dragons (D&D) is the most popular tabletop roleplaying game, but not the only one. What if you could play an Alkhemister fighting dybbuks (malevolent spirits)? Or a leftist chef with a shady past in a kosher deli? We'll look at some roleplaying games and how they can be used to engage with Jewish learning in an immersive, unique way.

sessions.title: Introducing V'Ahavta: Jews against the far right
sessions.desc: The Torah commands us to love our neighbours as we love ourselves – so why are we seeing a rise in support for the far right? Come and hear more about the collective of UK Jews taking a stand against the far right, racism, antisemitism, and anti-migrant violence. We'll be discussing why this is a deeply Jewish issue, and how you can get involved.

sessions.title: The informal code and key experiences: naming our intuitions
sessions.desc: 'The Informal Code and Key Experiences: Naming Our Intuitions' explores what makes informal education work. Tracing youth movements from the Wandervogel onward, the lecture unpacks Reuven Kahane's eight components of the informal code – voluntarism, moratorium, pragmatic symbolism and more – giving educators language for what they already intuit.

sessions.title: Is protective presence for you? Boots on the ground/praying with your feet
sessions.desc: This will be an unabashed attempt to recruit you to join us protecting endangered Palestinian communities with our bodies, but will also be appropriate if you just want to learn what we do and the Jewish and moral why. Torat Tzedek initiated protective presence in August 2023. Defenders range from their 20s through their 70s. Could it be for you?

sessions.title: Philosophical Talmud: how to keep a negative commandment
sessions.desc: It's a mitzvah (commandment) not to murder. There are about 8 billion people you're not murdering right now. Is that one mitzvah? Or 8 billion mitzvot? We'll ask: how does one keep a negative mitzvah? Come to experience the Talmud as living philosophy. L'ilui nishmat Shaul Ben Yehuda Arieh / In loving memory of Shaul Berkowitz z"l.

sessions.title: When Torah meets the world: a global activist and a rabbi in conversation
sessions.desc: What happens when Torah meets a world in crisis? Can Torah study itself be a form of activism? An activist and a rabbi explore how Jewish texts inform their work – and how their work shapes their understanding of Torah – while wrestling with urgent questions of our responsibility, as Jews, at this moment.

sessions.title: Fighting the forces of division – Sarah Sackman MP in conversation with Zoe Jacobs
sessions.desc: After a challenging year for the Jewish community and other minority groups, keeping communities cohesive is critical. Join Sarah Sackman, member of Parliament for Finchley and Golders Green, and Zoe Jacobs of Finchley Reform Synagogue to reflect on the resilience of north London and how we can stand together against those who would divide us.

sessions.title: Noah Diamondstein in concert
sessions.desc: Come hear the music of accomplished multi-instrumentalist Noah Diamondstein, whose melodies are featured in Jewish communities across the Diaspora. Spanning multiple genres, styles, and topics, Noah's music is sure to connect with you and make you want to sing along!

sessions.title: Family crafternoon: puppet storytelling
sessions.desc: Create weird and wonderful puppets, give them names and bring them to life as you invent stories, characters and adventures together!

sessions.title: Meet Bracha the beaver!
sessions.desc: Meet Bracha the Beaver and hear about her amazing return from extinction in the UK! She and her family are building dams which bring back wildlife, prevent flooding and clean our polluted waters, helping us to look after the world as G-d's creation. Join us for this fun, interactive family session!

sessions.title: Dance is food for the soul!
sessions.desc: Hear testimony from Ukraine and Israel about the impact of war and how dance is providing relief from trauma, as well as stories from other Jewish communities in Europe, Cuba, and South America which provide a template for action in the UK.

sessions.title: Desert Island Discs, live at Limmud: castaway with Delphine Horvilleur
sessions.desc: In the spirit of the BBC classic, Delphine Horvilleur shares the eight pieces of music, the book and the luxury item she'd take to a desert island, and the stories behind them. Woven through are the threads of Jewish life, identity and memory that connect us as a community. Expect warmth, surprise and insight.

sessions.title: Praying for a miracle?
sessions.desc: Mishnah Berachot calls prayer for what is already determined a tefilat shav – a prayer in vain. But when is something truly impossible? Isn’t anything possible for G-d? We’ll explore texts that wrestle with this question, opening up deeper questions about prayer, faith, divine power, and the nature of reality.

sessions.title: Who can learn, who can teach? Deafness and halachic capacity
sessions.desc: Rabbinic texts use cheresh as a legal category, not simply a word for a deaf person. Reading Mishnah Terumot 1:2 and Talmud Chagigah 3a, where two people who could not speak become learned, alongside Pamela Barmash’s 2011 Masorti ruling on sign language, we ask: what changes when communication, not hearing or speech, is what counts?

sessions.title: Mahjong
sessions.desc: Come play mahjong! We'll teach you if you've never played before and (hopefully) have a few different tables with all levels of play.

sessions.title: Artists' lives – Claude Cahun and Marcel Moore: from the Paris avant-garde to the Jersey resistance
sessions.desc: ‘Under this mask, another mask. I will never be finished removing all these faces.’ Lucy Schwob (Cahun) and Suzanne Malherbe (Moore) became friends, lovers, experimental artists and photographers. After settling in Jersey in 1937 they took extreme risks to subvert the German occupiers.

sessions.title: Decisions, decisions: a Jewish introduction to executive functioning skills
sessions.desc: What does it take to plan, prioritise and learn from experience? This workshop explores the role of executive functioning skills, the cognitive toolkit behind focus, memory, and organisation. Discover the Jewish backstory to research in this field and take away top tips drawn from Jewish tradition to help you become (a little bit) more productive.

sessions.title: Everything this frum activist learnt from the Catholic Church
sessions.desc: After years of talking about systemic harms within my own community, I went to a Catholic safeguarding conference. It blew my mind.

sessions.title: Summer camp and the tent: histories of British Jewish youth movements since 1967
sessions.desc: Two years ago I completed the first historical study of 20th-century British Jewish youth movements, using oral history and archival research to try and understand the relationships between Jewish youth, their parental communities in Britain and Israel, and wider socio-political developments. Then I did a year of movement work.

sessions.title: ‘Oylem-Habe’ – ‘The World to Come’: a one-act farce by Sholem Aleichem
sessions.desc: The great Yiddish humourist Sholem Aleichem (creator of Tevye the Dairyman in ‘Fiddler on the Roof’) pokes fun at highly assimilated American ‘allrightniks’ with their Yiddish-English and complete separation from their roots. Except now, they want to buy a place in the World to Come… We will read through this short comedy in English and Yiddish.

sessions.title: So, what kind of Zionist are you?
sessions.desc: Zionism has never had just one face. From competing visions of the Jewish future to the realities of Israel today, we’ll move between texts, ideas and conversations with Israelis from different backgrounds to build a group portrait of Zionism in all its diversity, and ask not only what Zionism was, but what it might mean now.

sessions.title: Israel and America: an alliance under pressure
sessions.desc: What holds the US–Israel partnership together – and what puts it under pressure? Historian Gil Troy, author of 'The Essential Guide to the US–Israel Partnership', explores the alliance’s history, shared values and tensions, and asks how it can adapt to a changing political landscape on both sides of the Atlantic.

sessions.title: Unapologetically Jewish: a spoken word journey – performance + conversation
sessions.desc: Through spoken word and storytelling, Vanessa traces 25+ years as a Jewish voice – from HBO’s Def Poetry to the rupture of 7 October. Through poems and personal stories, she explores what it means to speak publicly as a Jew and Zionist, the cost of doing so, and the courage it takes to remain visible.

sessions.title: Tales and bits of wisdom from a pro bono shadchan
sessions.desc: I have been an amateur shadchan and marriage and love life counsellor for 38 years and I wish to share my personal and original modus operandi, my failures and successes, my practical philosophy and some experience-based advice, in the hope of stimulating the next generation of shadchanim (matchmakers) with a passion for this mitzvah.

sessions.title: An introduction to karate
sessions.desc: Karate helps its practitioners to develop physical fitness, mental resilience, discipline and, of course, self-defence skills. In this session Andrew and Eliana will teach you some of the basic techniques of Shotokan karate. The session is suitable for ages 7+, but anyone under the age of 12 must be accompanied by a parent or guardian.

sessions.title: Can the 'People's Emergency Briefing' help change the world?
sessions.desc: Jews were given the earth to 'tend and protect' (Genesis 2:15). But the climate and nature crisis means we are on a deeply dangerous trajectory. Are we capable of the wiser, more compassionate and far-sighted choices required for us to thrive in the decades and centuries ahead? Watch the film with us and join a supported discussion.

sessions.title: Jewish abortion ethics: neither choice nor life
sessions.desc: What do Jewish texts say about abortion? When does life begin? How is a foetus seen – as an independent entity or part of the mother’s body? Whose rights take precedence – the mother’s or the foetus’s? Until when and in what situations is abortion permitted? We will study sources from the Talmud to modern rabbinic literature.

sessions.title: Therapy that speaks our language: culturally competent psychedelic care for Jews
sessions.desc: What does psychedelic care look like when it truly understands Jewish lives? Two personal stories open a conversation with psychotherapist Hannah Radomski, founder of Ketter's legal psilocybin retreats in Europe, and Adriana Kertzer of the Jewish Healing Society. Fellow panellists will discuss building culturally competent care for our community.

sessions.title: Jews should count: the revealing numbers hidden in plain sight
sessions.desc: Jews are obsessed with, and anxious about, surveys, polls and censuses, yet all too often we fail to count the countable – the telling and revelatory numbers that need no special training to give up their secrets. In this session I will show how my students have counted Jewish things and we will do a fun exercise together.

sessions.title: (Don't) walk like an Egyptian
sessions.desc: Did you know that the ancient Egyptians practised same-sex marriage? It's definitely true, I read it in the midrash to Leviticus 18:3! All this and many more absolutely 100% true facts about life in ancient Egypt and Canaan, in no way influenced by the biases of rabbis 2000 years ago.

sessions.title: A Jew in a museum display case: POLIN Museum in Warsaw
sessions.desc: Almost every major city has its own Jewish museum. And in each one a question emerges: how to present the subject without exoticising it, without turning it into a tourist trap, without reinforcing stereotypes? How can we present the history of a minority without reinforcing a sense of alienation and separation from the history of the majority?

sessions.title: Jewishness, in Arabic: turning up the volume
sessions.desc: What happens when contemporary Jewish artists take the stage in Arabic? Through music and performance, we will explore the history and revival of Jewish repertoires in Arabic and the questions they raise about belonging, memory, and identity. What can singing in Arabic make possible, and what tensions does it bring to the stage?

sessions.title: Love me kosher: gender and sex
sessions.desc: You may have heard from some TikTok or other that there are actually 6 genders in the Talmud. Is this really true? Can the ancient Israelites have known something about the complex realities of gender identity? In this session, we will explore these and similar questions!

sessions.title: Orientalising the self: Else Lasker-Schüler and the politics of belonging
sessions.desc: German-Jewish poet and artist Else Lasker-Schüler (1869–1945) has often been perceived as an eccentric bohemian who escaped into an Orientalist fantasy world.
