Focusing on her drawings, this presentation argues that her work was instead deeply intertwined with contemporary debates about Jewish identity – debates that continue to resonate today.

sessions.title: ‘Anything new is prohibited’ – was Rabbi Moses Sofer the first Charedi Jew?
sessions.desc: This brilliant early-19th-century rabbinic scholar kept strict Orthodox standards and was known for opposing new practices, secular studies, and the Haskalah (Jewish Enlightenment) and Reform movements. But it’s not that simple. Learn what his motto 'Chadash assur min haTorah' (the new is forbidden by the Torah) really means...

sessions.title: After the votes: Trump, the Middle East, Israel and the road ahead
sessions.desc: The votes are in – but what do they mean for Trump, the Middle East, Israel and the wider Jewish world? Dahlia Scheindlin, Benny Morris and Gil Troy unpack the Israeli election, Middle East dynamics, and US midterms, explore their implications for geopolitical relations, and ask what comes next.

sessions.title: LGBT+ social
sessions.desc: Join us for a relaxed LGBT+ social, a chance to meet other LGBT+ Limmudniks, catch up with friends and connect with community. Whether you’re coming on your own or with others, drop in, say hello and spend some time together in a welcoming LGBT+ space.

sessions.title: Finding your community: a listening space for Jews in the non-Jewish charity sector
sessions.desc: Are you Jewish and working for a non-Jewish charity, NGO or non-profit? Join a facilitated listening space to connect with peers, share experiences, explore challenges and successes, and help shape a new network for Jewish professionals and trustees in the third sector.

sessions.title: Advocacy
sessions.desc: I want to introduce people to the basic principles of advocacy, including how to analyse the argument you are advancing, and anticipate its likely reception by the audience, and anyone opposing your views. I want to consider how different styles of advocacy suit different audiences, and think about strategies for staying disciplined.

sessions.title: Sacrae: singing 'a cappella' Christian settings of Jewish texts (1 of 2)
sessions.desc: A chamber choir for Limmud! If you love singing a cappella settings by the likes of Tallis, Brahms and Howells, and if you've got good sight-singing skills, then Sacrae is for you. We'll sing Jewish-texts-only sacred choral works. Note: you’ll find music links below this info on the website (not on the app).

sessions.title: Quilting Jewish London's Future (2 of 2)
sessions.desc: Share old camp t-shirts to personal rituals that are your positive reflections of being Jewish; that you want to pass on to future generations. We will collage/embroider fabrics, discuss individual stories while contributing to a collective public art quilt for JW3 in London. No quilting or art experience required.

sessions.title: Behind the headlines in Israeli news
sessions.desc: Israel is a country that is as diverse as it is complicated. Together we will explore the hottest topics in Israeli public discourse today (subject to change at any given minute). We will try and understand the different sides of the issues, and what diverse opinions Israelis hold on the matter.

sessions.title: Justice and mercy – Hindu and Jewish parallels
sessions.desc: The Jewish and Hindu traditions struggle in remarkably similar ways with the question of how justice and mercy can be reconciled. In this session we will explore this multi-faceted seam of wisdom, drawing on the Hindu Bhagavad Gita, the Zohar, the Nobel Prize-winning philosopher and economist Amartya Sen and even the poetry of T.S. Eliot.

sessions.title: Echoes of anxiety: how different people faced the same historic crises
sessions.desc: Human worries, from political turmoil to family life, transcend time, yet personal circumstances shape how we confront them. Using the National Library of Israel’s rich letter collections, this session compares how different people responded to the same crises, offering a deeply personal lens on resilience throughout modern Jewish history.

sessions.title: AI and creation
sessions.desc: While Clive does not pretend to know anything much about AI, he is intrigued by parallels that can be learnt by looking carefully at the Torah's account of creation in Bereshit (Genesis). What are the dangers, what are the possibilities and what is the problem? Have we ever seen anything like it before? Come and argue with Clive's take on it all.

sessions.title: The Elias Show
sessions.desc: The Elias Show is the latest musical solo creation of virtuoso trombonist and internationally acclaimed performer Elias Faingersh – a man who makes the impossible sound effortless. This is a musical journey weaving together lyricism, humour, tenderness, and parody in a show that feels both deeply human and delightfully unpredictable.

sessions.title: Is there such a thing as a bashert (soulmate)? And if so, should you be looking for yours?
sessions.desc: 40 days before birth, a heavenly voice announces your destined partner. Or does it? We’ll explore the concept of bashert through midrashim, rabbinic stories, and a fascinating 20th-century responsum about the wedding ceremony. Along the way, we’ll ask: Is there really one right person? What do these sources say about love, choice, and commitment?

sessions.title: Antisemitism has no borders. Can the response keep up?
sessions.desc: Antisemitism travels fast, mutates and finds new audiences. The response has to cross borders too. Leon Saltiel goes inside the global push to confront it: the alliances, political battles and tools involved, including the International Holocaust Remembrance Alliance definition. What can global cooperation change, and where does it fall short?

sessions.title: Through her eyes: life as a young Palestinian woman in the West Bank
sessions.desc: What does everyday life look like for a young Palestinian woman living in the West Bank? In conversation with Dalia Blass from Yachad, Yara shares her personal experiences of growing up and living under occupation.

sessions.title: ‘What about…?’: a fair challenge or a way to change the subject?
sessions.desc: Someone names an injustice; someone else points to another injustice elsewhere in the world. Is that a distraction, a necessary wider lens, or both? This session asks when whataboutery exposes selective attention, when it shuts discussion down, and how to make room for more than one community’s suffering without using one to dismiss another.

sessions.title: When Herbie Hancock led the Friday night service
sessions.desc: In 1968 some of the biggest names in jazz came together in New York to record a Friday night service. Our familiar prayers had been set to jazz music and had been received so enthusiastically in synagogues where the concerts had been performed that a decision was made to record it. Come and hear it, and the story of how it all happened.

sessions.title: Feed the birds? Exploring an unusual Ashkenazi tradition
sessions.desc: This session analyses the tradition of feeding birds during the Shabbat in which we read about the Israelites crossing the Red Sea. In particular, we will explore how this tradition is actually in contradiction with certain laws of Shabbat, thereby being a microcosm of what happens when Jewish law contradicts human experience.

sessions.title: The most important woman in the world!
sessions.desc: Well... maybe not in the entire world, but certainly in the Jewish world. Dona Gracia Mendes Nasi was so rich and so generous that she was known to Jews everywhere simply as ‘La Signora’. Her wealth gave her access to the courts of Renaissance Europe but the Spanish Inquisition was never far behind…

sessions.title: UK Jewish Film presents: A Serious Man (2009)
sessions.desc: Minnesota, 1967. Physics lecturer Larry Gopnik (Michael Stuhlbarg) is under pressure. His daughter steals from him to save up for a nose job; his pot-head son gets stoned at his own bar mitzvah; his brother Arthur is an unwelcome house-guest. Larry's wife Judith wants a divorce and the lawyers' bills are mounting. What else could possibly go wrong?

sessions.title: A Jew on the run
sessions.desc: Yossi Zabari is an Arab-Jewish, queer comedian from Israel/Palestine, now based in Europe and raising two suspiciously white kids. In ‘A Jew on the Run’, he blends stand-up, storytelling and personal chaos to explore identity, guilt and survival and how to escape a mess you never signed up for.

sessions.title: Tikkun olam, antibiotic resistance and factory farming: practical steps to help the first and reduce the others
sessions.desc: Do tikkun olam, the danger of increased antibiotic resistance and the morals of factory farming concern you? Come and discuss practical steps to take part in the first and to reduce and avoid the others.

sessions.title: AI or A-Oy: building a synthetic Jew
sessions.desc: Are AIs born Jewish, or do they have Jewishness thrust upon them? What even is a so-called 'artificial intelligence'? In a world where AI has become nothing more than meaningless jargon, could one feasibly build a synthetic consciousness, and would such a being without a physical form be able to become a member of the tribe?

sessions.title: Forgotten rebellion: a history of the 613 CE Jewish revolt
sessions.desc: An overview of the final Jewish revolt against the Romans and the ruling Emperor Heraclius. Discussing both the revolt itself and the wider geopolitical situation in the early-7th-century Middle East.

sessions.title: Who's afraid of Bruriah in 2026?
sessions.desc: An artist and a rabbi, both Orthodox feminists who love Talmud and the Jewish people, talk about a woman's place in the beit midrash, the art studio, and everywhere in between. Together we'll attempt the impossible: to take a serious look at women and Judaism, without getting (too) bitter.

sessions.title: Reimagining Israel education
sessions.desc: Israel and Jewish life in the Diaspora have changed. Has Israel education kept pace? We’ll look at the realities that shaped it, how our relationship with Israel has evolved, and what an honest, relevant and nuanced approach could look like today. Together, we’ll reimagine how to teach Israel in a way that speaks to the world we now live in.

sessions.title: Kumi Ori: the concert
sessions.desc: Ariella Zeitlin's signature show. A concert built around rising and reclaiming voice: original music, live violin, and the story underneath it.

sessions.title: Speed dating for all (age 20–34)
sessions.desc: Countless couples met at Limmud. Maybe you’re half of one of them. Bring yourself and only yourself to this relaxed session. We will be separating by age demographic in the room. Daters will choose a coloured sticker (or multiple) based on their preferences and pronouns.

sessions.title: A new method for managing polarising conversations: come try it out!
sessions.desc: Learn a new way to have hard conversations with respect. The ancient Jewish spiritual genre of Mussar helps us manage polarising talks with calm, humanity and integrity. We will learn Mussar guidelines, then discuss our different views on Israel – a hot topic! Come prepared to disagree with patience, an open mind and willingness to learn.

sessions.title: From line to form: essentials of drawing
sessions.desc: Learning to draw is learning to see. Join Matan Sacofsky for a session exploring the foundations of drawing, from observational habits and mark-making to capturing form and light. Whether you are picking up a pencil for the first time or looking to refine your gaze, discover practical tools to translate sight to paper.

sessions.title: Tayelet
sessions.desc: Bou lirkod! (Come and dance!) Enjoy all the atmosphere of Tel Aviv’s Tayelet (seafront promenade), learning dances regularly danced in Israel, suitable for newcomers and returnees with a relaxed and fun atmosphere. This is an introduction to Israeli dance for the young and young at heart. Have fun! Learn all the basic moves but with some new music.

sessions.title: Speakeasy
sessions.room: I hear there's a whisper going round...
sessions.desc: Ssssssssssssssssssssssssssh. Nothing to see here.

sessions.title: Vayarutz vayomer: he ran and he talked – or run and chat (2 of 4)
sessions.desc: If you fancy a chance to stretch your legs as well as your minds then do join us for this outdoor run. We can meet new people and discuss Jewish topics, Limmud sessions, running schedules or just enjoy being outside. Be prepared to run for an hour and maybe get muddy.

sessions.title: Good morning, Limmud!
sessions.desc: Limmud Festival meets breakfast TV! Join our studio audience every morning for an insider's scoop on the events of the previous day, hot takes from some of your favourite Limmud presenters, a forecast of the day’s highlights and lots of silliness and shtick.

sessions.title: A Bevis Marks Heritage Centre taster
sessions.desc: Bevis Marks opened its new Dangoor Heritage Centre last month, showcasing the complete restoration of the UK's oldest synagogue and the history and treasures of the Spanish and Portuguese Jewish community. Join the Centre's first artist-in-residence and one of the Bevis Marks Foundation's trustees for some highlights of the new exhibitions.

sessions.title: Building a healing service
sessions.desc: As worsening mental health crises worldwide compound the herculean task of living a human life, our shuls and Jewish spaces have the immense potential to be loci of healing for our people. Come and learn some best practices, musical/poetic/scriptural repertoire, and 'matbeia tefillah' (the fixed structure of prayer) for effective healing services.

sessions.title: What did the snail think? The prostitute and the penitent from a snail's-eye view
sessions.desc: A famous story in the Talmud tells of a young scholar who travels to visit a famous sex worker, gets struck in the face by his tzitzit, and deflates. By looking at famous nineteenth-century art, we ask about comparable characters in the story, and like the cat in Manet's Olympia, wonder if the snail which dyes the tzitzit also has a story to tell.

sessions.title: The grandparents' guide to autism and ADHD (all are welcome)
sessions.desc: This practical session explains autism and ADHD and explores challenges that can arise in everyday family life. We’ll discuss how grandparents can better understand children’s needs, respond with confidence and build stronger relationships. We’ll also consider what we can learn from Judaism to support the whole family.

sessions.title: Cut, paste, tell: what does your connection to Israel look like?
sessions.desc: In this hands-on collage workshop, we'll write, cut, arrange, examine, rearrange and share our stories with Israel, however near, far, or complicated. No art skills or knowledge needed, just an open heart and curiosity.

sessions.title: Whose hand is it anyway?
sessions.desc: The rabbis used the human hand to measure everything from space and distance to dimensions. But when hands come in different sizes, how do we arrive at one halachic standard? This session will explore the sources, the debates and some surprising practical consequences of a few centimetres.

sessions.title: Gett out: Bertha Pappenheim and the fight for equity in Jewish divorce
sessions.desc: Join Rebecca Rogowski to learn more about one of her she-roes: Bertha Pappenheim, a German-Austrian Jewish women’s rights activist and the founder of the Jüdischer Frauenbund (Jewish Women’s Association). In this shiur (study session), we will focus on Pappenheim’s efforts to reform Jewish divorce laws.

sessions.title: The money game
sessions.desc: Talking about money is still one of the hardest things to do, whether it be family money from inheritance or disposable income for young professionals. Judaism offers us insights into how money can be a source of ethical values. Join us, an accountant and a rabbi, as we explore Jewish values related to money and play the money game together!

sessions.title: Ask a Palestinian
sessions.desc: What does it mean to live as a Palestinian in Israel in 2026? Join Khalid and Lilach for an open Q&A and frank, personal conversation about identity, belonging and everyday life. Bring your questions, your curiosity and an open mind.

sessions.title: The Valkyries don't ride to Tel Aviv – why Israel 'cancelled' Wagner (2 of 2)
sessions.desc: 25 years ago, Daniel Barenboim conducted Wagner in Israel, challenging a decades-old taboo and sparking a firestorm of controversy. Why was (and is) Wagner effectively ‘cancelled’ in the Jewish state? Is refusing to play an antisemitic composer an act of Holocaust memory, sensitivity to survivors or an anachronistic denial of cultural freedom?

sessions.title: Mindfulness for Jews | part 2: how to not beat yourself up for not meditating (2 of 3)
sessions.desc: Take a deep breath. Meditate. Go for a walk. Most of us could write a book of healthy advice, but the challenge is in the doing. Then the inner critic arrives, scolding us for falling short. Drawing on neuroscience, mindfulness and ancient wisdom, we'll explore how to grow with something much stronger than willpower. All are welcome.

sessions.title: Almost normal: navigating the world as an undiagnosed autistic adult
sessions.desc: Life is exhausting when trying to look 'normal'. Join Belinda to explore the reality of being neurodivergent in a neurotypical world. The session examines masking, sensory overload, and late diagnosis among others. It also touches on some recent scientific developments. Discover why autism is a strength to be embraced, not a disorder to be fixed.

sessions.title: Morning dance party
sessions.desc: Start your day right with Limmud Festival's sober morning rave. Dance like your rabbi isn't watching. Move your body like only you know how. Come in your finest sequins, activewear, tefillin, flower crowns or pyjamas – whatever feels good. All ages welcome. Expect uplifting tunes from global beats and dance anthems to funk and hip hop.

sessions.title: What can a challah tell us about Jewish life across different countries and communities?
sessions.desc: As we bake rainbow challot together, we’ll explore the realities of intersectionality and Jewish diversity across Europe and beyond: what connects us, what changes, and how identity, belonging and tradition shift across different spaces – from Pride to events like Limmud.

sessions.title: Darchei shalom: balancing personal religious observance and relationship with others · Limmud's Beit Midrash (2 of 4)
sessions.desc: Talmud in the original in three groups (beginners, intermediate and advanced), each with a skilled teacher. We will discuss questions such as: ‘Can I trust other Jews whose religious practice is different from my own?’ New faces welcome! More information on the Beit Midrash in the handbook and app – or just come for one day or stay all week.

sessions.title: Egalitarian prayer: a halachic exploration
sessions.desc: One of the major dividing lines in Jewish life is whether prayer is gender-egalitarian, with people of all genders leading and counting towards a minyan, or if those roles are reserved for men. We’ll take a whirlwind tour of the sources behind both approaches while learning about prayer, leadership, and why a minyan matters.

sessions.title: Vengeance is not a strategy
sessions.desc: After 7 October, Israel turned to righteous fury: strike harder, trust force, call it security. Yonatan Zeigen asks whether vengeance has made anyone safer. Drawing on peacebuilding, politics and the legacy of Vivian Silver, he asks and answers: what strategy could actually lead Israelis and Palestinians out of endless war?

sessions.title: Recycling history: saving the unknown gems in the cupboard
sessions.desc: Every household holds quiet witnesses to history – letters, journals, and photos tucked in lofts and drawers. Using National Library of Israel collections, we’ll discover how ordinary keepsakes become historical gems; how these personal items fit into global Jewish memory; and even learn practical tips for sorting the treasures in your own home.

sessions.title: Why do we need neuroscience for mental health?
sessions.desc: Mental ill-health is on the rise and our treatments have changed little in decades – but what’s the brain got to do with it? Taking the case of depression, we will explore how research linking mind and brain can provide deep insights into mental health and develop better treatments. Plenty of Q&A time provided and no scientific background required!

sessions.title: Breathwork with live music
sessions.desc: Come for a guided breathwork meditation held inside live music, with the violin moving with the room in real time. The session closes with guided journaling, to help you land and hold on to what came up. An intimate, embodied counterpart to the concert: a chance to go inward rather than watch a stage.

sessions.title: Great is human dignity: Gadol Kvod Ha-Briot!
sessions.desc: Jewish law can be viewed as a compendium of discrete rules, but there are also values such as human dignity which function as a meta-halacha. What is the basis of this concept, how has it been applied through the centuries, and what is its role today in discourses surrounding gender, sexuality, disability, and ageing?

sessions.title: Dangoor UK Jewish Film Short Doc Fund 2026 winners
sessions.desc: Five short documentary winners: Oslo Court, a beloved Jewish restaurant; Rambling, friendships formed on countryside walks around Manchester; Fish, Chips and Faith, a rabbi in a halal fish and chip shop; The Last Jewel of Hatton Garden, inside a Jewish-run business; Mizrahi Mismatch, a couple married for 67 years. Films followed by a discussion.

sessions.title: How the kol isha industry came to life
sessions.desc: How can you be a celebrity while observing tzniut (modesty) and embracing kol isha? Explore how ultra-Orthodox women embrace kol isha, the restriction on women singing before men, to create a world of music, film and social media for women and girls only, giving rise to frum (Orthodox) celebrities, new markets and an industry built on this paradox.

sessions.title: Jewish mindfulness meditation: in the sanctuary of silence...
sessions.desc: How often do we honour our weary, weather-beaten nervous systems with the gift of settling, softening, and deep rest in the sanctuary of silent space? Jewish mindfulness meditation offers just this opportunity. After a short Jewish wisdom teaching, we will enter into guided sitting, suitable for absolute beginners and experienced meditators alike.

sessions.title: The antisemitism definition experiment
sessions.desc: The definition of antisemitism is a bitterly contested issue today. Much less attention is paid to how definitions of antisemitism are interpreted in real-world situations. In this session we will conduct an experiment in seeing how far existing definitions may 'stretch' to indict or absolve those accused of antisemitism.

sessions.title: Who gets a seat at the table?
sessions.desc: What can a Jewish table tell us about who we are – and who belongs? Bringing Jewish sources into conversation with food writing and anthropology, we’ll explore how food transmits memory, shapes identity and draws boundaries. Can the food we share tell us where the boundaries of Jewish belonging lie – and who gets a seat at the table?

sessions.title: A breath of fresh air
sessions.desc: Grab a hot drink and wrap up warm for some fresh air and an amble around the hotel grounds! The walk will take place along a wheelchair-accessible route.

sessions.title: When Israel enters every room
sessions.desc: Vanessa grew up in a golden age of New York Jewish life. Today, anti-Zionism shows up everywhere – from pop culture and the arts to schools, social media and friendships. Through storytelling, spoken word and conversation, she explores what has changed and what she worries about for the next generation.

sessions.title: When we deeply disagree: navigating difficult conversations when the stakes are high
sessions.desc: Marshall Rosenberg’s Nonviolent Communication offers practical tools for navigating the conversations we find the hardest – when we feel hurt, angry, judged and longing to be heard and understood. Come and learn a different way of approaching conflict: one that looks beneath the words and actions and helps us stay connected across difference.

sessions.title: In the studio with Matan Sacofsky: painting, place, and identity
sessions.desc: Join artist Matan Sacofsky for an exploration of figurative oil painting, plein air landscapes, and his recent 'Self Portrait' series. Matan shares insights into his studio process and visual storytelling, examining how themes of identity, observation, and place intersect to offer an intimate look at contemporary Israeli art.

sessions.title: Oy vey, I’ve become my Jewish mother
sessions.desc: You swore you’d be different. Then you caught yourself worrying about every tiny hiccup, missed nap and undrunk milk. A relaxed sharing circle for new mums to talk about the funny, messy and unexpected business of becoming a Jewish mother. Babies welcome; having it all figured out definitely optional.

sessions.title: The Bell Review: from recommendations to reality
sessions.desc: Jonathan Frisher joins a special guest to explore the Bell Review: how it came about, what its recommendations mean, and what government can do to tackle antisemitism in schools. They’ll also consider what we, as Jews, can do to help turn those recommendations into lasting change.

sessions.title: Megillat Antiochus: the biblical book you've never heard of
sessions.desc: We were all taught that Tanach has 24 books. But no one told you that many medieval Bibles have one more. Come and see the magnificent manuscripts of Megillat Antiochus, fully clad with vowels and trope, ready to be read in synagogue on Shabbat Chanukah. Together we'll find out what it takes to make it into the Bible, and what it takes to drop out.

sessions.title: How to have the most [insert here] Passover seder
sessions.desc: Insert as appropriate: lively, creative, fun, thought-provoking, argumentative, nostalgic, dramatic, introspective, unexpected, amorous, thrilling, inclusive, illuminating, child-focused, adult-focused, engaging, meaningful. A panel to coincide with the formal launch of Leon Fenster's new 'Living Tapestry' Haggadah.

sessions.title: From testimony to memory: retracing my grandfather’s journey
sessions.desc: Through my grandfather Max Stempel’s recorded testimony, I’ll retrace his extraordinary wartime journey across Europe, from persecution and hiding to separation and survival. I’ll also share my return to France, where meeting descendants of other survivors brought his story, our shared history and the legacy we carry vividly to life.

sessions.title: Uprooting the family tree: Yiddish anarchism and the politics of nostalgia
sessions.desc: This is a presentation and discussion exploring my own research into the life of my great-great-grandfather, Morris Myer, a Romanian-born Yiddish anarchist, journalist and, by the end of his life, an ardent Zionist. The session will open into a broader discussion on the politics of memory, the revival of Yiddish, and the history of Zionism.

sessions.title: Palestinians on two sides of the Green Line
sessions.desc: Yara lives in the West Bank; Khalid is a Palestinian citizen of Israel. In this session, they explore the different realities of Palestinian life on either side of the Green Line, as well as where their experiences intersect.

sessions.title: After the elections: imagining Israel and Palestine’s political future
sessions.desc: Dahlia Scheindlin analyses the post-election landscape in Israel and the Palestinian territories. What does the current leadership mean for occupation, annexation, negotiation, or regional approaches to peace? Could Israeli policy change relative to the last four years, or before 7th October? Are there new ideas for ending the conflict?

sessions.title: Deep listening 2: transform your relationships with family, friends and foes (2 of 2)
sessions.desc: You’ve explored the eight steps of Deep Listening. Now put them to work in more depth. In this hands-on session with Emily Kasriel, you’ll look at the traps that stop you listening when you disagree, and have more practice to deeply listen in challenging conversations. Attendance at session 1 is required.

sessions.title: Volunteering is not just for festival – but come along and microvolunteer today!
sessions.desc: Join the Jewish Volunteering Network to craft items for social impact organisations. Make items like twiddle toys for people with dementia, upcycle old T-shirts (bring your own) or make cards for refugees, people in care homes and children in hospital. Craft, chat, have fun while microvolunteering, and learn how to continue all year.

sessions.title: L’cha Dodi: is there a perfect melody?
sessions.desc: How do we welcome Shabbat and what is it about L’cha Dodi that moves us so? Come sing and learn with Ayala, and some special musical guests... We’ll explore a few settings of L’cha Dodi and try to answer: why are there so many? And can the perfect tune exist? Ask Ayala about the Jewish Theological Seminary's cantorial and rabbinical schools!

sessions.title: When you know the system – and it still feels impossible
sessions.desc: Professionally, we work as a clinical psychologist and an academic researching health and social care. Personally, we are also caring for our daughter with complex disabilities. Chaired by a systemic therapist, we talk about what we have learnt from the uphill struggle families face to get help and support from health and social care services.

sessions.title: Laminate yourself!
sessions.desc: Time to get two-dimensional! Come by the social programming kiosk to make some lanyard decorations to feel more like yourself this Limmud.

sessions.title: Real tikkun olam (repairing the world), too often missed in a blazing, beautiful Talmudic story · The Open Beit Midrash
sessions.desc: Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai retreats in a cave for years, destroys with the intensity of his gaze, and then learns... We'll find that Gila Fine's rules of reading such a story yield brilliant results for seeing the lesson. We'll consider the dangers and necessity of retreat and repair – or how to make sure this Limmud is not entirely an indulgence.

sessions.title: Behind the doors of rabbinical schools
sessions.desc: What is the life of a student rabbi? What's good/bad about the training system? This panel reveals the experiences of students in rabbinical schools worldwide including a low-residency programme and a fully online programme. If you want to know how your leaders are trained or are considering the rabbinate yourself, come and ask your questions.

sessions.title: Birthright Israel drop-in session
sessions.desc: Thinking about going on Birthright Israel? Drop in to find out more, ask questions, explore opportunities and get help with your application. You can also complete your eligibility interview and find out what to expect. Whether you’re ready to apply or just curious, come and have a chat!

sessions.title: TikTok Judaism: how social media is reshaping Jewish life and tradition
sessions.desc: TikTok, Instagram, and YouTube have revolutionised global culture – and Jewish life is no exception. Social media has given rise to new expressions of Jewish identity, customs and tradition. In this session, our students will explore the intersection of digital media and Jewish life, and discuss how screen culture is reshaping ancient traditions.

sessions.title: Israel and Europe: it’s complicated
sessions.desc: A lively conversation about European Union (EU)–Israel relations, what Jewish organisations can influence, and where their influence has limits. Using concrete examples, we will explore who makes decisions in the EU, what powers they have, and how European policy towards Israel is formulated and implemented. No prior EU knowledge required.

sessions.title: The Jews of India
sessions.desc: In the Jews of India session I will outline the different groups of Jews who found their separate ways, many years ago, to various areas of India. We will learn about their history, culture, and ancestry.

sessions.title: Sharing books of Jewish interest
sessions.desc: Whilst rummaging in Tills Bookshop, Edinburgh, this summer, I came across 'Dora Bruder' by Patrick Modiano, a fascinating read about a fifteen-year-old Jewish girl who goes missing in Paris in 1941. How many books of Jewish interest are there, that we have yet to read? So, bring along that less well-known volume and be prepared to enthuse about it!

sessions.title: Reframing Esther in the history of institutional abuse
sessions.desc: To what degree do women in the Book of Esther have agency over their lives, their bodies, and their choices? By understanding their experiences as an example of institutional abuse, we will consider how Esther’s story can help us to understand and oppose institutional abuse as it existed throughout history and as it still exists in today’s world.

sessions.title: So how do I bless my dog on Shabbat, and what’s the Mi Sheberach if my cat falls ill?
sessions.desc: Three rabbis, David Mitchell, Charles Middleburgh and Jonathan Wittenberg, share a love of animals. After nine years of barks and miaows, their pet siddur, 'Siddur Ahavat Kol Chai – for People and Their Beloved Pets', is out. Get a whiff of its canine, feline and all-too-human prayers for pets, from arrival in your home to their eternal rest.

sessions.title: What does it mean to show up for community?
sessions.desc: What does it mean to care for a community you’re not physically part of? We’ll explore Jewish ideas of community, responsibility and chesed, and ask what makes an act of service meaningful. Then we’ll put it into practice by writing and decorating cards for residents of an Israeli senior centre, turning conversation into connection.

sessions.title: Fascinating cases involving religion and law
sessions.desc: Three barristers discuss this year's cases involving religion and law. Wigs optional.

sessions.title: Listening to each other across the Israel divide
sessions.desc: Israel once united us; today I hear story after story about how it rips apart communities and families. Facilitating a listening/discussion session was moving at my last Limmud, and I want to do it again. As someone who has defended Israel and endangered myself fighting Israeli injustice, I hope to create a safe space to speak with each other.

sessions.title: From movement to motivation: how physical activity boosts mental health
sessions.desc: Ever wondered why going for a jog gives you a mental boost? Physical activity can be a powerful treatment for depression, but we are only just beginning to understand how it works. This session will explore the surprising connections between movement, the brain and motivation, and how they may point to new ways of tackling depression.

sessions.title: What is G-d? How do we connect to G-d? What if we don’t have G-d?
sessions.desc: This panel will explore the diversity of approaches to G-d in the Jewish community, and look at how this diversity manifests in communities. We will consider how useful it is to talk about G-d across a Jewish community with such a divergent relationship to G-d. L'ilui nishmat Shaul Ben Yehuda Arieh / In loving memory of Shaul Berkowitz z"l.

sessions.title: Getting crafty
sessions.desc: Join us for a relaxed session of arts and crafts at the Wellbeing Hub. Supplies are provided but anyone is welcome to bring their own crafts for some creative collaboration!

sessions.title: Screening and discussion: The Darkest Light: We Need to Talk About Carlebach
sessions.desc: His melodies are sung in almost every synagogue. He was also a serial abuser of girls and women. The Darkest Light, Best First Feature at the San Francisco Jewish Film Festival, asks us to hold both. Join Simon Mendes and a panel of survivor advocates and leaders: what do we do with a beloved figure who brought so many in and left so many reeling?

sessions.title: The story of Abayudaya Jews, Uganda
sessions.desc: Exploring the history and development of the Abayudaya Jewish community of Uganda, from its origins in the early 20th century to the present day. The presentation will highlight the community’s traditions, Jewish identity, challenges, achievements, and contributions, while also examining its current needs, opportunities, and vision for the future.

sessions.title: Now that's what I call bad Jewish music!
sessions.desc: In a session that actually makes a more serious point than it appears at first sight, I will show how I came to love the Jewish music that I always hated. I will play examples of awful Jewish music to show how they capture what it is to be Jewish more effectively than the work of artists like Leonard Cohen.

sessions.title: Dear diary
sessions.desc: We are all moved by 'The Diary of Anne Frank'. But did you know that many other Jewish men and women wrote diaries documenting their experiences during the Shoah? David will introduce some of these remarkable testimonies so that we can allow their voices to be heard once more.

sessions.title: Revising the coalition: how new right populism reshaped the Heritage Foundation's approach to 'Judeo-Christian' consensus
sessions.desc: I’ll examine the tension between the Heritage Foundation's use of 'Judeo-Christian' rhetoric, often co-opting Jewish support and theology, and the recent influx of staff influenced by figures like Nick Fuentes. I’ll explore how these opposing forces coexist in one think tank and why neither serves the long-term interest of Israeli or Diaspora Jews.

sessions.title: What am I, Chopped Liver?
sessions.desc: For nearly two decades, Daniel has been a Limmud fixture, documenting Jewish life in unique storytelling songs. The award-winning songwriter returns with more smart, funny, moving, topical yet timeless tales of family, faith, identity and the business of being Jewish. May or may not include his 'hits' This Jewish Christmas and Bad Rabbi.

sessions.title: How to build an oasis in the desert: the story of Israel’s innovation economy
sessions.desc: This session explores how Israel became a modern innovation powerhouse in just a century. Based on the speaker’s original periodisation of Israel’s innovation history, it examines the key forces behind this remarkable transformation.

sessions.title: On presence – examining the influence of Martin Buber on three artists: Cecile Elstein, Maureen Kendal and Alana Lake
sessions.desc: Recent research published in the International Journal on Media and Presence will be presented, followed by a facilitated discussion.

sessions.title: Who wants to be Jewish now? Artists, identity, and the new Jewish art world after 7 October
sessions.desc: How the aftermath of 7 October has forced Jewish artists to confront identity, visibility, and belonging, and how those choices are reshaping the contemporary Jewish art world.

sessions.title: Rosalind Franklin and DNA: was she robbed of recognition?
sessions.desc: Rosalind Franklin’s work produced Photo 51, which helped reveal DNA’s double helix. After her death, three men won the Nobel Prize. Was she denied recognition through sexism and scientific rivalry, or has a more complicated story become a feminist legend? And how far did her Anglo-Jewish upbringing shape the scientist she became?

sessions.title: Can breathwork be frum? Inside the Orthodox healing turn
sessions.desc: This lecture and experiential workshop combines an introduction to the Orthodox healing turn with a guided meditation experience. Through the case of Fally Klein, we will explore how breathwork, embodied spirituality, and new forms of healing are reshaping religious knowledge and authority in Orthodox Jewish life.

sessions.title: Outspoken Miriam · The Open Beit Midrash
sessions.desc: Who was this biblical leader? By studying her appearances in Torah and midrash, we will piece together a coherent personality. The work of Ilana Pardes, a Hebrew University professor, helps us understand this complex, sometimes unpalatable, female saviour, prophet and protestor. We learn in memory of the irrepressible Nina Epstein-Mirelman.

sessions.title: The Gaza genocide allegation and how to counter it
sessions.desc: The allegation that Israel committed genocide in Gaza has gained widespread acceptance. However, the evidence and legal basis are scant. It needs to be resisted on its merits, both because it creates support for anti-Jewish and anti-Israel violence, and because it deforms the very concept of genocide, hindering prevention and resistance.

sessions.title: Zine-making drop-in
sessions.desc: Sit for a moment and contribute to the Limmud zine! Think advice for first-time Limmudniks, images of Jewish joy, and reflections from your experience.

sessions.title: Wellbeing coffee and chat
sessions.desc: Join our lovely wellbeing Yads (Limmud volunteers) for a coffee or tea and chat!

sessions.title: When we don't like G-d's answers: a journey through the book of Habakkuk
sessions.desc: In this session we will explore the back and forth between G-d and the prophet Habakkuk in Habakkuk 1–2. We will explore the various tones and dynamics that exist between them, with a focus on what we can learn from Habakkuk’s relationship with G-d and how our study of this text can influence our own theology or prayer experiences.

sessions.title: From the Bell Review to real change: young people in politics
sessions.desc: You don’t need to be an MP to shape politics. Drawing on his involvement in the Bell Report, Jonathan Frisher explores how young people can turn the issues they care about into action, make their voices heard and influence the people who make decisions.

sessions.title: The psychology of sports betting: what every parent, educator and fan needs to know
sessions.desc: A quick bet on the match. A friendly flutter. What could be the harm? Sports betting has never been easier, or more heavily marketed. We'll explore what's really happening in the brain when we bet, how the apps are designed to keep us playing and why smart people keep making losing bets. No betting experience required. All are welcome.

sessions.title: The shofar and Hasidic niggunim: the power of sound beyond words
sessions.desc: What can a simple sound or a wordless melody awaken within us? This lecture invites you to explore the connection between the shofar and Hasidic niggunim. Through breath, sound, and repetition, both traditions touch the heart, express what words cannot, and open a path to prayer and joy. Join us on a journey into the spiritual power of sound.

sessions.title: Holocaust Memorial Day 2027: no place for prejudice
sessions.desc: The Holocaust followed anti-Jewish prejudice that was encouraged in everyday life. Join Olivia Marks-Woldman (CEO, Holocaust Memorial Day Trust), Karen Newman (vice-president, Board of Deputies) and a rep from KeshetUK to discuss this history and challenging prejudice today, including antisemitism, homophobia and disability discrimination.

sessions.title: Mahloket Matters #2: is it possible to be too inclusive? (2 of 3)
sessions.desc: Continue exploring the Pardes Institute's curriculum on Mahloket (disagreement) by exploring the following questions: How do we decide when to stay in relationship when we deeply disagree with someone? What is at stake in making these decisions? We'll explore Jewish text, engage in role play, and learn new skills along the way!

sessions.title: Coffee hour: meet the 2027 Limmud Festival chairs
sessions.desc: Harry and Nicole will be sitting in the bar for around an hour to chat about Limmud Festival 2027. Come for a coffee and a chat about what you'd like to see at next year's Festival and how you can get involved – no need to sign up, just drop in and say hello!

sessions.title: Building on old foundations
sessions.desc: Contemporary Jewish life is built on the past, but there are many different ways to react to tradition. Taking inspiration from art and architecture which face the challenge of making new work in significant historical sites, how can we thoughtfully and creatively engage with our heritage, acknowledging the past and giving space to the present?

sessions.title: The royal mohel: Jacob Snowman and the rise of medical circumcision
sessions.desc: During the 20th century, circumcision was transformed from a source of stigma into a symbol of successful Anglo-Jewish integration. Nobody was more instrumental to this shift than Dr. Jacob Snowman, famous for circumcising the future King Charles in 1948. This talk explores Snowman as man, myth and legend, up to and beyond his death in 1959.

sessions.title: Same hate, different target? Refugees, migrants and the Jewish story
sessions.desc: We often talk about antisemitism and anti-refugee sentiment separately. Both turn the stranger into a threat. But do they have more in common than we think? If so, fighting one could mean fighting the other. Could changing how people think about refugees today help in the fight against antisemitism? Join Rabbi David Mason to explore the links.

sessions.title: I can't deal with this now
sessions.desc: At a time when many Jewish communities are focused on security, the war in Israel-Palestine and key domestic issues, how do we find compelling ways to talk about global challenges like climate change, nature loss and poverty? Come to this session to reflect on texts that speak to what new narratives we need to bring to these conversations.

sessions.title: On the frontlines of global Jewish life: Jewish Agency shlichim on leadership, crisis, and connection
sessions.desc: What does it mean to represent Israel and strengthen Jewish communities during some of the most challenging moments in recent history? Join a panel of Jewish Agency shlichim (emissaries) serving around the world as they share personal stories, hard-earned lessons, and unique perspectives on education, engagement, leadership, and crisis response.

sessions.title: Halachic feminism and women's leadership in Orthodox communities
sessions.desc: What roles can women hold within Orthodox communities, and how has halachic feminism shaped communal leadership? This session will explore the relationship between halacha, women's religious leadership, and the changing life of Orthodox communities. In loving memory of Brenda and Russell Smith z"l.

sessions.title: See the unseen
sessions.desc: ‘He always wants to know where I am. He says it’s because London isn’t safe for Jewish women.’ Caring or controlling? Explore the subtle signs of coercive control, what healthy relationships look like, and how we can support someone experiencing abuse. Join Jewish Women’s Aid to learn more.

sessions.title: Medieval haggadot and zine making
sessions.desc: Join me to take a look at one of the most important Jewish tales – the Passover story. We will look at some medieval haggadot that tell the ancient story in a contemporary style, before creating our own zines that can be added to your bookshelf!

sessions.title: When is it a mitzvah to criticise? · The Open Beit Midrash
sessions.desc: Jewish tradition values argument – and commands us to rebuke wrongdoing. When does loyalty require us to speak out, and when does criticism become destructive? Through Jewish sources on tochecha (rebuke) and machloket l’shem shamayim (disagreement for Heaven's sake), we’ll explore disagreement, responsibility and what we owe our communities.

sessions.title: Gaza beyond the headlines
sessions.desc: Abdalrahman is a refugee from Gaza, an educator and peace advocate. He will share his personal story and experiences of life in Gaza. Yara lives in the West Bank and will draw on her work with humanitarian organisations to explore the impact of the war on children in Gaza.

sessions.title: Sketch and stretch
sessions.desc: Join us for a relaxed outdoor drawing session where we'll sketch what we see on our walk around Pendigo Lake! No prior drawing experience necessary and materials will be provided.

sessions.title: Good Morning Gaza: art, war, and memory
sessions.desc: Screening of Good Morning Gaza, a documentary following Israeli soldiers after 7 October as they create an improvised podcast during their military service in Gaza, using humour and creativity to cope with war. A discussion follows about the film, the moral complexities of war, personal experience, collective responsibility, and the role of art.

sessions.title: Speed Mishnah: learn Rosh Hashanah! · The Open Beit Midrash (2 of 4)
sessions.desc: Have you ever wanted to learn Mishnah but didn't know where to start? Come along and learn an entire masechet (tractate), and celebrate with a siyum (completion party) on Wednesday morning! A range of presenters will teach every single mishnah in Tractate Rosh Hashanah over four days. No previous knowledge or Hebrew required.

sessions.title: Deciding who gets the future: health, inequality and where society is heading
sessions.desc: Two neighbourhoods a few miles apart can differ by a decade in life expectancy, and Michael Marmot has spent his career explaining why. Ageing populations, insecure work lives and new medical technology are all reshaping that gap, though not necessarily in a clear direction. Where will we be in ten years?

sessions.title: JW3 is listening and we want to hear from you!
sessions.desc: We’re inviting you to join us for a fun, informal co-creation session. Bring your ideas, passions and curiosity. Meet the JW3 team, share what matters to you, and help shape future programmes and events. No experience needed – just your ideas and a desire to help build the next chapter of a vibrant, inclusive JW3 together.

sessions.title: Trailing the Jews of the Dutch countryside
sessions.desc: Amsterdam is a jewel in the history of Dutch Jewry. But let’s provincialise Amsterdam and look at the Dutch countryside! In the 19th/20th centuries, small Jewish communities thrived and built shuls, cemeteries, Jewish education and more. Travel with me from Groningen to Maastricht and learn more about the rich tapestry of Jewish history in Europe.

sessions.title: Only one door to l’dor v’dor? Expanding our concept of Jewish continuity
sessions.desc: What does l’dor v’dor mean beyond the nuclear family? Jewish continuity is often understood as: raise Jewish children. But passing on our heritage can take many forms. We’ll use Jewish thought, lived experiences and historical Jewish figures as inspiration to expand ideas about intergenerational connection. Join us to rethink our Jewish legacies!

sessions.title: The power of being believed: validation, health and hope
sessions.desc: From invisible pain and a 13-year diagnostic odyssey to professor, CEO and activist, I share how lived experience became purpose. Through the intersections of chronic illness, being gay and Jewish, I explore the harm of not being believed, the ethics of validation, and how finding my voice transformed pain into activism, leadership and change.

sessions.title: Oy vey, Broadway! Tales from an out, proud gay Jew in showbiz
sessions.desc: Too queer for some rooms? Too Jewish for others? Actor, singer, director, host and artist Ralph Bogard has done every kind of show and ALMOST every job, from the West End to NYC to interviewing the iconic John Waters. In this funny, honest talk, he shares what he’s learned and what happens when you stop leaving part of yourself at the stage door.

sessions.title: Sacrae: singing 'a cappella' Christian settings of Jewish texts (2 of 2)
sessions.desc: A chamber choir for Limmud! If you love singing a cappella settings by the likes of Tallis, Brahms and Howells, and if you've got good sight-singing skills, then Sacrae is for you. We'll sing Jewish-texts-only sacred choral works. Note: you’ll find music links below this info on the website (not on the app).

sessions.title: How are obsessive compulsive disorder (OCD) and Judaism connected? A lived experience analysis
sessions.desc: My session comes from personal experience: I have OCD and grew up in the Jewish community – each experience helps me understand the other. We'll examine the parallels between the suffocatingly meticulous nature of religious rituals, and the practices that those with OCD often follow, with the aim of promoting freedom and self-realisation for all.

sessions.title: Judaism uncovered
sessions.desc: How do you deal with bad rabbis? What does Judaism say about eating disorders? Is there a Jewish theology of sleep? How did the Bible get divided into chapters? What does rabbinic literature say about mother-son relationships? We will look at important Jewish questions that do not usually get covered but should. And others.

sessions.title: Can Jewish law save a world in crisis? Halacha, power, and the planet
sessions.desc: Three rabbis and two environmental leaders examine what responsibility means in a global crisis, across personal habits, communal action and professional influence. Does halacha over-emphasise the individual and ignore the collective? Can ancient tradition offer a workable decision-making framework for business leaders and policymakers?

sessions.title: UK Jewish Film Festival: Changing Perspectives – short films for teenagers and all the family
sessions.desc: With an opportunity for discussion after the screenings. Carry with Both Hands: Leah caught in the middle of her family’s divided ideas. Dead Parent Club: Ollie’s dad has unexpectedly died. Ollie and his sidekick make a chaotic quest for peace. Rachel Jones Needs a Boyfriend Not a Bat Mitzvah: A young Welsh Jewish girl's quest for a boyfriend.

sessions.title: Family chocolate tasting
sessions.desc: Explore the fascinating origins of chocolate and handle real cocoa beans. We’ll mindfully sample a variety of chocolates and learn how to taste like a true expert. We will end the session with a chocolate game! Vegan options will be available.

sessions.title: Why did we invent G-d?
sessions.desc: A study of source texts and a shared journey into the greatest foundational idea around which Jewish thought was built.

sessions.title: Variant sudoku
sessions.desc: Come learn how to do variant sudoku and solve your very own, home-made, Limmud-themed sudoku!

sessions.title: Lo Nafsik Lirkod (Don’t stop dancing) – Am Yisrael Chai
sessions.desc: Come and experience the Israel 79 programme launched by the Israeli Dance Institute for schools, youth movements and everyone who wants to engage with Israel. You do not have to be an expert to join but you may be when you leave! Dance is a celebration – join the circle!

sessions.title: From activism to the ballot box
sessions.desc: Can you turn conviction into a political party – and take the risk of standing for office yourself? Yonatan Zeigen shares what it took to build a new political home, step into the electoral arena and find out whether change is possible from inside the system.

sessions.title: Can science build a bridge when politics is stuck?
sessions.desc: From chemical engineering to serving as Israel’s acting chief scientist, Tareq Abu Hamed has worked across research, technology and public policy. This session asks what science can make possible across political divides – and where technical solutions meet the harder realities of power, trust and politics.

sessions.title: The American Jewish story: what happened – and what comes next?
sessions.desc: American Jews built a remarkable story of belonging, achievement and influence. But the old certainties are shifting. What has changed – and what comes next? Gil Troy explores the choices, challenges and possibilities facing American Jewry, and asks how this community can carry its history forward while helping shape America’s future.

sessions.title: Women’s Gallery live: rethinking Orthodox leadership
sessions.desc: Join Joanne Greenaway for a live Women’s Gallery podcast recording with Shira Marili Mirvis, Israel’s first female sole spiritual leader of an Orthodox community. They’ll explore her pioneering approach to communal leadership, opportunities for women in Orthodoxy, Israel-Diaspora perspectives and what the Jewish world needs next.

sessions.title: Yossi Zabari — Live in Hebrew
sessions.desc: A Hebrew-language performance by Yossi Zabari blending stand-up, storytelling and spoken word, drawing on personal experience, politics, identity and life abroad.

sessions.title: Mrs Elswood lookalike competition
sessions.desc: Have you ever looked at your jar of Mrs Elswood and felt you were looking in a mirror? Come along for a chance to be crowned Limmud Mrs Elswood lookalike 2026. Separate categories for pre- and post-rebrand. Spectators welcome.

sessions.title: The PEDJ of reason: competing theories of human biblical authorship
sessions.desc: Academic Bible study has transformed since the 19th-century theory of the J, E, P, and D sources, but Jewish conversations about these ideas have not kept pace. We’ll compare the Documentary Hypothesis and the Supplementary Hypothesis, by applying them to three familiar texts: Jacob's ladder, the sale of Joseph, and the splitting of the sea.

sessions.title: Who is this for? Telling Jewish stories to insiders and outsiders
sessions.desc: What happens when the people tasked with explaining Jewish culture to the world become part of the spectacle? International curators and educators explore crafting Jewish narratives for both community insiders and wider audiences, and the realities of representing identity, memory and heritage: where the curator ends and the exhibit begins.

sessions.title: Jews love dead Jews
sessions.desc: Why do we so often connect with Jewish stories through tragedy, persecution, and death? From Holocaust education to commemorations and memorials, are we telling a story of Jewish life, or primarily of Jewish suffering? This storytelling session asks what happens when we take ownership of our narrative and focus on the stories we want to tell.

sessions.title: The footballers’ table: what really happens behind the scenes?
sessions.desc: What is a footballer’s life like beyond the match? Drawing on nearly 500 games and his work supporting players at the Professional Footballers’ Association, Dean Furman shares dressing-room stories, the game's highs and hard lessons, and the skills that help players thrive after football. Bring your questions and football stories!

sessions.title: From the heart concert
sessions.desc: Join Abbie Strauss for a soulful concert of music that inspires hope, healing, and connection. An intimate musical experience that reaches the heart and brings us together.

sessions.title: Jurnet's House: the oldest Jewish house in England – its story and its future
sessions.desc: Jurnet’s House is a rare living link to medieval Jewish Britain. Rooted in Norwich, it reveals a largely hidden story of life, contribution, prejudice, expulsion and survival, and brings that history into public view through an exceptional surviving place.

sessions.title: Imagining our own death
sessions.desc: The Piacezner Rebbe, Rabbi Kalonymus Kalman Shapira (1889–1943), in the Warsaw Ghetto, wrote 'Hachsharat Ha'avreichim', a spiritual manual filled with visualisation practices. In this session, through study of his writings and a guided meditation, we will imagine our own death, and afterwards, have a chance to draw, journal, and reflect together.

sessions.title: Dialogue in motion
sessions.desc: Can we understand each other without a word? Using tools from dance movement therapy, we'll explore how movement builds connection and synchrony in a group, and how bodies can hold a dialogue on even the most complex topics. And we'll have fun. No experience needed, just a body that moves and a heart that beats.

sessions.title: Book recommendations club
sessions.desc: Think book club… but without the homework, guilt, or that one guy who actually did read the whole book and wants to give a Limmud talk about it. In this session, we’ll discuss our favourite reads, share what’s currently keeping us up past bedtime, and connect with fellow book lovers – no essays, spoilers, or required reading lists included.

sessions.title: From Bafana Bafana to the PFA: a Jewish journey through football
sessions.desc: Born in South Africa, Dean Furman built a professional career across British and South African football, earning 58 caps for Bafana Bafana and captaining his country. A proud Jew, he’ll reflect on Jewish identity in football, his playing career and his work supporting players at the Professional Footballers’ Association.

sessions.title: A deaf rabbinical student: authority beyond cantillation
sessions.desc: I am a profoundly deaf woman training to become a rabbi. I cannot chant the Torah, and most congregants don’t sign. Drawing on rabbinical training, the Shulchan Aruch on Torah-reading errors and Masorti rulings on sign language, I ask who controls ritual roles and what a congregation must change to recognise leadership beyond sound.

sessions.title: Jewish sociological research
sessions.desc: This session examines social scientific research in Jewish communities. Research is often directed by communal organisations and deals almost exclusively with antisemitism and demographics. Examples from my research in Berlin, Germany, highlight benefits, risks, and taboos of an independent and scientific approach to studying our communities.

sessions.title: Kol HaNeshamah: songs for the soul
sessions.desc: When words aren't enough, music can offer comfort and help us find hope. Join Zoe Jacobs and Sarah Grabiner on a musical journey through familiar favourites and new discoveries. We'll find connection as together we sing texts that offer light in the darkness.

sessions.title: The assignment: born for this
sessions.desc: Raised in the golden age of Jewish New York City, Vanessa chronicles three years that transformed her Jewish life. Through spoken word and raw storytelling, she moves through 7th October, Israel, motherhood, fractured friendships, cancellation, being heckled onstage and finding her voice when staying silent was no longer an option. Followed by Q&A.

sessions.title: Stirred, not shaken: essential mixers for Jewish leadership of the 21st century
sessions.desc: What can an Old Fashioned, an Espresso Martini, and a Tequila Sunrise teach us about Jewish leadership? More than you might think. In this interactive session, participants will mix cocktails while exploring leadership styles, evolving communal needs, and the challenges facing Jewish leaders today. Come thirsty for insights, and liquor!

sessions.title: West Shire Story: scratch musical and discussion
sessions.desc: If you love West Side Story and/or care deeply about Jewish identity and continuity, then this session is for you! We will start with a ‘scratch performance’ (a first, informal run-through) of West Shire Story – a short musical about a Jewish family moving from north London to rural England – and then discuss some of the issues it raises.

sessions.title: The Greek Jewish story: from ancient roots to the Holocaust
sessions.desc: Greece’s Jewish story spans over two thousand years, from the Hellenistic world to the destruction of Greek Jewry in the Holocaust. Historian Leon Saltiel brings this history to life through the people, places and turning points behind it. What can Greece’s past reveal about Jewish life in Europe – and the histories we still struggle to remember?

sessions.title: Together for our planet
sessions.desc: 'Laudato Si' and 'Al-Mizan' are great Catholic and Muslim manifestos on caring for our shared home. As work begins on a Jewish document, Kamran Shehzad of the Bahu Trust and Jonathan Wittenberg of EcoJudaism discuss how our faiths inspire and challenge us and bring our communities hope and direction in facing the climate and biodiversity crises.

sessions.title: The marvellous mind of Leon Roth: where Spinoza met Maimonides
sessions.desc: Leon Roth, founder of Hebrew University’s Philosophy Department, rescued G-d from the Cartesians. He showed how the ostracised Baruch Spinoza used the rabbinic thinker Moses Maimonides to explain moral conduct and what it means to love G-d. The London School of Jewish Studies’ dean asks a world expert on Roth how we can live a good life.

sessions.title: Being an Orthodox woman-rabbi: Orthodox feminism in Israel
sessions.desc: As an Orthodox woman-rabbi committed to halacha, I explore how feminism and Orthodoxy thrive together. I share my journey and the changes transforming women’s roles in Jewish law, study, and synagogue life. I discuss how female religious leadership is reshaping public discourse and shaping the future of contemporary Judaism.

sessions.title: Sacred breath: somatic healing in a Jewish container
sessions.desc: Breathe, sing and feel. This experiential workshop weaves somatic breathwork with Jewish kavanah (intention) and niggunim (wordless melodies) to help release emotion, settle the nervous system and integrate what arises. No experience needed, just bring yourself (and a water bottle, comfy clothes and a blanket).

sessions.title: G-d was in this place – unpacking the meaning of Jacob’s ladder
sessions.desc: After Jacob leaves his family home he lies down to sleep and sees heavenly beings ascending and descending a ladder. When he wakes up he realises that this was no ordinary dream. In this session we will look at a series of commentaries (in English) and diverse works of art to aid our understanding of this extraordinary moment.

sessions.title: Great 'Jewish' American Songbook
sessions.desc: The Great American Songbook is a term given to popular songs written mainly during the first half of the 20th century. A large number of these composers and lyricists were Jewish (eg Gershwin, Berlin and Arlen). In this interactive session we will explore the lives of some of these people and Jonathan will perform a selection of these songs.

sessions.title: Scottish ceilidh dancing
sessions.desc: If you're feeling scunnered, get yerself over for some traditional Scottish dancing at Limmud's ever-popular annual ceilidh! Any and all are welcome – no prior experience necessary!

sessions.title: UK Jewish Film presents: Yentl (1983)
sessions.desc: Adapted from a story by Isaac Bashevis Singer, with a screenplay by Jack Rosenthal and Barbra Streisand, Yentl is the star’s directorial debut, with an award-winning musical score and great songs. Yentl has a passion for learning. After her father dies, she disguises herself as a boy in order to attend a yeshiva. But then she falls in love…

sessions.title: Benny Morris: cross-examined
sessions.desc: What can historical evidence establish – and where does moral judgement begin? In a searching conversation with Vadim Blumin, Benny Morris faces questions about his research, its critics and the conclusions drawn from it. From Palestinian displacement to Israel’s fight for survival, a chance to examine the arguments with the historian himself.

sessions.title: Zionism for me is… a love letter from the margins
sessions.desc: What happens when the Zionism you inherited collides with the Zionism you encounter? Through a personal text laid out like a page of Talmud, we’ll explore memory, longing, power and responsibility, putting competing Zionisms and their critics into conversation. Then we’ll turn to the margins: what is your Zionism, and how would you argue with it?

sessions.title: Saturnine Judaism: an exploration
sessions.desc: This session examines HaShem's origins as a Near-Eastern Saturnine deity, paralleling the Canaanite god El, Hurrian Kumarbi, Syrian Dagan, and Sumerian Enlil. It traces this deity's developmental history and character as well as its influence on Judaism's oldest foundations, asking what this reveals about the nature of G-d and Jewish peoplehood.

sessions.title: The 'R' word – retirement...
sessions.desc: The session will be extremely informal, focussed entirely on the retirement experiences – or retirement fantasies – of the attendees. The discussion will be 'gently' facilitated, seeking to ensure that all attendees have an opportunity to participate in whatever ways they find most comfortable.

sessions.title: Sunrise, sunset, showtime! A queer Jewish cabaret
sessions.desc: Show tunes, chutzpah, a little kvetching and a lot of kvelling (bursting with pride). A nice Jewish boy goes from a brother (and camel) in Joseph to a Kylie musical to Tevye? He should be so lucky! And he was. Ralph Bogard brings his queer, Jewish take on great songs from musicals to Limmud. Sing along if you can’t help yourself.

sessions.title: Arguments for the existence of G-d
sessions.desc: I present contemporary arguments for the existence of G-d. Is G-d the sort of being whose existence can be proven, or argued for? Already convinced G-d does or doesn't exist? On the fence? We'll explore these questions with good humour and mind-warping philosophy! L'ilui nishmat Shaul Ben Yehuda Arieh / In loving memory of Shaul Berkowitz z"l.

sessions.title: What's new in the collection at Manchester Jewish Museum?
sessions.desc: In the last year, Manchester Jewish Museum has accepted over 100 new objects into their collection - from recipe books and workplace antiques to reflections of Jewish life in Manchester today. In this session, curator Samuel will share stories about these fascinating acquisitions, and showcase some of the museum's ongoing projects.

sessions.title: HaTikvah – hope and responsibility
sessions.desc: Hope is a core Jewish value – a force that has sustained the Jewish people throughout history, embraced by the Zionist movement and taken as our anthem. But what does it mean to have hope? What can our sources and history teach us about it? HaTikvah (Israel's national anthem, 'The Hope') asks not only what we hope for, but what hope demands of us.

sessions.title: From jazz to Hijaz
sessions.desc: What made a jazz singer become a paytanit (singer of liturgical poetry)? In this uplifting session, Yahala shares – and mainly sings – her personal journey as a musician reconnecting to her Sephardi roots. Through stories and a fusion of musical traditions, join us for a soulful exploration of identity, heritage and the niggunim that bring us home.

sessions.title: The ban on so-called LGBT+ conversion practices and the people it impacts
sessions.desc: So-called LGBT+ conversion practices can occur in religious communities, healthcare and families. This panel will explore what these practices look like, their impact on LGBT+ people, the draft UK bill to ban them, and the role of faith communities, centring those affected and asking what Jewish communities can learn.

sessions.title: Did Judaism invent the nudge?
sessions.desc: What can a mezuzah teach us about behavioural science? Why does Judaism make us count, bless, repeat, remember and ritualise? From Shabbat to tzedakah, discover the hidden behavioural nudges woven into our laws and practices – and what they reveal about how Judaism shapes not just what we do, but who we become.

sessions.title: Building beyond the walls: learning from the world's best batei midrash about how a house of study can transform Jewish life in the UK
sessions.desc: Get inspired by the success and impact of modern yeshivot, Hadar and Pardes, hearing how they can be a powerful place of belonging and community that revitalises the Jewish ecosystem, with students spreading their confidence, commitment and skills. We'll also get a sense of an emerging UK beit midrash culture and how to shape it.

sessions.title: Log your Limmud lore
sessions.desc: So many great Limmud stories get lost to time. Come and chat with other Limmudniks to tell your stories and write them down so that we can compile a log of Limmud lore (i.e., great Limmud moments, think funny overheard conversations, unexpected interactions, session mishaps etc.).

sessions.title: Israeli dance party
sessions.desc: Let your hair down and have fun at our late-night Israeli dance party – a mixture of old and new, circle, line and partner dances. A lot of fun for lots of people! We start with easy dances so everyone can be included. Save your energy and join our circle!

sessions.title: Why safeguarding is a scam (but doesn't have to be)
sessions.desc: Institutions love to hold up their safeguarding programmes as proof that they are safe environments for children, but what happens when abuse actually occurs? Is safeguarding alone actually helpful, or can it act as a fig leaf for bad-faith actors? Let's discuss how to recognise and evaluate that question, and what solutions might exist.

sessions.title: Lewis Goldsmith – radical, Napoleonic spy and journalist
sessions.desc: Jeremy Smilg will talk on Lewis Goldsmith. Goldsmith was a radical English Jew, who worked in Paris for Talleyrand and became a spy for Napoleon, before returning to England and becoming a conservative polemicist calling for Napoleon's assassination.

sessions.title: Georg Placzek: the atomic age's most influential background character
sessions.desc: Fondly remembered but rarely credited, Georg Placzek, son of wealthy Jews, the ‘ever stimulating Bohemian’, spent his life crossing continents, dodging Nazis, Soviets, and bureaucrats alike, while contributing hugely to the atomic age. Who was he? What did he discover? Why was he ‘done with all jews’? This session is for a non-scientific crowd.

sessions.title: Karaoke
sessions.desc: We're going to have to pay a huge damages bill to the Hilton after this session because we're about to raise the roof! Come and belt a song that represents your Jewish identity, or perform a ballad by a Jew, for some Jews. We just simply can't wait to see you there.

sessions.title: Feast of strangers: a menu of meaningful conversations
sessions.desc: Curious to try a deeper conversation with someone you’ve never met? Join this warm, friendly space inspired by Theodore Zeldin’s Feast of Strangers. Pick a topic from the conversational menu and discover what happens when strangers talk. This session is fully participative and offers a chance to connect with someone in a fresh, interesting way.

sessions.title: And now they're 26...
sessions.desc: The Jewish Lives longitudinal study has been following young Jews in the UK since they were 11 years old. They are now 26. Come and hear about our latest findings – where are they living? What are they doing? Who are their friends and partners? How do they relate to Israel?

sessions.title: Oy the world's a stage: Anglo-Jewish theatre 1956–2026
sessions.desc: Until now, Jewish identity was rarely seen on stage beyond Broadway imports or when disguised. Now Jewish writers are openly disentangling Anglo-Jewish identity in the West End and beyond. Is this a golden age for British-Jewish playwrights and what does it mean for our culture?

sessions.title: This is how we fight in Gaza
sessions.desc: Drawing on testimonies from soldiers and commanders who have served in Gaza since 7th October, this session examines Israeli policy, its implementation and consequences on the ground. Recurring patterns across testimonies reveal the reality behind military actions and invite us to question and confront policies carried out in our name.

sessions.title: 'Living the mystery': grasping the ungraspable
sessions.desc: How has Jewish understanding of G-d evolved throughout the ages? Through diverse (Jewish) sources, we explore how generations have related to the Divine and how historical contexts shaped these perceptions. What can these changing perspectives teach us about approaching the Almighty, and how might they enrich our own understanding of G-d today?

sessions.title: Psychedelic rest and integration
sessions.desc: Embark on a hypnotic musical adventure with Nathan Finkel, a musician who blends traditional instruments with a series of reluctant machines creating a unique and immersive aural experience. Drawing on Jewish melodies used in prayer and meditation, he offers an escape from the bustle, inviting you to unwind in a world of whimsical soundscapes.

sessions.title: Speakeasy
sessions.room: I hear there's a whisper going round...
sessions.desc: Really, keep shtum.

sessions.title: Silent disco
sessions.desc: It’s Mr Worldwide! Come and get your headphones and dance the night away! Mr Worldwide!

sessions.title: Bouncing into Graceland
sessions.desc: A singalong session to celebrate the 40th anniversary of the greatest album by the greatest Jewish singer-songwriter: Paul Simon’s Graceland. Bring your instruments and your voices and let's get together and call ourselves an institute.

sessions.title: Vayarutz vayomer: he ran and he talked – or run and chat (3 of 4)
sessions.desc: If you fancy a chance to stretch your legs as well as your minds then do join us for this outdoor run. We can meet new people and discuss Jewish topics, Limmud sessions, running schedules or just enjoy being outside. Be prepared to run for an hour and maybe get muddy.

sessions.title: X arks the spot
sessions.desc: These tables full of beautiful art, ask for the "puzzle print" when you break here. The code might have helped Noah traverse the flood (and sounds like what artists hope to make here).

sessions.title: Darchei shalom: balancing personal religious observance and relationship with others · Limmud's Beit Midrash (3 of 4)
sessions.desc: Talmud in the original in three groups (beginners, intermediate and advanced), each with a skilled teacher. We will discuss questions such as: ‘Eating at my mother-in-law’s home – is she trustworthy?’ New faces welcome! More information on the Beit Midrash in the handbook and app – or just come for one day or stay all week.

sessions.title: Tikkun olam, but what’s in it for me? Self-interest, cooperation, and the mathematics of the common good
sessions.desc: We’ll use ideas from game theory, evolution, and behavioural science to explore individual incentives and collective welfare. We’ll ask how institutions, expectations, trust, and incentives can make cooperation possible – and what that might teach us about building systems in which doing good is also a sensible, self-interested thing to do.

sessions.title: 1290 – the Jewish community before the expulsion
sessions.desc: Fabulously wealthy financiers or oppressed outsiders? The King’s chattel or members of the ruling elite? What do we really know about the Jews of England before the expulsion, and why did it all end, if it ended at all? Come and walk in the footsteps of this long-lost community through the documents and clues they left behind.

sessions.title: Good morning, Limmud!
sessions.desc: Limmud Festival meets breakfast TV! Join our studio audience every morning for an insider’s scoop on the events of the previous day, hot takes from some of your favourite Limmud presenters, a forecast of the day’s highlights and lots of silliness and shtick.

sessions.title: Art and text: how are we like the families in the Bible?
sessions.desc: Artists have found family life in the biblical book of Genesis a fascinating subject. Come and explore some amazing artwork and study the texts that inspired the art. Join an arts educator and a rabbi to discover new ways of seeing Torah text in biblical artworks and to uncover the visual imagery of biblical texts.

sessions.title: Shared future, uncertain times: Jewish–Arab partnership after the elections
sessions.desc: With the Israeli elections behind us, what’s next for Jewish–Arab partnership?
