Join a lively conversation on where shared society stands and where it could go, and discover Seeds of Partnership, bringing young Jewish and Palestinian leaders together to learn, lead and build a shared future.

sessions.title: 'You can't get there from here, but you can get here from there': a communal visioning workshop
sessions.desc: What happens when you cross architectural principles with Montessori educational philosophy? MG Taylor is a collaborative methodology that gets people to co-create solutions for complex wicked problems. Come along to learn more and have a go in this interactive workshop where we will build a vision for our communal future.

sessions.title: Domestic service refugees – finding sanctuary and safety from Nazi persecution
sessions.desc: Around 20,000 Jewish refugees, mainly young women, entered Britain through domestic visas. For many, including our mothers, this little-known route offered a vital means of escape from Nazi persecution. What kind of welcome did they receive? Join us to share personal stories and learn about the historical background.

sessions.title: From shtetl to Savile Row: Jewish threads in British tailoring
sessions.desc: From the shtetl to the East End, Nottingham and Savile Row, discover the Jewish story woven into British tailoring. We’ll explore migration, famous names, hidden craftspeople and Jewish traditions around textiles, alongside my own family’s journey from bespoke tailor to seamstress – and my own 20+ years at the sewing machine.

sessions.title: The Jewish resilience project
sessions.desc: The Jewish Resilience Project is a lecture offering clarity in a disorienting moment. Drawing on Jewish history and the psychology of narrative, hope, and resilience, it explores the stories of the Jewish people before and after 7th October, and maps a personal and collective path towards a more resilient shared future.

sessions.title: How can they say what they're saying?!?
sessions.desc: For decades, Israel's critics have thrown the most ghastly words at Israel that they can think of to see which ones stick. There's been racism, even Nazism, of course fascism, colonialism, imperialism, expansionism, apartheid and now genocide. We'll take a dispassionate look at these and ask why such accusations are believed.

sessions.title: Mindfulness for Jews | part 3: making space for G-d (3 of 3)
sessions.desc: When life gets full, what's the first thing we let go of? Often, the very thing that nourishes us most. In this final session, we'll turn to Jewish tradition to frame the journey inward, and practise together. We may find there's more space inside than we thought. All are welcome.

sessions.title: Cutting through the noise: creativity, mindfulness and Judaism
sessions.desc: A chance to put down your phone, quiet the noise and get your hands busy. Through collage and creative prompts, we’ll explore mindfulness, reflection and some Jewish ideas about who we are and what gives our lives meaning. Come for the creativity, stay for the conversations – and leave with something you’ve made yourself.

sessions.title: What Can European Jewish Communities Learn From one another?
sessions.desc: Jewish communities in Europe are diverse, yet often face similar challenges around belonging, leadership, nd resilience. This interactive session explores what communities can learn from one another, using ECJC’s network as a lens. Participants will work through real-life scenarios and explore how cross-border exchange can strengthen Jewish life.

sessions.title: On being chosen
sessions.desc: Are we the chosen people? What might that even mean? Some Jewish philosophers have sought to expunge this belief; others have sought palatable interpretations. We'll explore one great Jewish thinker's attempt to defend the doctrine. Curious? Come along! L'ilui nishmat Shaul Ben Yehuda Arieh / In loving memory of Shaul Berkowitz z"l.

sessions.title: International Jewish advocacy in the post-7 October world: challenges and opportunities
sessions.desc: This session discusses the promotion of a Jewish agenda at the international level and how to mobilise support from governments and institutions worldwide. It will draw from real experiences from the United Nations and other international organisations, and describe how this work has changed after 7 October, including current challenges.

sessions.title: Behind the hechsher: the world of kosher certification
sessions.desc: What does it really take to make food kosher? From factory floors to restaurant kitchens, kosher certification involves far more than checking ingredients. Join David Neifeld, director of the Sephardi Kashrut Authority, for a behind-the-scenes look at modern kashrut, its challenges, surprising discoveries and halachic decisions.

sessions.title: Before you jump the gun: an insider’s account of IDF service
sessions.desc: In contemporary Britain, the IDF is deeply polarising. In this interview session, Raphael Zarum speaks with an IDF soldier about his experiences. Did blue-and-white idealism survive contact with reality? When did British sensibilities bewilder fellow recruits? What were the greatest challenges? Audience questions will be welcomed.

sessions.title: We know how the story ends: rethinking medieval Jewish London
sessions.desc: We know how the story ends: England’s Jews were expelled in 1290. But does that distort how we tell their story? Starting with the Jewish cemetery beneath today’s Barbican, we explore a community woven into medieval London, the Jew-shaped hole its expulsion left, and the long journey from exclusion to civic life.

sessions.title: Me, myself and I: performing your real-life stories
sessions.desc: Vanessa Hidary, Yossi Zabari, Rachel Creeger and Elias Faingersh discuss the joys and challenges of bringing your identity and personal history to the stage and how the audience reactions impact the performer.

sessions.title: Finding your voice
sessions.desc: For artists, and for anyone who's been holding something back. Drawn from my Rise Into You coaching programme. We look at what keeps people quiet, and practise getting loud anyway.

sessions.title: Born to be discontented: the Jewish roots of Israeli innovation
sessions.desc: Shimon Peres saw dissatisfaction as the Jews' greatest historical contribution. Is this the secret to the Start-up Nation? With 20+ years in Israeli startups, Nirit Harel explores how arguing and questioning shaped Israel's innovation, from water tech to medtech. We also ask: what is the difference between true disruption and just good marketing?

sessions.title: Chew on this: feasting, fasting and eating disorders in Jewish life
sessions.desc: In Jewish families food is rarely just food. It's love, memory, repentance, guilt, all on the same plate. Between kashrut, fasting, feasting and well-meaning comments, the table can be a minefield. Here we explore how to avoid screwing up our kids, and how to support the people we love.

sessions.title: How to pray – and why bother?
sessions.desc: Unlocking the meaning of the traditional Amidah prayer. We ask: Why these particular words? Where is their origin in the Torah, and what greater significance do they convey? Can we make this prayer still relevant today? What are the consequences if we cannot? Bring a siddur, a Tanach, and an open mind.

sessions.title: But how does AI actually work?
sessions.desc: Bring the question about how AI actually works that you have never quite dared to ask. How does a chatbot decide what to say? How is a model trained, and why does it still get simple sums wrong? What maths underlies the words? Write it on a card and put it to people who build and study these systems. No slides, no speeches, just clear answers.

sessions.title: An MP and a journey to fairness for refugees: David Mason in conversation with Peter Prinsley MP
sessions.desc: Hear David Mason in conversation with Peter Prinsley, a Jewish member of Parliament, on how he engages with refugees and asylum in the UK. From his seat on the Home Affairs Select Committee, Peter helps challenge and scrutinise government policy. But he also brings something more: knowledge of Jewish history, and values of compassion and fairness.

sessions.title: Counter-terrorism law and the Jewish community
sessions.desc: The threat of terrorism against the UK Jewish community is as high as it has ever been. This session will explore how counter-terrorism law developed and how it has impacted the Jewish community in recent years, from synagogue attacks to Palestine Action.

sessions.title: Jewish mindfulness meditation: relax... nothing is under control...
sessions.desc: When we allow ourselves the serenity of surrender to that presence which runs deeper than the managing mind, glimpses of peace become possible. Jewish Mindfulness Meditation invites us to pause for a moment, to let go and to let G-d. All are welcome.

sessions.title: Life is just a bowl of demons: Jewish Babylonian magic bowls
sessions.desc: In ancient Babylonia, demons were blamed for illness, disaster and bad luck. Fortunately, local Jews had access to the cutting-edge security technology of the day: Aramaic incantation bowls. We’ll explore the world of ancient Jewish magic and discover why, when facing evil, the most powerful weapon was always words.

sessions.title: Falling through the cracks: does Jewish life exclude non-parents?
sessions.desc: With so much of Jewish life structured around the nuclear family, how do childless people fit in? This session will look at practical ways to build more inclusive Jewish communities where connection and belonging don’t depend on parenthood. Come ready to get involved in reimagining our rituals, traditions, and communal activities.

sessions.title: Remarkable human and social wisdom 1500 years before Freud
sessions.desc: Between two famous stories in the Talmud (Baba Metsia 58b–62a) are a series of insights into the human personality and psyche – in the home and in the marketplace; plus a social agenda – far ahead of their time. No text background required.

sessions.title: Sketch and stretch
sessions.desc: Join us for a relaxed outdoor drawing session where we'll sketch what we see on our walk around Pendigo Lake! No prior drawing experience necessary and materials will be provided.

sessions.title: Self, soul and text: discovering ourselves through Jewish wisdom and music
sessions.desc: Jewish texts have the power to illuminate our lives in deeply personal ways. Through a blend of text study, music, conversation, and reflection, we'll explore timeless Jewish wisdom alongside our own experiences, discovering how ancient teachings can help us navigate modern life with greater meaning, connection, and purpose.

sessions.title: Through a veil: translating the Bible, 4: choosing a (Jewish) translation (4 of 4)
sessions.desc: Jewish Publication Society, ArtScroll, Koren ... with all the translations out there today, how should we go about choosing one? We’ll briefly survey some well-known Jewish translations and discuss their merits and faults. We’ll also learn about ‘triangulating’ translations as a way of getting closer to the original Hebrew.

sessions.title: Jumpstarting hope in Gaza: can water and energy solutions save lives now and rebuild trust?
sessions.desc: In Gaza, access to water, sanitation and power has become a matter of survival. Tareq introduces Jumpstarting Hope in Gaza, a coalition working with Palestinian partners to mobilise decentralised water, sanitation, hygiene and energy solutions. What can technical aid do in a humanitarian emergency, and where are its limits?

sessions.title: Intergenerational story collaging
sessions.desc: Interview and be interviewed by a fellow Limmudnik who was born in a different decade to you! Guidance will be provided on how to ask thought-provoking questions, and you will then get the opportunity to tell each other’s stories of Jewish joy through the medium of collage!

sessions.title: A rabbinic view of human rights and hope in Israel
sessions.desc: This session will combine Jewish texts, reports of Israeli human rights NGOs and personal experience. What is the sobering human rights reality for both Jews and non-Jews in Israel/Palestine today? What Jewish sources must drive us to action? What are the texts and experiences that sustain me and give me hope to continue after 31 years?

sessions.title: Learn to jam with the Limmud House Band
sessions.desc: Ever wanted to improvise but never quite known where to start? We'll explore how the rhythm and lead sections work together, how to find your space in the song, and we'll put it into practice with jam-friendly chord progressions. Bring an instrument, your voice or just your ears – everyone’s welcome, no experience required.

sessions.title: From Burning Man to Birmingham: lessons in community building
sessions.desc: Since 2019, Nicole has been subconsciously comparing her two favourite communal environments: Black Rock City, USA, and the Hilton Birmingham Metropole. Now, mostly to use this catchy title, she will share what she has learnt as a festival team member and participant at Limmud, and as a camp lead and ranger in the world's largest temporary city.

sessions.title: Ask an academic
sessions.desc: Join this panel of academics from across history, art, anthropology, and sociology, answering your questions about Jewish studies in British universities today.

sessions.title: Having productive arguments about Israel (and other topics)
sessions.desc: Jews have always argued, yet sometimes we may avoid heated arguments. What makes an argument productive rather than divisive? Can arguing actually bring us closer to the truth and each other? How might we bring the spirit of machloket l’shem shamayim (disagreement for Heaven's sake) into our lives and conversations (about Israel and otherwise)?

sessions.title: Medieval Jews and witches: a pattern of exclusion?
sessions.desc: In this session I will consider continuities between violence and prejudice against Jews and against witches in the European Middle Ages. The image of the witch coalesced in Europe in the 1320s, just after the great expulsions of Jews from England and France. Are medieval antisemitism and medieval witch-hunting related forms of prejudice?

sessions.title: Jewish filmmaking in a fractured time
sessions.desc: Simon worked on three Jewish films born of love for this community and its infuriating parts: The Darkest Light (Carlebach's abuse), Sabbath Queen (a queer renegade rabbi), and Alliance (Yeshiva University’s LGBTQ+ students). Matan Sacofsky's Good Morning Gaza follows IDF reservists. Clips, plus how films get made. Bring an idea to workshop!

sessions.title: Co-resistance and steadfastness: solidarity when the power isn’t equal
sessions.desc: Can you resist together when one side holds far more power – and what does solidarity look like when the stakes aren’t the same? How can we stand together without pretending the power gap is not there? Yara and Yonatan get beyond slogans to examine what works, what falls flat and what can backfire.

sessions.title: Drawing and watercolour painting
sessions.desc: For ages 5 and up. Attendees can draw or paint whatever they wish. Basic, reasonable-quality materials (paper, paints, brushes and pens) will be provided. I will provide some photographs if ideas are needed. I will be able to help beginners to start. Previously this has been a fun and relaxing session.

sessions.title: Considering the work of Achille Mbembe II (2 of 2)
sessions.desc: We’ll look at Jewish/Hebrew resonances in Mbembe's work. We’ll notice the difficult humanism of his work and look at the question of universals in both his and contemporary Jewish writing. We’ll also try and assess his embrace of the Diaspora, knowing that Jews’ relation to power has changed since the Holocaust and the establishment of the state.

sessions.title: Dance, feel good, repeat
sessions.desc: What does dancing do for our wellbeing, and why can moving to music lift our spirits? Shoshana Burns brings together conversation, feel-good movement and a fun routine you can learn and take away. Join in, watch, or simply ease into your day with music and movement. There’s no pressure to dance: take part in whatever way feels right for you.

sessions.title: Embroider someone else's socks
sessions.desc: Trade a sock with someone you may not know and leave your mark on their sole forever. Drop by the kiosk with some socks and make some friends you'll never forget.

sessions.title: The four faces of G-d · The Open Beit Midrash
sessions.desc: If G-d is not visible, how could G-d speak to Moses ‘face-to-face’ (Exodus 33:11)? Through the study of some outlandish and inviting midrashim (rabbinic interpretations), we will analyse the many faces of G-d and what they mean for our relationship with the divine today. We must face how we see this world...

sessions.title: Ashkenazi time
sessions.desc: The Jewish tradition was created in the Middle East where the sun rises at around 6 am and sets at 6 pm (plus/minus one hour). That's great in the Middle East and North Africa. Ashkenazi Jews had long summer nights and short winter days which challenge many halachic categories. They developed a unique approach to time. Come and discover more!

sessions.title: Poles and Jews after World War II: salient issues
sessions.desc: After the Shoah, Jews in Poland experienced antisemitism, political oppression, and fundamental collective identity issues. A small community re-emerged after the end of communism and thrives, though challenges abound. They include historical controversies, property issues and the Middle East conflict. This story has broader relevance.

sessions.title: The JQ: what if Jewish life was just one click away?
sessions.desc: What if every Jewish opportunity, event and organisation was just one click away? With AI at its core, discover how The JQ is reimagining how to explore Jewish life, from events and volunteering opportunities to learning, services and Jewish milestones. See the technology in action, put it through its paces and help shape its future. All welcome.

sessions.title: Rabbinic licence or propaganda? The case of Nadav and Avihu
sessions.desc: The rabbis often take licence with biblical stories, to protect the reputations of their heroes and demonise the villains. Should we celebrate their creativity or are they engaging in propaganda? We will look in depth at a less well-known and particularly egregious example. What really happened after Aaron's sons, Nadav and Avihu, lost their lives?

sessions.title: Mahloket Matters #3: how to have a hard conversation (3 of 3)
sessions.desc: How can we develop and improve our listening skills to have more peaceful and better experiences when we disagree with others? In this final offering from Pardes, learn new skills, explore new texts, and take some time to reflect on how you can be a more productive conversation partner in heightened or fraught conversations.

sessions.title: The story of Moses and the Green Man
sessions.desc: Join in a discussion between a rabbi and an Islamic scholar about an unusual story from the Quran in which Moses encounters a mysterious figure named in later tradition as the Green One (Al-Khidr). The story has Jewish parallels!

sessions.title: Beyond welcome: communication and authority in the synagogue
sessions.desc: A synagogue can welcome a deaf congregant and still leave much of communal life inaccessible. In this practical session, we redesign a Friday-night service led by a profoundly deaf rabbinical student in a congregation that doesn’t sign. Who does what, with which resources, and what happens when support fails? Access must work both ways.

sessions.title: Mental health and artificial intelligence
sessions.desc: A recent survey revealed that a third of adults have used AI tools to support their mental health. What kind of future do you want when it comes to mental health and AI? Come and explore a new set of creative materials which have been developed to help religious groups reimagine the future together with AI researchers from the Wellcome Trust.

sessions.title: The power of words: a meta-narrative for the Torah?
sessions.desc: The Torah is full of stories, but does it have an overarching narrative that delivers one core message? Join Elliott Karstadt to consider this question and to test out his theory: that the meta-narrative of the Torah is about the power of words over violence.

sessions.title: Criminal cases of interest to the Jewish community in 2026
sessions.desc: Paul Harris presents a selection of criminal cases in 2026 which are relevant to the UK Jewish community including those where Jewish individuals have been victims of hate crime and accused of crime. He also discusses how hate crime is policed in 2026.

sessions.title: The Talmudic drawing studio
sessions.desc: What does it mean to learn Torah as an artist and to engage with our heritage not for religious instruction, but for creative inspiration? Using a mix of text study and drawing prompts, experience how artistic engagement can encourage playful encounters with traditional Jewish texts, and expand the learning conversation.

sessions.title: What is the health of democracy in Israel?
sessions.desc: Israel’s democracy has faced fundamental challenges from the start. Dahlia Scheindlin, author of the 2023 book 'The Crooked Timber of Democracy in Israel: Promise Unfulfilled', assesses how democracy in Israel has fared over the last four years, and what can be expected for all those living under Israeli rule.

sessions.title: British Jewish youth movements and their changing relationships to Israel-Palestine
sessions.desc: Join Yachad for a discussion with the leaders of several British Jewish youth movements. We’ll consider how each movement approaches Israel-Palestine education and how/why this is changing. We’ll explore the increasing tension between youth movement members and older generations, as their perspectives on Israel-Palestine diverge.

sessions.title: Against the odds: why Jewish humanitarians keep showing up
sessions.desc: Amid rising antisemitism, war in Israel and Gaza, and deep foreign aid cuts, Jewish and Israeli humanitarian organisations face challenges and cynicism from all sides. Learn about their work, challenge common misconceptions, and hear remarkable stories of resilience, solidarity, and hope.

sessions.title: The Jewish journey of George Eliot
sessions.desc: George Eliot, Britain's finest writer in the 19th century, is one of the greatest writers in the English language. Her last book, 'Daniel Deronda', stands out because of its philosemitic storyline that supports the idea of the Jews as a nation who deserve a state in Palestine. The session will cover Eliot's progress towards this end.

sessions.title: Bridge and kalooki
sessions.desc: Come along to Limmud's annual bridge and kalooki (a rummy card game) session. Cards provided, just bring yourselves and we can match up groups as needed. All ages welcome.

sessions.title: Artist talk: ‘Communicating the Jewish experience’
sessions.desc: Jewish artists across the spectrum are increasingly hiding their identity for fear of cancellation. Marice will discuss how she is actively reversing this in her art practice by depicting and celebrating her Jewish identity, family and culture and how these artworks, which are intensely individual, speak to and resonate with a much wider audience.

sessions.title: Francesco Tirelli’s ice cream shop: a personal family journey through history and memory
sessions.desc: I will share the story behind my children’s book about my father-in-law, rescued by Francesco, an inspiring Righteous Among the Nations. I discuss my creative process with illustrator Yael Albert, exploring the core challenge of sensitively presenting Holocaust history to children.

sessions.title: Being a Jewish head of an Oxford college
sessions.desc: As the head of an Oxford college for 11 years I had to deal with antisemitism, encampments, Jews for Israel, Jews Against Israel and issues of free speech. Very tricky and stretching but very satisfying.

sessions.title: Sleep well, sleep Jewishly
sessions.desc: Struggling with sleep is apparently not a new phenomenon. A sleep consultant and a rabbi map the best techniques for a good night's sleep, and find that Judaism has the perfect prescription. Come to our session and say goodbye to the endless nights tossing and turning.

sessions.title: The Magic of Storytelling
sessions.desc: Magic is an incredible tool for developing presentation skills, communication and confidence. Sacha has performed for audiences worldwide and run similar workshops for FTSE 100 companies. Join him as he helps you to elevate your next presentation – whether pitching in the boardroom or sharing a dvar Torah. You may even learn a trick or two...

sessions.title: Yer a midrashist, Harry! Torah, fanfiction and the art of reading between the lines
sessions.desc: Rabbis wrote stories to fill Torah’s gaps. Harry Potter fans have done much the same, at considerably greater length. We’ll put midrash and fanfiction in conversation and ask what both can teach us about interpretation, authorship, canon and the endlessly creative Jewish act of reading.

sessions.title: Leading together: a taste of an Israeli–Palestinian leadership session
sessions.desc: What does it take to really talk to each other, and listen? How do you move past fear and barriers to actually work together? Teens and young adults: step into a leadership session built for Israeli and Palestinian young adults, and try out the skills behind real, honest dialogue for yourself. Teens welcome!

sessions.title: Finding your Jewish voice in unprecedented times
sessions.desc: How do we find – and use – our Jewish voice in this moment? Through guided writing prompts, storytelling and conversation, Vanessa helps participants explore identity, belonging and what they want to say now, turning lived experience into words. No writing or performance experience necessary.

sessions.title: The Nazification of the neurosciences: origins and consequences (1 of 2)
sessions.desc: How did German neuroscience, once internationally distinguished, become subordinated to Nazi ideology? We examine eugenics, racial hygiene, compulsory sterilisation and physicians’ roles in accommodating the persecution of Jewish scientists, before considering the fate and enduring influence of Jewish neuroscientists, including Ludwig Guttmann.

sessions.title: Understanding Israel's geography (from what river to which sea?)
sessions.desc: Israel is famously a tiny country, about the size of Wales (or New Jersey for US audiences). Despite this, it has a surprisingly varied and interesting geography. Join me for this session to explore Israel's land and natural resources and how this has shaped the country and its development.

sessions.title: ‘A Letter to the Publick’: Anglo-Jewry in pamphlets
sessions.desc: Pamphlets were the social media of their day, where political controversies were hotly debated. In the 18th and 19th centuries, arguments for and against Jewish emancipation flew back and forth in these flimsy publications. They tell a story of changing attitudes to Jews in Britain and how they advocated for political rights.

sessions.title: French elections 2027: a beginners' guide
sessions.desc: Beyond the narrow focus on the extreme right of much English-language coverage, this session seeks a broader view of the 2027 French elections by introducing a politically diverse range of candidates, Jewish and non-Jewish, and setting them in longer-term context. What do the campaign so far, and historic precedents, tell us?

sessions.title: Know thyself? Discover your leadership and communication style
sessions.desc: We’ll begin with a self-assessment, discover your PAEI profile and meet Adizes’ four archetypes of leadership and communication. We’ll uncover the patterns that shape how we act, communicate and make decisions – then explore what happens when very different, even opposite, styles meet at work, in communal spaces and in social life. Come as you are!

sessions.title: Should Jews support assisted dying?
sessions.desc: Assisted dying – whereby an already dying person can apply for life-ending medication to hasten their death and end their suffering – is not legal in the UK, but is currently being debated by members of Parliament and has a good chance of being passed. What might a Jewish response be?

sessions.title: Rabbi, Rabba, Rabbanit: meet some of the Maharat community at Limmud
sessions.desc: What makes a Jewish leader? A title? A role? The work? There are over 100 graduates of Yeshivat Maharat around the world and more studying there now. Join some of them here at Limmud for learning and a conversation. Explore the different titles, the paths that led them there, and what these choices reveal about Jewish leadership today.

sessions.title: How to read lovingly, and find in Torah lessons to be more caring · The Open Beit Midrash
sessions.desc: Does reading Torah make one better? When literature degrees are in decline, what arguments are there for the virtue of reading? We will experience this virtue through a pithy Talmudic claim about the nature of Torah (on Sotah 14a). We will see the ways we need to read and centre Torah in our communities to lovingly restore a learning of love.

sessions.title: A dance floor for everyone
sessions.desc: From children to grandparents, everyone can join in. This playful, welcoming workshop invites all ages to explore movement, music and rhythm together. Try simple dance games, share your own moves and discover how dancing can bring us closer and brighten the day. No experience or special steps needed: just come as you are.

sessions.title: Limmud fungus foray
sessions.desc: Mushrooms are mysterious. Seen as life-giving, mind-blowing and deadly, fungi inspire fear, wonder and confusion. Against the odds, they thrive in cities like Birmingham. Join a walk to meet your fungal neighbours. We’ll learn to identify fungi growing at the National Exhibition Centre (!), exploring their role in ecosystems and Jewish traditions.

sessions.title: Crafts and conversations (2 of 2)
sessions.desc: Everybody's so creative! Bring your latest craft project, and work alongside other crafty people in a low-pressure social environment. Come with friends or make some new ones: everybody's welcome!

sessions.title: In our image: should we build minds greater than our own?
sessions.desc: We are building machines designed to outthink us, and most of the debate is about safety and rules. This goes deeper. What kind of act is it to create something more powerful than ourselves, who decides, and what does it do to us? With an AI engineer, a human rights barrister, a philosopher and a rabbi with expertise in Torah and technology.

sessions.title: A Zionist and an anti-Zionist walk into Limmud
sessions.desc: What happens when a Zionist and an anti-Zionist both join Limmud's programming team? And what happens when we choose to sit down with those who see the world differently? We’ll explore different perspectives on Zionism, while seeing what might be possible if we spent more time talking with those we disagree with, rather than talking about them.

sessions.title: I disagree. Now what?
sessions.desc: Can we disagree without falling out, shutting down or trying to win? Working in small groups, we’ll use a structured tool to have a real conversation across a difference of opinion, then explore what we noticed about listening, talking and disagreeing, and what might help in everyday life.

sessions.title: Belonging on condition: Jewish, queer and caught in the crossfire
sessions.desc: What happens when the spaces where you expect to belong ask you to leave part of yourself at the door? From cultural boycotts of Jewish artists and institutions to the exclusion of Jewish voices from progressive movements, Alina Bricman and Ariel Heller explore the increasingly contested boundaries of belonging and solidarity.

sessions.title: Hello kitchen – a guide for the culinary novice
sessions.desc: Come and hear how Claire and Nic taught their dads to cook and bake, and perhaps you too will leave with a few new culinary skills!

sessions.title: Yad appreciation space
sessions.desc: We are inviting all Yads (Limmud volunteers) to stop by so that we as the Limmud team can show our appreciation for all your hard work and dedication in making the festival happen.

sessions.title: Inside the Jewish songwriter's studio
sessions.desc: What makes Jewish music good, and what makes good Jewish music? Subjective questions, to be sure, yet critical for Jewish songwriters to be able to answer for themselves. Bring an instrument and learn some tools to get you started, strategies for approaching texts, study melody as 'midrash', and leave with the seeds of some new songs.

sessions.title: Subcontractors of guilt: Holocaust memory and Muslim belonging in post-war Germany
sessions.desc: This presentation will discuss how German society 'subcontracts' guilt for the Holocaust to new minority immigrant arrivals, with the false promise of this process leading to inclusion into the German social contract and equality with other members of post-war German society.

sessions.title: Poké-Torah – where Judaism meets Pokémon – gotta catch 'em all?
sessions.desc: Is it permissible in Jewish law to participate in Pokémon battles? Can you catch Pokémon on Shabbat? Which Pokémon are the most Jewish? Tackling the questions that really matter, Roni will be bringing the Judaism while his teenage daughter Danya will be bringing expert knowledge of Pokémon. Poké-Torah! I choose you!

sessions.title: The meaning of the Kedushah
sessions.desc: The Kedushah isn’t only a key part of the Amidah service, it is the key to understanding how Jewish prayer developed and how it works. A close investigation of the evolving text of the Kedushah will reveal its history and stages of development and will cast a new light on many of our key prayers.

sessions.title: What does a Jewish MP say in Parliament to his Labour colleagues? What difference does it make?
sessions.desc: Peter Prinsley, member of Parliament for Bury St Edmunds and Stowmarket and a former ear, nose and throat surgeon, talks about his time in Parliament as the oldest and most surprised new Labour member elected in 2024. He will also speak about his continuing efforts to advocate for the Jewish people here in the UK and in Israel.

sessions.title: 1948: the war that still shapes Israel
sessions.desc: Israel’s independence. Palestinian displacement. A war whose consequences still shape the conflict. Drawing on decades of archival research, Benny Morris examines the military decisions, political ambitions and human experiences of 1948, and its lasting imprint on Israeli society. How does Israel’s founding war continue to shape everyday life?

sessions.title: Learning to stay with difficult feelings: what Saul and David can teach us
sessions.desc: What if trying to feel better is sometimes what keeps us stuck? Drawing on Acceptance and Commitment Therapy and biblical stories, we’ll explore our impulse to protect ourselves and our families from emotional pain – and the costs of doing so. We’ll consider avoidance, acceptance, and what becomes possible when we change our relationship with pain.

sessions.title: Musical mayhem: what happens if I play this?
sessions.desc: Ever wondered what happens when people connect through sound instead of words? Come play, explore and make some noise – no experience needed. There are no wrong notes here. Try things out, de-stress or just listen. It’s all about curiosity and connection, not performance.

sessions.title: Can anger be righteous? · The Open Beit Midrash
sessions.desc: From the Talmud to the Rambam (Maimonides) and into the modern period, rabbinic tradition generally views anger negatively. Anger appears as a kind of weakness, a temptation, even as the root of idolatry. But is rage always a bad thing? Can it be useful or morally sound?

sessions.title: Rikud Chadash
sessions.desc: Get a taste of the Israeli Dance Institute's youth dance programme – for the young and young at heart. Learn new line and circle dances to energise you and encourage you to join the circle.

sessions.title: A breath of fresh air
sessions.desc: Grab a hot drink and wrap up warm for some fresh air and an amble around the hotel grounds! The walk will take place along a wheelchair-accessible route.

sessions.title: Speed Mishnah: learn Rosh Hashanah! · The Open Beit Midrash (3 of 4)
sessions.desc: Have you ever wanted to learn Mishnah but didn't know where to start? Come along and learn an entire masechet (tractate), and celebrate with a siyum (completion party) on Wednesday morning! A range of presenters will teach every single mishnah in Tractate Rosh Hashanah over four days. No previous knowledge or Hebrew required.

sessions.title: Mikveh for the mind
sessions.desc: Miriam Berger and consultant psychologist Stuart Linke are building a mikveh which encapsulates both of their areas of work: religious ritual and mental wellbeing. Is this embracing its original purpose or repurposing the water? Come and hear about Wellspring and make up your own mind.

sessions.title: When learning is disrupted: children and education in the West Bank
sessions.desc: What happens to children when their education is repeatedly disrupted? Yara explores how settler violence, military activity and restrictions affect Palestinian children’s ability to get to school, learn safely and maintain a sense of routine.

sessions.title: More mysteries: how one family remained Jewish and stayed alive (mostly)
sessions.desc: My family began in a tiny shtetl near Dvinsk, in the middle of nowhere, and ended up scattered across the world. Following the Steinmans to Theresienstadt, Moscow, Cape Town, Tashkent, Rumbula and Israel, I uncovered many mysteries. I’ll explore some of the strangest, and the biggest mystery of all: how do you remain Jewish and stay alive?

sessions.title: From representations in popular culture to popular antisemitic narratives: case study in Poland
sessions.desc: Antisemitism doesn’t always emerge from where we expect. In this workshop I will use the most recent research from the POLIN Museum in Warsaw to demonstrate how images existing quietly within popular culture build stereotypes and give a platform to antisemitic tropes. We will look at similarities and differences between our countries.

sessions.title: 'The Gang' – avant-garde art, poetry and politics in 1920s Yiddishland
sessions.desc: Di Khaliastre (The Gang) was a major Yiddish cultural avant-garde group and poetry/art magazine in interwar Poland. It brought together some of the brightest stars on the interwar Yiddish literary and art firmament (I. J. Singer, Markish, Chagall), but then fell apart in the mid-1920s. We will meet the protagonists and ask: why did they part?

sessions.title: Speed dating for all (age 35+)
sessions.desc: Countless couples met at Limmud. Maybe you’re half of one of them. Bring yourself and only yourself to this relaxed session. We will be separating by age demographic in the room. Daters will choose a coloured sticker (or multiple) based on their preferences and pronouns.

sessions.title: Shine and shield: making Jewish amulets for protection
sessions.desc: Create your own personal amulet inspired by symbols of protection, blessing, and good fortune. Drawing on the Jewish tradition of the kamea, a protective amulet, we’ll look at traditional and contemporary amulets and art, then reimagine the practice through our own creations. No art experience necessary.

sessions.title: Cryptic crossword corner
sessions.desc: Join us for some relaxed cryptic crossword solving! If you've never attempted one before, come and learn from our pros. If you're a regular Ximenes, come and twist your brain with some fiendish favourites. Crosswords of all levels provided. Here's a warm-up: 'Tehillim muddled encapsulates beloved place' (6).

sessions.title: Vessels of Truth: Art, Judaism, and the Courage to Speak Out Loud
sessions.desc: How can physical making help us navigate mental health, family memory, and Jewish tradition? Join artists Jacqueline Nicholls and Marice Cumber for an intimate conversation on using creativity to process inner struggle and challenge silence. Jacqueline’s daily Talmudic drawings, textiles, and papercuts use handwriting and craft to question sacred texts and give voice to unspoken histories, while Marice’s oversized ceramic vessels transform raw diary entries and family photographs into bold, shame-defying statements on emotional pain. Together, they explore how drawing, clay, and Jewish identity intersect to turn vulnerability into resilience.

sessions.title: Tikkun olam: a changeable idea
sessions.desc: We talk about it a lot, but what exactly is tikkun olam? Join Elliott Karstadt to journey through the historical layers of this sometimes elusive concept.

sessions.title: Light the darkness – family session (9+)
sessions.desc: On Holocaust Memorial Day, we ‘light the darkness’ by placing memorial candles in our windows so light spills onto the street. Join Olivia to learn, in an age-appropriate way, about people affected, and create your own memorial candle. Be ready to be creative with ideas, crafts, text and images to honour lives destroyed. Suitable for 9+.

sessions.title: 2026 winners of the Pears Short Film Fund at UK Jewish Film
sessions.desc: Winners of the Pears Short Film Fund at UK Jewish Film. This year, both films are brilliant comedies that focus on family relationships and reflect the diversity of the British-Jewish community. The films are set in Scotland and Nottingham. A discussion follows the screenings. The films are King of the Jews and The Goyfriend.

sessions.title: Self-destruction in the Torah and the Odyssey
sessions.desc: Can a restless spirit ever truly return home? Christopher Nolan’s recent cinematic adaptation of Homer’s epic throws up some fascinating contrasts and similarities with the biblical text. We will see how Abraham, Jacob, Simeon and Levi on one hand, and Odysseus and his men on the other, cope with G-d’s law and Zeus’s law respectively.

sessions.title: If Maimonides were alive today…
sessions.desc: What would one of Judaism’s greatest thinkers make of the Jewish world today? From religious differences and modern technology to education, community and Jewish identity, we explore how the ideas of the Rambam (Maimonides) might challenge, inspire and shape our understanding of Judaism in the 21st century.

sessions.title: A Mishnaic series of unfortunate events
sessions.desc: What happens when one decision sets off a chain reaction of increasingly disastrous consequences? In this session, we’ll follow a bizarre and unexpected sequence of events, uncover the surprising legal questions hidden within it, and explore what the rabbis have to say about responsibility, consequences, and when things go spectacularly wrong.

sessions.title: Family stroll
sessions.desc: Let’s get outside, breathe some fresh air, stretch our legs and make some connections with other Limmud families!

sessions.title: Zionism in the age of anti-Zionist mania
sessions.desc: Zionism is under attack – and the argument is about more than Israel’s government. What happens when criticism hardens into denial of Jewish peoplehood and self-determination? Gil Troy confronts the anti-Zionist fervour, challenges its assumptions and makes the case for understanding Zionism on its own terms.

sessions.title: Intro to the earliest societies of the Land of Israel – part 2: Bronze Age before the 'collapse'
sessions.desc: We may never know for sure whether Jews or Israelites ever occupied what we now know as the Land of Israel before the monarchies of Israel and Judah … but someone did. In this session we move into the Bronze Age – about 3500–1200 BCE – and look at some fascinating archaeological findings from this period.

sessions.title: The wagon tale: a story, a journey, and a tune (children’s session)
sessions.desc: A story of a journey with Hasidim, a driver, horses, and a wagon – reaching their destination through music, dance, and joy. In this interactive session, we will share an uplifting Hasidic tale about overcoming hardship, play tunes, and travel on a magical journey from a traditional wagon all the way to the Beatles’ Yellow Submarine!

sessions.title: Teshuvah, tefillah and tzedakah – how can they possibly help?
sessions.desc: In a key prayer over the High Holy Days, it is claimed that teshuvah, tefillah and tzedakah (very poorly translated as repentance, prayer and charity) can achieve something significant – on the face of it, change G-d's mind about life and death. Can anyone seriously believe this and, if not, then what is it trying to say?

sessions.title: Collab-alat Shabbat: a celebration of Jewish liturgical music
sessions.desc: Calling all liturgy nerds! Join our presenters for a whistle-stop tour of Kabbalat Shabbat (the Friday-evening service welcoming Shabbat), where you will learn tunes from a variety of different styles of service. Delve into the cultural and musical significance of each piece whilst taking part in a live singing experience.

sessions.title: A little more conversation...
sessions.desc: Comedian Rachel Creeger presents an experimental new chat show. She and a guest will explore their takes on the themes that we've been taught not to discuss: religion, politics, and the hill you would die on. Three rules: the guest picks the topics, it's a dialogue with no attempt to influence each other's opinion, and they shake hands at the end.

sessions.title: Performing the unfinished past: Samuel Fischer-Glaser and Angela Stiegler’s ‘Temporary Monument in 10 000 Steps’ Au au au Hi hi hi
sessions.desc: At a time when democracy is under pressure internationally, Fischer-Glaser and Stiegler’s performance project explores Germany’s failed denazification after 1945 through the figures of survivor Philipp Auerbach, who fought for Holocaust reparations, and sculptor Anton Hiller, whose career continued despite his involvement with the Nazi regime.

sessions.title: Jews standing up for Palestinian rights: Na’amod’s approach
sessions.desc: Na’amod is a fast-growing movement of hundreds of UK Jews, mobilising the community in support of freedom and justice. Join Na’amodniks as we share our varied approach to acting against occupation and apartheid, and standing up for Palestinian rights - in the streets, in community events, and outside government.

sessions.title: The view from over here is not the same as the view from over there
sessions.desc: Understanding others’ intentions can be risky, especially when suspicion clouds our judgement. Through a dramatic episode in the book of Joshua, where civil war is narrowly averted, we’ll explore misunderstanding, communication, and jumping to conclusions – and consider how this ancient story speaks to our own divisive time.

sessions.title: How to innovate – Glaswegian style!
sessions.desc: How do you change a narrative? How do you (re)grow a community? Using the warts-and-all story of how the West End Project and Hillhead Progressive were set up, we'll consider where Judaism is at: both challenges and opportunities – all through the lens of grassroots efforts. You can also bring your own stories of innovation to share!

sessions.title: From testimony to novel: writing a Holocaust survivor’s story
sessions.desc: How do you turn a Holocaust survivor’s testimony into a novel without losing the truth behind it? Drawing on the story of Edith Geltstein Schwartz, this session explores memory, gaps, historical research and the ethical choices involved in writing a survivor’s story 80 years on.

sessions.title: What could go wrong? AI and our Jewish obligations
sessions.desc: Recent developments in artificial intelligence have alarmed even the frontier companies. What does Judaism teach about establishing boundaries on technology and retaining responsibility for agents, whether human, animal, or mechanical?

sessions.title: SpiriTeam: youth leading youth in sacred and community moments
sessions.desc: How do Jewish and communal experiences resonate with us as teens? When we’re the ones leading them. Having youth lead youth in Kabbalat Shabbat, ceremonies, and ma'amadim (gatherings) makes it meaningful for all of us – whether we’re guiding up front or participating. It creates authentic connection, genuine ownership, and leadership that lasts.

sessions.title: Step in: learn to dabke
sessions.desc: Link arms, find the rhythm and stamp your feet. Dabke is a traditional Palestinian line dance, performed at weddings and celebrations and built on moving as one. In this lively, hands-on workshop you will learn the basic steps and join the line. No experience needed, just comfortable shoes and a willingness to join in.

sessions.title: Let's talk about 'The Elephant in the Room'
sessions.desc: After walk-outs on consecutive days at Edinburgh following a song about a Shoah survivor's journey to the 'Promised Land', Daniel added this song to his show. No more walk-outs. Coincidence? Perhaps. Jewish performers face big challenges in secular spaces (and in Jewish ones). Daniel will share more songs and the 'good rabbi' will facilitate the discussion.

sessions.title: Halacha and peace in the thought of Rabbi Messas
sessions.desc: How do Sephardi halachic authorities weigh their rulings? Using Rabbi Messas and the case of stam yeinam (wine handled by non-Jews) – whether public Sabbath desecrators render wine forbidden by touching it – we will study responsa and explore his view of the relationship between halacha and peace. In loving memory of Brenda and Russell Smith z"l.

sessions.title: How do you repair a world that keeps surprising you? Epidemics, evolution, security, and finding the places where intervention matters
sessions.desc: If we want to contribute to tikkun olam, where should we intervene? A disease outbreak or other public safety threat may emerge not from one overwhelming cause, but from several modest factors interacting in just the wrong way. Together, we will explore some examples of how to understand and target these factors to make the world safer.

sessions.title: ‘Say you are my sister’: creating new commentaries from the silences in Genesis 12 and 20
sessions.desc: Our matriarch Sarah is twice passed off as Abraham’s sister and ‘shared’ with the local king. The Torah documents Abraham’s motivations, but says nothing about Sarah’s feelings. In this session we’ll explore existing commentaries on the texts, then write new ones that centre Sarah’s experiences and allow her voice to be heard. No Hebrew needed.

sessions.title: A loaf of bread, the walrus said, is what we rabbis need
sessions.desc: Long before you could view the north-west London eruv on Google Maps, the eruv wasn’t made of wire at all – it was made of bread (really). But whose bread was it, and how did bread come to define who makes up a family or community? We’ll read an excerpt from the Talmud and find out just what a Warburton’s sliced loaf has in common with Torah.

sessions.title: Poems to boost our mood
sessions.desc: Poet and author Marvin Shaw is delighted to launch his eighth book, '200 Poems To Boost Your Mood – and other stories', right here and right now at Limmud! Marvin will recite a collection of poems from the book, explain how the book came to be written and give pointers on how to use poetry as a means to find joy and healing.

sessions.title: Tricks of the Mind
sessions.desc: Sacha is a professional magician and mind-reader with over 15 years' experience entertaining audiences around the world. Join him for an interactive show combining incredible sleight of hand, clever misdirection and psychological suggestion, delivered with plenty of humour and guaranteed to leave you amazed.

sessions.title: Traitors
sessions.desc: It’s The Traitors. Get them before they get you. A room full of Limmudniks, and one is a liar. A Jewish host runs the ultimate reality game of trust and treachery. Let the mind games begin...

sessions.title: Pints of knowledge with the Jewish Agency
sessions.desc: Pull up a chair, grab a drink and let's talk Israel. Politics, culture, identity, community – even where to find a truly decent falafel. Meet the Jewish Agency delegation for a lively, informal chat. Bring a question, an opinion or just your curiosity. No speeches, no PowerPoint, no right answers. Just good conversation over a pint.

sessions.title: How to Be an Israeli Abroad Without Becoming an Embassy
sessions.desc: Saying “I’m Israeli” often feels like a political statement. Yossi Zabari explores why Israelis abroad are expected to answer for their government, while asking whether they can really detach themselves from what is done in their name. A critical conversation about responsibility, guilt, and the gap between a country, its government and its people.

sessions.title: Leadership on the line: honestly, how are we doing with leading the tiny, precious entity that is Anglo-Jewry?
sessions.desc: A session for people who hold very senior roles in Jewish community organisations. Bring a strong drink with you from the bar and be willing to participate with curiosity, openness and vulnerability. Natalie has worked with many of the community's big organisations over the last decade and will invite their leaders to kick off the conversation.

sessions.title: How a fake Hasidic rabbi captured the love of Jewish TikTok
sessions.desc: How does a cheque-kiting charity fraudster work his way out of Odessa, Texas, pretend to convert to Orthodox Judaism, adopt nine children, and get away with abusing all of them, all while building a social media empire making Jewish educational and cultural content that takes JewTok by storm? The true and horrific story of OurUniqueFamily.

sessions.title: Kavanah: after the trip – a Jewish integration circle
sessions.desc: Bring your past or recent psychedelic experiences to a confidential circle held in a Jewish frame. Through sharing, Jewish wisdom and reflection, we'll explore what came up and what we take into everyday life. Open to all, whatever your experience. Run by Kavanah (a Jewish space for psychedelic preparation and integration) and Ketter Retreats.

sessions.title: Finding your voice: LGBT+ Jewish storytelling
sessions.desc: Our stories have the power to create connection and change. This interactive workshop will explore LGBT+ Jewish storytelling, helping you reflect on your own experiences and learn how to shape and share your story. Whether you’re an experienced storyteller or unsure where to begin, everyone is welcome.

sessions.title: Modern jive dancing
sessions.desc: Come along for a fun lesson in this partner dance. It's easy to learn the basics, and it can be danced to many different types of music. Get ready to show off the moves you've just learned at the disco later!

sessions.title: The session of the damned
sessions.desc: They are the accursed ones: The ones who present sessions at Limmud yet never get mentioned in promotional emails for the festival. In this session they will compete before Þrøskvár the Dread, Knight Commander of the Limmud Email List, for a prize beyond rubies: The honour of being mentioned in 2027's publicity material. Maybe.

sessions.title: Is anyone here a doctor? My conference abstract is over the word limit!
sessions.desc: I would like to set up a network of non-medical scientists and researchers, at any career stage, to develop a lively community of people who enjoy discussing their experiences in their fields and support each other. Join this session to also get to know famous Jewish scientists past, present, and possibly future. Science memes guaranteed.

sessions.title: TVTrop – or, how and why to cantillate things that shouldn't
sessions.desc: So, you know how to leyn. You can tell your tvir from your rvia. But do you know why to leyn? What do the signs really mean? The Guy Who Made the Steamed Hams Megillah™ will introduce you to the deep structure of trop (cantillation marks) and how to use it where you'd never expect. By the end, we'll have our own mini Megillat Limmud to chant!

sessions.title: How to receive the priestly blessing without getting kugel on your shtreimel
sessions.desc: Did the Vilna Gaon use a knife and fork when he ate? How many hands should you put on your child's head when you bless them on Friday night? Which day of the year is most auspicious for wearing a greasy shtreimel (fur hat)? I will answer all of these questions and in so doing I will reveal the fundamental principle of Judaism. Buckle up.

sessions.title: When you gotta go: Jews and the loo
sessions.desc: Come and explore law, lore, and contemporary issues related to Jews and their toilets/bathrooms/water closets/washrooms/outhouses. Fear not – no bathroom humour is involved!

sessions.title: The Gala
sessions.desc: It's that time of the festival again. Join hundreds of fellow participants for the Gala, celebrating everything that has happened over the past five days. There'll be music from the House Band, entertainment, programme highlights and moments of reflection, with a chance to give tzedakah (charity). Let's close Limmud Festival 2026 together.

sessions.title: Dolly – a universal hero of our times
sessions.desc: Dolly Parton has several Jewish connections – some well-known and some less so. In this relaxing session, we’ll listen to some songs, uncover some fascinating stories and celebrate an amazing life. Come if you are a superfan or just curious.

sessions.title: UK Jewish Film presents: We Met at Grossinger's (2025)
sessions.desc: Grossinger’s was the Jewish holiday resort in the Catskill Mountains, New York State, the ‘Borscht Belt’. In its golden era in the 1950s and 1960s, it welcomed first lady Eleanor Roosevelt, comedian Jerry Lewis, baseball star Jackie Robinson, and Hollywood royalty Elizabeth Taylor. This film takes us on a journey through the resort’s history.

sessions.title: Israeli dance party
sessions.desc: Let your hair down and have fun at our late-night Israeli dance party – a mixture of old and new, circle, line and partner dances. A lot of fun for lots of people! We start with easy dances so everyone can be included. Save your energy and join our circle!

sessions.title: Darchei shalom – ways of peace: the path to building community
sessions.desc: Can I compromise the letter of the law for peace? What causes the most fighting in communities? How are people with disabilities, low-income individuals, or non-Jews viewed? How does one not compromise their personal identity when interacting with people different from themselves? We will analyse the literary and meta-themes of Mishnah Gittin.

sessions.title: The violin remembers
sessions.desc: Jewish lives, identity and culture before, during and after the Nazi era. Through live performance and the history behind the music, the violin takes us through exclusion, displacement, deportation and extermination, and finally into remembrance, showing how music can bear witness long after the events themselves.

sessions.title: Speakeasy
sessions.room: I hear there's a whisper going round...
sessions.desc: Mamaleh's the word.

sessions.title: The rebbetzin's disco
sessions.desc: Here’s the pshat (plain meaning): the rebbetzin plays good music. You dance. A lot. We all go meshuggah and have a good time. And tomorrow we can carry on kvetching about our knees, back, ashkenormativity…

sessions.title: House Band hootenanny
sessions.desc: The Limmud House Band are back for another night of musical mayhem. Expect big tunes, unexpected guests, questionable dance moves and plenty of singalongs as the band swap supporting roles for centre stage. It’s the final night and it’s time to end Limmud 2026 with a bang.

sessions.title: The pickle is present
sessions.desc: Mr Pickle enters his performance-art era. Inspired by Marina Abramović, this durational work explores presence, gaze and the briny limits of connection. Sit opposite Jewish Culture Month’s mascot and hold his gaze. No script. No props. Just you, and the pickle of your existence. Limited 1:1 capacity.

sessions.title: Vayarutz vayomer: he ran and he talked – or run and chat (4 of 4)
sessions.desc: If you fancy a chance to stretch your legs as well as your minds then do join us for this outdoor run. We can meet new people and discuss Jewish topics, Limmud sessions, running schedules or just enjoy being outside. Be prepared to run for an hour and maybe get muddy.

sessions.title: Speed Mishnah: learn Rosh Hashanah! · The Open Beit Midrash (4 of 4)
sessions.desc: Have you ever wanted to learn Mishnah but didn't know where to start? Come along and learn an entire masechet (tractate), and celebrate with a siyum (completion party) on Wednesday morning! A range of presenters will teach every single mishnah in Tractate Rosh Hashanah over four days. No previous knowledge or Hebrew required.

sessions.title: Darchei shalom: balancing personal religious observance and relationship with others · Limmud's Beit Midrash (4 of 4)
sessions.desc: Talmud in the original in three groups (beginners, intermediate and advanced), each with a skilled teacher. We will discuss questions such as: ‘How should I interact with non-Jews, especially on their holidays?’ We will finish this morning with some time together sharing what we have learnt and thinking about how to continue our Talmud journey.

sessions.title: Is protective presence on the West Bank effective?
sessions.desc: Concerned citizens, many of them Jewish, have volunteered on the West Bank offering protective presence. Now, the effectiveness of that is being questioned. We will examine the evidence, and I will reflect on my personal experience to assess whether foreign volunteers are still able to deter violence in the midst of the ethnic cleansing.

sessions.title: Tefilotenu: a spiritual humanistic siddur
sessions.desc: Tefilotenu is the first Spiritual Humanistic Jewish siddur published. It keeps Hebrew, and much of it can be sung to familiar melodies. But it does something fundamentally different, by changing the direction of prayer – not upward, but across, between people. None of it supernatural.

sessions.title: Rabbit holes and Rothschilds: my grandmother's family tree and the world of the court Jews
sessions.desc: Tracing my grandmother's family tree led me to the world of the court Jews, financiers to Europe's princes. Their families, businesses and charity spanned the Jewish world, and their networks still quietly link many of us to each other and to places we know. Discover how genealogy leads to history, and how close my family came to the Rothschilds.

sessions.title: Level up your leyning
sessions.desc: Do you want to improve your leyning skills? Come hear tips and tricks and get resources for learning longer aliyot (Torah reading portions) in a shorter time. This session is designed for people who already have basic leyning skills.

sessions.title: The kiruv movement: when faith is sold as a solution
sessions.desc: Julia was fifteen when kiruv (outreach) offered her answers. It wasn't framed as teenage rebellion, but as teshuva (repentance). After a rocky journey, Julia speaks of the almost magical solution of a world of certainty offered by kiruv to vulnerable young people. This session invites critical thinking about outreach, belonging, and belief.

sessions.title: UK Jewish Film presents: The Long Journey Home (2026)
sessions.desc: A vital cinematic testament to the Jews of Iraq. Researcher and filmmaker David Kahtan has spent over 20 years making this documentary, chronicling the history of the Jews of Iraq from ancient Babylon, through the violent pogrom of the Farhud, and the mass exodus in the 1950s, right up to the modern day. A reminder of a lost Jewish community.

sessions.title: My journey from author to interviewing 100 graphic novelists
sessions.desc: After publishing 'The English GI', Jonathan Sandler built the platform he wished existed. 100 interviews later, his Substack and work on a graphic novel imprint at Mensch Publishing mark his journey as a global interviewer. From London, Los Angeles and New York to Latvia, discover what meeting creators taught him about visual memory and history.

sessions.title: Guiding geopolitical journeys for Israel-sceptic leaders
sessions.desc: Each year Pizazz Israel Tours hosts hundreds of non-Jewish leaders like journalists, politicians, influencers and student leaders on 7–10-day geopolitical journeys through Israel and Palestinian-run areas. Many arrive sceptical of Israeli actions and Zionism. We explore how their views change through their visit and what impacts them most.

sessions.title: Reclaiming resilience: women, trauma, and healing in Addis Ababa
sessions.desc: What does resilience mean to women who have lived through trauma? Drawing on PhD fieldwork in Addis Ababa, this talk centres Ethiopian women's own accounts of coping and recovery, and closes with a reflection on an unexpected encounter with Ethiopia's Beta Israel community.

sessions.title: ‘Shmattes’: an exploration of identity through poetry, games and drama
sessions.desc: ‘These are the rags our foremothers and forefathers / pieced like prayers in the murk of sweatshops.’ ‘Velvel’s Violin’, Jacqueline Saphra’s 2023 poetry volume, considers what it means to be Jewish in the Diaspora right now. Insights from her poems, along with ‘shmattes’ from our own personal histories, will be the springboard for writing poetry.

sessions.title: Standing on the edge: navigating synagogue anxiety
sessions.desc: Ever slipped into synagogue late, hoping to stay invisible? Drawing on personal experience of navigating Jewish spaces from the margins, this session explores ritual anxiety and belonging. Using gentle cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT) tools, we’ll examine projected judgement, manage panic, and find ways to participate on our own terms.

sessions.title: BoD@Work building resilience: tackling antisemitism at the water cooler
sessions.desc: What works when responding to casual antisemitism at work? Through discussion and shared experience, we'll explore effective approaches, common challenges, and the questions people wish they felt more confident addressing in workplace conversations.

sessions.title: The Grimsby Jewish community: now a destination synagogue
sessions.desc: The Grimsby shul is in the heart of the East Marsh ward of Grimsby, which often features as one of the ten most deprived wards in the country. Now only about 12 Jews inhabit the town. But we have become a fashionable ‘destination synagogue’ and we struggle on. This session will consider the difficulties and joy of keeping a small community alive.

sessions.title: An ABC of High Holy Days liturgy
sessions.desc: A poem where the first letter of each line spells out a word may sound like primary school homework. But acrostics (and mesostics!) are a recurring feature of many prayers and piyyutim (liturgical poems) in the High Holy Days liturgy. Come and find out why they’re more than a clever word game and your High Holy Days will never be the same again.

sessions.title: Coffee morning
sessions.desc: Join us for a goodbye cup of coffee (or tea) at the Wellbeing Hub!

sessions.title: A Jewish achievement: mass youth volunteering in the developing world
sessions.desc: 160,000+ young people, including thousands of young Jews, have volunteered in the developing world through Projects Abroad, the organisation I set up in 1992. In my new book, I identify Jewish entrepreneurship and tikkun olam as key factors in the invention and its successful implementation.

sessions.title: Bringing sexy back (to the sources)
sessions.desc: Sex education is critical but has been characterised by stock phrases and oversimplification. Join a rabbi and a violence against women and girls educator as we draw on Jewish texts and feminist scholarship to unpack cliches about consent. We'll navigate these sources together to develop a Jewish sexual ethic that feels rich, nuanced, and relevant.

sessions.title: 'Oy vey ist mir': exploring the physical and mental health legacy of pogroms, persecution, and migration on the Jewish people
sessions.desc: Some physical and psychological conditions are over-represented in the Jewish people. The talk explores the historical and cultural roots of common illnesses, and locates them in the traumatic experiences of our history. Did Jewish preoccupations with health re-emerge following the events of 7th October or perhaps they never went away...?

sessions.title: Find your chutzpah!
sessions.desc: In ancient discourse and as contemporary resistance, chutzpah is the special sauce that makes difficult situations slightly easier to navigate. This session weaves together Talmudic tales with a modern memoir, which I think is quite a chutzpahdig thing to do.

sessions.title: Ever wondered what happens behind the scenes when someone makes aliyah?
sessions.desc: Join us for a look at the process from the first enquiry to approval, including eligibility, paperwork and bureaucracy, with plenty of time for questions and discussion.

sessions.title: The Jewish woman who unravelled the secret of life
sessions.desc: Discovering the double-helix structure of DNA was one of science's great achievements. Rosalind Franklin, a British Jew, played a pivotal role but was not given the recognition she deserved until long after her death. We will look at the story behind this feat, her other ground-breaking work, and how she overcame the odds as a woman and a Jew.

sessions.title: Environmental charity funding: have Greenpeace lost their green?
sessions.desc: Should a foundation support environmental charities if management become Israel/Gaza obsessed? Are geopolitics limiting our environmental options? Nick will describe a spectrum of financing (commercial, responsible, sustainable, through to pure philanthropy) along with some ethical dilemmas that he has encountered in recent years.

sessions.title: Artists: Cecile Elstein and Beatrice Lyssey
sessions.desc: The lives, art and friendship of two Jewish artists: Cecile Elstein, a sculptor, printmaker and environmental artist who came to London in 1961 from apartheid South Africa; and Beatrice Lyssey, a Swiss-German artist and art teacher who came to London during World War Two and taught Bauhaus ideas in London art schools in the 1950s and 1960s.

12117.name: Clare Aarons
12117.bio: Clare has been the learning and engagement producer at JW3 for the last two and a half years. She is responsible for the adult education programme as well as JW3's social action programme. She was recently awarded an MSc in Organisational Leadership and Innovation from the Zelikow School of Jewish Nonprofit Management, part of Hebrew Union College.

11885.name: Nic Abery
11885.bio: Nic has nearly 30 years of experience in education and has spent the past eight years working in strategic school change in Jewish schools across the UK and Europe.

12176.name: Tareq Abu Hamed
12176.bio: Tareq Abu Hamed is the CEO of the Arava Institute for Environmental Studies. He is a recognised leader in renewable energy technology and regional environmental cooperation. He was the Israeli Ministry of Science’s vice chief scientist. Under his leadership, the Arava Institute was nominated for the 2024, 2025 and 2026 Nobel Peace Prize.

12204.name: Rafi Addlestone
12204.bio: Professionally a strategy consultant in the sustainability and impact space, Rafi holds various volunteer communal roles, as chair of trustees at EcoJudaism, co-chair of Golders Green United Synagogue, trustee at JW3, and other bits and bobs. He lives in exile in north London with his wife Caro and their three daughters.

11952.name: Deborah Anstandig
11952.bio: Deborah Anstandig is the educational director of engagement at Pardes. She has taught at SAR High School and The Heschel School in New York City and has participated in fellowships in pedagogy and facilitation. Deborah is a graduate of Yeshiva University, Hebrew College Rabbinical School and the Harvard Graduate School of Education.

11959.name: Arik Ascherman
11959.bio: Arik Ascherman is a rabbi who has led Israeli human rights organisations helping Jews and non-Jews for over 31 years. He is internationally recognised as a role model for faith-based human rights activism. His NGO brings defenders from abroad to join Israelis in on-the-ground protective presence and advocates for public housing for Israelis.

12115.name: Avital Assulin
12115.bio: Avital was born in Canada to Moroccan-Israeli parents and spent many years immersed in the Jewish community there before moving to London. Through school, camp, friendships and community life she has experienced and built connections across both Sephardi and Ashkenazi traditions. She's bringing all of this to share at Limmud. Her session is dedicated in loving memory of Keith Jeremy Posner z"l.

12153.name: Anthony Bale
12153.bio: Anthony Bale is professor of English at Cambridge. He studies medieval English cultural history and has published widely on medieval Jewish-Christian relations. He was part of the team that produced the award-winning 'Blood' and 'Jews, Money, Myth' at the Jewish Museum London. His new book, 'The First Witches', will be published in February 2027.

12200.name: Dena Barasi
12200.bio: Dena Barasi is a strategic leader in the energy sector with over 20 years’ experience. Dena combines deep industry knowledge with a passion for influencing policy that benefits communities and the environment. Dena is also a trustee of Kol Rina Golders Green Partnership Minyan.

12179.name: Lisa Barrett
12179.bio: Lisa is the rabbi at Birmingham Progressive Synagogue and also works as a Jewish prison chaplain.

12085.name: Francine Barsam
12085.bio: Francine Barsam is a London-based marketing and communications consultant specialising in strategic marketing, PR, and brand development. Alongside her professional work, she leads educational discussions on her grandfather's testimony at schools and universities across the UK and at the annual Marche de la Mémoire in Saint-Martin-de-Vésubie.

12089.name: Karine Barsam
12089.bio: Karine is a programme manager connecting the next generation of professionals through events, webinars, roundtables and thought leadership. Working across technology, real estate, transport and education, she brings industry leaders and emerging talent together to exchange ideas, build connections and explore the future of work.

11931.name: Eddie Bass
11931.bio: Eddie has had an eclectic education. Now in his 91st year, he draws on his interest in drama, comedy and funny stories, which he writes himself. He digs deep into the legends of Chelm – the historic 'Village of Idiots', now a popular holiday destination in Poland. He makes up humorous stories about the Jews in both the historic and modern Chelm!

12196.name: Nadine Batchelor-Hunt
12196.bio: Nadine is a journalist, broadcaster and actor. In her documentary for BBC World Service titled “Black, Jewish, and Proud”, she travelled to Israel to interview Ethiopian Jews during the festival of Sigd. She currently works for PoliticsHome, covering politics in parliament and regularly appears on national television and radio.

11916.name: Zac Bates Fisher
11916.bio: Zac is the student fieldworker for the Movement for Progressive Judaism (MPJ) and serves as their representative on the Board of Deputies. Zac studied politics at the University of Sheffield. He is a regular lay-reader at Bromley Shul, and when not working or davening he enjoys English beer, Italian food, Russian classical music and Scotch whisky.

11951.name: Sophie Bellamy
11951.bio: Sophie Bellamy is a PhD student at Durham University. Her doctoral research explores Jewish history in the North East of England with a focus on the early twentieth century and the politics of everyday life.

11822.name: Edward Ben-Nathan
11822.bio: Edward spent his career at IBM, then helped run his tennis club. He has had an abiding interest in history and politics for decades and has presented previously at Limmud on the 'Glorious Revolution'.

12109.name: Miriam Berger
12109.bio: After 18 years at Finchley Reform Synagogue, Miriam left to pursue her dream: opening a community mikveh within a centre of wellbeing. Prior to its opening in 2028, she is immersing herself in encouraging people to dip their toes into an ocean of rituals to support mental health, elevating life's milestones and turning the tide for new chapters.

12054.name: Jonathan Bergwerk
12054.bio: Jonathan Bergwerk is an occupational psychologist and speaker who explores the lives of notable Jewish figures, ancient and modern. His talks combine biography and psychological insight with an examination of each subject’s wider contribution to society.

11953.name: Rahel Berkovits
11953.bio: Rahel Berkovits, a senior faculty member at the Pardes Institute of Jewish Studies, teaches Mishnah, Talmud and halacha. She is the halachic editor of, and writer for, the Jewish Orthodox Feminist Alliance's 'Hilkhot Nashim' source series. Rahel, a founding member of Shirah Hadash, received rabbinic ordination from Herzl Hefter and Daniel Sperber.

11838.name: Adam Berlin
11838.bio: Adam Berlin gives regular divrei Torah (talks on the weekly Torah portion) at Golders Green Synagogue, where he was treasurer. He has long come to Limmud with his wife, Andrea, and three children. He leads the media research team at Goldman Sachs. He led the Jewish societies at Oxford and Harvard Business School and studied at Darche Noam Yeshiva.

12092.name: Eden Berman
12092.bio: Originally from Jerusalem, Eden Berman is the Jewish Agency's shlicha (emissary) to Noam and Marom in London. She studied at Bezalel Academy of Art and Design and was a student and partner at the Secular Yeshiva. Eden misses the Israeli sun (and chutzpah), loves good conversation, and believes Jewish identity is something each of us gets to choose.

12045.name: Zachary Bernstein-Rothberg
12045.bio: Zachary Bernstein-Rothberg graduated from the Jewish Theological Seminary in 2026 and is now the rabbi at SHEMA, the Masorti community in Borehamwood. He received an MA in Bible and its Interpretation, and enjoys bringing both familiar and less-familiar biblical texts to broader audiences. He also focuses on mental health in the Tanach.

11904.name: Nicholas Blain
11904.bio: By day, Nicholas Blain is an educator, running Quartic Training: he helps clients through financial exams (such as Chartered Financial Analyst) and sustainable investing topics (climate, impact, environmental, social and governance). By night he runs a private foundation supporting environmental, educational, social and medical charities.

11969.name: Sonya Blanck
11969.bio: Sonya Blanck is the pseudonym of a Hastings-based writer and academic whose work primarily focuses on the occult and psychedelic facets of Judaism.

11888.name: Dalia Blass
11888.bio: Dalia is Yachad's youth and student worker. She has been involved in the Jewish community from an early age, including over a decade in Noam, and has led youth programming in Jewish and non-Jewish spaces. She is passionate about social justice beyond the Jewish community and has volunteered abroad with refugee charities.

12024.name: Lara Bloom
12024.bio: Lara is a professor and CEO.
