Her work focuses on transforming health and social care systems that often fail those they're meant to serve, embedding lived experience into research, policy, education and service design to drive measurable change. She lives at the intersection of queer and Jewish identity, with lived experience of chronic illness.

12062.name: Vadim Blumin
12062.bio: Vadim Blumin is head of the Jewish Agency for Israel in the UK and Western Europe. Ukrainian-born, Israeli-raised and now London-based with his husband and their daughter, his work sits where Israel, Jewish identity and communal life meet. A rabbi and educator, he believes in asking difficult questions, and seeking answers rooted in love.

12194.name: Ralph Bogard
12194.bio: Ralph Bogard has gone from Tevye (alternate) in the Olivier-winning Fiddler on the Roof at Regent's Park to interviewing Debbie Harry and Ricki Lake at Camp John Waters. A London actor, singer and host known for Jewish and LGBTQ work, he also directed Encore Award winner The Importance Of Being Anxious and was creative director of Joyfully Jewish.

11869.name: John Bowers
11869.bio: Barrister and author specialising in employment law, discrimination and human rights. Deputy High Court judge. Recently wrote 'Downward Spiral' about declining standards in public life. Principal, Brasenose College Oxford 2015 to 2026.

12148.name: Jason Braier
12148.bio: Jason is a barrister specialising in employment and discrimination law at 42BR Barristers. He takes particular interest in religious discrimination and carries out work alongside communal organisations on antisemitism and anti-Zionism in the workplace.

12187.name: Alina Bricman
12187.bio: Alina is the director of EU affairs of B’nai B’rith International. Prior to her time at B'nai B'rith, she was the president of the European Union of Jewish Students. She is a member of Romania’s delegation to the International Holocaust Remembrance Alliance (IHRA) and was the 2025–2026 chair of IHRA’s Committee on Antisemitism and Holocaust Denial.

11829.name: Sarah Bronzite
11829.bio: Sarah is director of education at New North London Synagogue. She previously led education at KeshetUK. She is a qualified primary school teacher and a lecturer on inclusion in the primary classroom. In her spare time she researches sex education, writes about gender-based violence and makes rye bread. Her two religions: Judaism and choral singing.

12069.name: Shoshana Burns
12069.bio: Shoshana Burns is the founder of Shoshana Burns School of Dance in Borehamwood. For 16 years, she has helped children and adults build confidence and connection through dance. A Jewish mother of two, she values the role of creativity, family and community in shaping Jewish life.

12207.name: Daniel Cainer
12207.bio: Daniel Cainer is an award-winning songwriter, storyteller and broadcaster. A veteran of 21 Edinburgh Fringes and seven off-Broadway runs, he writes original songs that explore Jewish life, family, faith and identity with wit, warmth and spiritual wisdom. His music is heard in theatres, on radio and TV, and in synagogues worldwide.

11878.name: Emily Carp
11878.bio: Emily is a fourth-year rabbinical student; a big, fat, butch lesbian; and a millennial who is chronically online. She has a lovely partner, three delightful step-kids, and a 5-year-old pug called Ziggy (who is in training to be a synadogue!)

12026.name: Mandy Carr
12026.bio: Mandy Carr, a Progressive Jew from Liverpool, has a lifelong fascination with identity, poetry and theatre. A teacher, dramatherapist, writer and former senior lecturer, her approach has been described as ‘playful, warm and inclusive’. She loves singing and is a member of the ‘Mixed Up Chorus’ in London.

12043.name: James Charles
12043.bio: When he’s not drumming in the Limmud House Band, James is the deputy technical manager at the Leicester Square Theatre in Soho. He also plays drums in the Chilli Willies, the UK’s finest Red Hot Chili Peppers tribute band.

12118.name: Mark Claydon
12118.bio: Mark is a designer, engineer and apprentice plumber. Having worked with artists such as Peter Gabriel, Madness, Everything Everything, and for BAFTA in the studio and on the road, he turned his focus to software. He has taught courses in programming from London to Gaza and enjoys creating interactive art exploring music and our brains.

12121.name: Sam Clifford
12121.bio: Sam Clifford is CEO of Jewish Women’s Aid. Sam's career in the Jewish charitable sector has ranged from working with Finchley Reform Synagogue and the Jewish Museum to freelance project management. Sam featured in the Jewish News’ ‘40 under 40’ at number 22 and is winner of the Jewish Leadership Council Lead Fellows Award 2026–7.

12168.name: Alexander Cohen
12168.bio: Alexander Cohen is a theatre critic and arts writer. He has written for the New Statesman, the Spectator, UnHerd, the Telegraph, and the Stage. At 26, he is the youngest member of the Critics' Circle Drama section and is a fellow of the Royal Society of the Arts.

11826.name: Alina Cohen
11826.bio: Alina is a lifelong maker, creative and occasional collector of far too many hobbies. She has been sewing for over 20 years and has a particular interest in creativity, mindfulness and the stories that connect us to our families and communities. She believes making things is good for the soul.

11827.name: David Cohen
11827.bio: David Cohen is a former civil servant (Ministry of Justice) with a Social Sciences degree from Leicester. He is a regular Limmudnik and his first book, 'Battles of the Wars of the Roses', about the turbulent period of English medieval history, was published by Pen and Sword in 2023. His next project will be 'Israel's early wars of survival'.

12182.name: Eliot Cohen
12182.bio: Eliot is a technology lawyer in London. Eliot co-founded Na’amod, a movement of British Jews against occupation and apartheid, following a year in Yeshivat Ma’ale Gilboa.

12102.name: Philip Cohen
12102.bio: Philip Cohen, retired social worker, approved mental health professional, and lecturer, draws on 40 years in mental health and personal storytelling to probe human dignity, classical Jewish ethics, and what it really feels like to stand on the edge of stepping into synagogue.

11908.name: Blu Cohen-Grazin
11908.bio: Blu is 16, but has already been to Limmud Festival 13 times. She is proudly atheist (as well as queer and neurodivergent) and yet has spent a remarkable amount of her life in shul and other Jewish settings. This is her second time presenting at Limmud.

12113.name: Judith Cohn
12113.bio: Judy is an English teacher originally from London then Birmingham who made aliyah at the age of 18 and subsequently relocated to Antwerp, Belgium. She studied English literature at Haifa University. She has been involved in assisting with the testimony of her brother Thomas Geve, author of ‘The Boy Who Drew Auschwitz’, who died two years ago.

11943.name: Anna Colton
11943.bio: Anna Colton is a clinical psychologist, podcaster, author, and regular on ITV's This Morning. She works with reality TV shows and West End productions, solo high performers, adolescents in crisis and eating disorders.

11812.name: Helen Conway
11812.bio: Helen Conway converted to Judaism in 2019 and is now a rabbinical student and founder of LISHMAH, a new organisation supporting Jews by choice. She is a retired judge, writer, experienced trainer and speaker and an internationally exhibited artist. She attends Menorah Synagogue in Manchester where she served on the board and in adult education.

11818.name: Belinda Copitch
11818.bio: Belinda is a researcher, author, and educator with a PhD in identity development. Bridging a background in microbiology, charity leadership, and neurodiversity, she explores workplace collaboration and autism. A 'third culture kid' now based in London, she uses her work to foster deeper human connection and institutional empathy.

11960.name: Ali Coy
11960.bio: Ali left a successful career as a software engineer to retrain as a nurse. They have volunteered in Africa, India and Palestine. Their Judaism informs a commitment to making the world a better place. Having moved from London to Glasgow out of love for being in nature, they are happiest hiking, cycling and wild camping throughout Scotland.

11983.name: Gavriel Creeger
11983.bio: A student with a keen interest in the history of the Mediterranean and Near East in ancient times and Late Antiquity.

11982.name: Mark Creeger
11982.bio: Working in corporate ethics and compliance software, Mark taught Jewish education and IT at multiple levels. He is a regular speaker and prayer leader at Barnet Synagogue and has taught bar mitzvah for over 40 years. Married to fabulous comedian Rachel Creeger, he shares two wonderful boys, a marvellous daughter-in-law and at least one grandson.

11981.name: Rachel Creeger
11981.bio: Rachel is a multi-award-winning stand-up comedian, writer and director, and the only practising Orthodox Jew on the UK comedy circuit. She's co-host of 'Jew Talkin' To Me?' podcast and has taken five critically acclaimed shows to the Edinburgh Fringe. As seen on BBC1, Amazon Prime and NextUp Comedy, and regularly heard across the BBC Radio network.

12037.name: Ben Crowne
12037.bio: Ben Crowne is a forensic accountant and serial trustee of community charities, including the Board of Deputies and the Bevis Marks Foundation – and once upon a time, Limmud. He co-edits the satirical zine 'Private Oy!' (ask your kids) from an old match factory in Bow (ask your parents).

12038.name: Tilla Crowne
12038.bio: Artist Tilla Crowne is currently artist-in-residence at Bevis Marks Synagogue. She is also the founder and co-editor of the underground satirical zine 'Private Oy!' and as a serial mushroom-botherer she will help guide you literally into and metaphorically out of the woods. If you cannot think of anything to say to her, ask her about her frogs.

12149.name: Marice Cumber
12149.bio: Marice Cumber is a ceramic artist whose practice explores her Jewish identity and family, intergenerational trauma, belonging, and the constant awareness of feeling like an outsider within the mainstream. Marice’s work has been exhibited internationally and is held in private collections.

12029.name: Teona Dalakishvili
12029.bio: Teona Dalakishvili is a project manager at the European Council of Jewish Communities (ECJC), working with Jewish communities across Europe on collaboration, education and community development. She has 15+ years of experience in international project management and community building working with organisations in more than 40 countries.

12004.name: Tasha Davis
12004.bio: Tasha is the UK representative for Tailor Made Birthright Israel, growing UK participation and building partnerships with communities and organisations. She manages madrichim (group leaders) recruitment and training, and the Recruiters Programme. She is involved in Jewish community work and is interested in how young adults explore Jewish identity.

11868.name: Daniel de Wijze
11868.bio: Daniel de Wijze is a civil servant working at Ofgem, the energy regulator for Great Britain. Since graduating with an MSc in Earth Science, he has worked in a variety of roles focusing on renewable energy. Alongside energy and climate, he has a particular interest in geography and geopolitics. Daniel lives with his wife in south London.

12034.name: Martin Di Maggio
12034.bio: Martin is a spiritual Humanistic rabbi of Anglo-Italian and Albanian heritage and is a sociolinguist specialising in endangered and minoritised languages. He has been studying towards semichah with Tzemah Yoreh, Frank Tamburelli and Jonathan Cohen, and focuses on Kaplan's religious humanism and Harold Schulweis' predicate theology.

11921.name: Noah Diamondstein
11921.bio: Noah Diamondstein is a senior rabbi and Jewish recording artist. He has served as artist/rabbi-in-residence and guest shaliach tzibur (prayer leader) at congregations and communities around the USA. Noah has been a featured educator/faculty member at Hava Nashira and SLBC Conference (formerly Songleader Boot Camp).

11936.name: Charlotte Disley
11936.bio: Charlotte Disley is a modern history PhD student at the University of St Andrews and a fellow at George Mason University. Her PhD examines the institutional history of the Heritage Foundation, focusing on social class, economic ideology, and welfare and healthcare policy. She holds degrees from King’s College London (BSc) and St Andrews (MLitt).

11811.name: Carmel du Parc Braham
11811.bio: Carmel is a London-based information professional. Originally a history and politics teacher, she later moved into the world of government in a bid to secure an invitation to the No. 10 Chanukah party. Reader, it worked.

11903.name: Josh Dubell
11903.bio: Education director at Solutions Not Sides, specialising in Israel-Palestine education, contested narratives and dialogue across difference. He designs curricula, facilitator training and school programmes that equip students to engage critically with conflict and is Limmud Festival's 2026 programming chair, shaping Jewish learning and debate.

11902.name: Robbie Duschinsky
11902.bio: Robbie Duschinsky is professor of Social Science and Health at Cambridge University. His research spans mental health, history, and social theory. He has won university awards for teaching, mentoring and the research culture of his team. He lives with Sophie Duschinsky and their two children.

11901.name: Sophie Duschinsky
11901.bio: Sophie is a clinical psychologist who specialises in working with neurodiversity across the lifespan. She enjoys creating a space for her clients to reflect on their strengths and values, and how they can use these to work towards their goals. She lives in London with her husband and two children.

12071.name: Anna Dyson
12071.bio: A future rabbi in Leeds, studying mainly remotely with the Academy for Jewish Religion, California. Interested in creating new Jewish spaces, interfaith dialogue, hosting difficult conversations, building community and self-development through Jewish sources. A social entrepreneur with an MSc in Jewish Organisational Leadership and Innovation.

12016.name: Samantha Ellis
12016.bio: Samantha Ellis’s book, 'Chopping Onions on my Heart', about her mother tongue, the language of Iraqi Jews, going extinct, was shortlisted for the Wingate Award. She’s also the author of 'How to be a Heroine' and 'Take Courage', and her plays include 'How to Date a Feminist'.

11962.name: Yaffa Epstein
11962.bio: Yaffa Epstein is senior scholar and educator in residence at the Jewish Education Project. She has taught for Wexner, Pardes, and across the spectrum of Jewish institutions and loves making Torah study accessible to all. A Limmud addict since her first conference in 2007, she has taught at over 100 Limmud events across five continents.

11978.name: Lilinaz Evans
11978.bio: Lilinaz was raised in south London, but her learning has taken her around the world: to Stockholm at Paideia, to Jerusalem at Nishmat, and then to New York, where she studies for rabbinic ordination at Yeshivat Maharat. She now serves as head of Jewish education and fellowships at Sadeh Farm. Lilinaz enjoys cooking for crowds and fibre crafts.

12047.name: Adina Fagelston
12047.bio: Adina Fagelston is an Israeli educator and Jewish Agency shlicha (emissary) at the United Jewish Israel Appeal in London. Israeli by nature, educator by choice, she has led experiential programmes on Jewish identity, Israel and peoplehood. She is passionate about creating meaningful encounters that spark dialogue, connection and belonging.

12195.name: Elias Faingersh
12195.bio: Known internationally as ‘The Orchestra Man’ and ‘The Golden Trombone of Europe’, Faingersh's theatrical work has earned many international distinctions, including the Grand Prix at the Reykjavík Fringe Festival and a 'Theater award' at the Edinburgh Festival Fringe (2026). His acclaimed production 'A Solo' also reached Off-Broadway in New York.

11941.name: The Limmud Family Team
11941.bio: The Limmud Families Team creates fun, creative and welcoming spaces where families can enjoy Limmud together. From making and playing to stories, adventures and sharing experiences together, there’s something for children and grown-ups of all ages. Sessions run outside of YTL (Young and Teen Limmud) and crèche hours.

12090.name: Nina Fefferman
12090.bio: Nina is a professor at Arizona State University and director of the US National Science Foundation Center for Analysis and Prediction of Pandemic Expansion. Her research is on the mathematics of complex adaptive systems, in evolutionary biology and infectious disease. She is especially interested in when self-interest aligns with the public good.

11963.name: Shimmy Feintuch
11963.bio: Shimmy Feintuch is a psychotherapist, educator, and speaker from New York City. His practice, Feintuch Counseling, focuses on addiction and couples counselling. He has taught at Yeshiva University's Wurzweiler School of Social Work and serves on the board of Jewish Queer Youth. He speaks on mindfulness, emotional wellness, and LGBTQ advocacy.

11872.name: Leon Fenster
11872.bio: Artist behind the nine-storey ‘London Jewish Mural’ at JW3. He has also illustrated a haggadah. He brings stories to life as kaleidoscopic artworks: from vast historical events to a couple's life as a ketubah (marriage contract). He previously built communities in Asia including chairing Limmud China and as chazan/para-rabbi of a Taiwan shul.

11935.name: Libi Fileman
11935.bio: Libi is growth manager for Birthright Israel at the United Jewish Israel Appeal, founding host of MHWOW in Leeds and a writer and entertainment editor for The Jewish Stand. An Adam Science Leadership Programme graduate and winner of the Magen David Adom Young Impact Award 2026, she is passionate about positive Jewish experiences for young people.

12145.name: UK Jewish Film
12145.bio: UK Jewish Film is dedicated to screening Jewish films that entertain, educate and enlighten diverse audiences in the UK and internationally. UK Jewish Film believes film has the power to cross cultures and unite audiences through the telling of cinematic stories that provide stimulating and unique views of Jewish and Israeli life and culture.

12077.name: Nathan Finkel
12077.bio: Nathan Finkel is a multi-instrumentalist and live performer whose work spans festivals, fires and jam sessions. This year he's turned aircraft radio signals into music and built visuals that are playable. A long-time Limmud house band member, he creates inclusive, improvisational spaces for musicians and audiences.

12080.name: David Finlay
12080.bio: David has researched, written about and performed different aspects of Jewish history and literature. He has a particular interest in the poetry of Yehuda Amichai and diaries written during the Shoah years.

11918.name: Charlotte Fischer
11918.bio: Charlotte Fischer is a community organiser who loves Jewish organisations – growing them, nurturing them, and helping them deliver to build the Jewish life we can only live together. She has helped communities build relationships across lines of difference and double their membership.

11816.name: Ellen Flax
11816.bio: Ellen Flax is a philanthropy specialist who currently supports the work of a graduate school of public health in New York City. She received her rabbinic ordination from Hebrew Union College-Jewish Institute of Religion and serves as the rabbi of several senior-care facilities.

11879.name: Yehudis Fletcher
11879.bio: Yehudis is the co-founder of Nahamu, a think tank that counters extremism in the Jewish community. She has a BSc in Social Policy, an MA in Religion and Theology and is undertaking a PhD examining theology as context for abuse. Her memoir, 'Chutzpah', was published by Penguin in 2025.

12066.name: Benjamin Forman
12066.bio: Ben Forman is a London-based technologist and genealogist. After 25+ years in live streaming, latterly as global head of live channels architecture at Amazon Prime Video, he now consults. He edits the journal 'Shemot', leads Jewish Records Indexing-Poland for Kaluszyn and built HistoryMapper, which maps Court Jews' networks.

12001.name: Niki Forman
12001.bio: Niki Forman is an American-Israeli living in Jerusalem. She works in recruiting and social media for Yahel, which runs volunteer and service-learning programmes across Israel, including a ten-month fellowship. She is also a classical musician, runs String Theory Jerusalem, and is a two-time Limmud Taskmaster winner.

11849.name: Marc Frank
11849.bio: Marc is a fully qualified Jewish mindfulness meditation teacher, practising Gestalt therapist, mental health support worker, and HaMakom UK's community manager. He lives and works in Totnes, Devon, where he also chairs Totnes Jewish Community and promotes regional interfaith initiatives as part of the Devon Faith and Belief Forum.

11947.name: Paul Freedman
11947.bio: Paul taught Physics before training for the rabbinate at Leo Baeck College, where he has taught Biblical Hebrew. He is senior rabbi at Hertfordshire Progressive Synagogue and has worked on liturgy for Liberal and Reform Judaism, including as final editor of the first British Reform haggadah and co-editor of its High Holy Days machzor (prayer book).

11948.name: Vanessa Freedman
11948.bio: Vanessa is Hebrew and Jewish Studies librarian at University College London, and was previously assistant librarian at Leo Baeck College. She is married to the senior rabbi of Hertfordshire Progressive Synagogue but is definitely not a rebbetzin! She has been to almost every Limmud since 1995.

11979.name: Sofia Freudenstein
11979.bio: Sofia graduated from Yeshivat Maharat in 2025 and recently completed her master’s degree in Jewish Philosophy at Yeshiva University’s Bernard Revel Graduate School. She is the director of Jewish life and learning for the Jewish Community of Helsinki, Finland. Sofia enjoys connecting with people, birdwatching, and playing the kantele (Finnish harp).

11821.name: Georgie Friend
11821.bio: Georgie is a violence against women and girls educator, working as senior training officer at Women's Aid England, teaching about domestic abuse and sexual violence. She is completing an MA in Understanding Domestic Abuse and Sexual Violence at Goldsmiths, University of London, and has worked, volunteered and been a trustee in Jewish organisations.

12203.name: Jonathan Frisher
12203.bio: Jonathan is a campaigner and sixth form student. At 13 he launched a campaign for better antisemitism education in the UK. His evidence helped shape the Bell Review. He now sits on the Department for Education’s Bell Review Implementation Group as its student member, is a special adviser to the Anne Frank Trust, and is involved with LJY-Netzer.

11976.name: Eva Frojmovic
11976.bio: Eva Frojmovic is a veteran Limmud presenter (always with pictures). Her day job is as an associate professor in art history and Jewish cultural history at the University of Leeds. In June 2027, she'll be co-hosting the British and Irish Association for Jewish Studies annual conference. So, next year in Leeds.

12192.name: Dean Furman
12192.bio: Dean Furman is a proud Jewish South African footballer and former captain of Bafana Bafana. After developing at Chelsea, he played for clubs including Rangers, Doncaster Rovers and SuperSport United, earning 58 caps. He now works as a player services executive at the Professional Footballers’ Association, supporting players off the pitch.

12041.name: The Limmud Fusion Programming Team
12041.bio: This year’s Fusion team, Jo Reuben and Dania Mann-Wineberg, have put together a selection of sessions that fuse different genres, activities and presenters. Expect weird and also wonderful, serious and also silly, shtick and also shtark (devout) – the possibilities are endless!

11955.name: Julia Gamarski-Hoyland
11955.bio: Originally from Brazil, Julia was indoctrinated at age 15 in a kiruv (outreach) setting. After leaving the Jewish world, she is now on a journey back to herself and a more authentic way of being Jewish. Julia is a student at Yashrut, paving her way to become a Jewish educator and sees it as her mission to encourage intellectual honesty in Judaism.

11870.name: Isaac Gantwerk Mayer
11870.bio: From a family of musicians, Isaac Gantwerk Mayer (he/ער/איהו) believes that creative art is one of the most powerful ways to get in touch with the divine. He composes music and piyyuṭim in Hebrew, Aramaic, and English. He is most well-known for his yearly Purim Torah 'meme megillah' videos on YouTube. He lives in Jerusalem.

11906.name: Eli Gaventa
11906.bio: Eli Gaventa works at the United Jewish Israel Appeal, exploring how young Jews can build their own relationship with Israel and discover new (and old) meanings of Zionism. He spends an unreasonable amount of time thinking about how we reinterpret Jewish texts and has read over 30 million words of Harry Potter fanfiction. These facts may be related.

12046.name: Konstanty Gebert
12046.bio: Polish journalist, underground in the 80s. Co-founder of the dissident Jewish Flying University (1979), the Polish Council of Christians and Jews (1989), the Jewish monthly 'Midrasz' (1997). 1989–2022 at ‘Gazeta Wyborcza’, Poland’s biggest daily. Currently at kulturaliberalna.pl. Author of a dozen books on Polish, Israeli and European history.

12039.name: Nick Gendler
12039.bio: In no particular order, Nick is a professional psychotherapist, a keen double bass player, a doting grandfather and a competent cyclist.

12042.name: Amit Georgi
12042.bio: Amit is the Jewish Agency Israel fellow at the Union of Jewish Students. Originally from Tel Aviv, Amit holds an MA from the Hebrew University. Studying in Birmingham inspired Amit to become a shlicha (emissary) for UK students. Amit is passionate about creating open spaces for students to connect with Israel and supporting Israelis on campus.

12198.name: Anna Gerrard
12198.bio: Anna Gerrard is rabbi of Three Counties Liberal Jewish Community and runs the Tefillateinu programme for the Movement for Progressive Judaism. Anna previously worked as outreach director for Liberal Judaism and Jewish chaplain for Clifton College in Bristol. She is passionate about community development and intergenerational programming.

12125.name: Khalid Ghanayim
12125.bio: Khalid Ghanayim is a media professional, educator and activist advancing Arab–Jewish partnership in Israel. As co-director of Seeds of Partnership, he develops and leads programmes for Arab and Jewish young adults, supports social initiatives and facilitates discussions on society, media and politics. He is a former chair of Sada for Social Change.

11813.name: Paul Ginsberg
11813.bio: Paul is a Glasgow-based community builder and ADHD life coach certified by the International Coaching Federation. His passion is unlocking potential. He helps ADHDers work with themselves more constructively and improve self-understanding, at work and in other areas of life. He also blogs about ADHD.

12059.name: Dyonna Ginsburg
12059.bio: Dyonna is CEO of OLAM, a global Jewish network advancing service, international development, and humanitarian aid. OLAM’s 82 partners work in 117 countries. A frequent lecturer, she has held leadership roles in Israeli social action and Jewish education NGOs. She holds degrees from Columbia and the Hebrew University.

11965.name: Micah Gold
11965.bio: Micah Gold has long contributed to Limmud as a space for bold ideas. He leads Mobilise Public, a consultancy driving community-led change across charities, housing and local government. He co-founded Kavanah, a Jewish space for psychedelic integration and spirituality, and holds a Certificate in Psychedelic Practice.

11974.name: Sasha Gold
11974.bio: Sasha is a facilitator and organisational consultant who spends her professional life creating experiences that bring groups of people together to collaborate on complex challenges. She is also part of Limmud's Executive, working on volunteer experience. She lives in north London with her partner and daughter after a formative decade in Israel.

12031.name: Melanie Goldberg
12031.bio: Having been volunteering at Limmud since 2019, Melanie is a participant care co-chair for this year's festival. She is passionate about combining her Scottish and Jewish heritage at her popular annual Limmud ceilidh! A regular at Jewish events in Scotland, she also loves the outdoors and works for a conservation charity.

12005.name: Sophie Goldblum
12005.bio: Sophie Goldblum is lecturer and programme director at Paideia, the European Institute for Jewish Studies. She holds an MA in Political Theory and an MA in Jewish Studies from the Hebrew University. She has learned Torah at Pardes, Hadar, Drisha, and Maharat. She is the chief editor of 'Daï', a progressive French Jewish journal.

12106.name: Jonathan Golden
12106.bio: Jonathan Golden is senior educator at OpenDor Media. He teaches at Hebrew College and founded HeartStance Education Consulting. He is also a fellow at the Center for Jewish Peoplehood Education. From 1999 to 2023, he taught at Gann Academy, a pluralistic Jewish high school in Waltham, MA and served as the school’s Israel curriculum coordinator.

11945.name: Daniel Goldfarb
11945.bio: This is Daniel's 25th Limmud. Yikes! Daniel Goldfarb was born in Boston; all the rest is commentary (lawyer/rabbi/teacher, Jerusalem resident since 1976; former director of the Conservative Yeshiva). He finds teaching at Limmud an annual privilege. And fun, too.

12143.name: Nicky Goldman
12143.bio: Nicky is CEO of the Jewish Volunteering Network, with over 40 years’ experience in Jewish community leadership. As a volunteer, she co-leads services at Jewish Care’s Sandringham campus, is an executive member of the Alliance of Jewish Women and their Organisations and a trustee of the Directory of Social Change and the Diamond Charitable Trust.

11884.name: Sam Goldstone-Brady
11884.bio: Samuel Goldstone-Brady is the curator of Manchester Jewish Museum, joining the team in January 2026. Previously, he has worked for the National Paralympic Heritage Trust, and completed a PhD in the history of sport wheelchair technology at the University of Glasgow. He is also a co-founder of the UK Disability History and Heritage Hub.

12175.name: Cécile-Bruriah Goncalves
12175.bio: Cécile-Bruriah Goncalves holds a PhD in Political Studies from the École des Hautes Études en Sciences Sociales and has taught at French universities. After studying at Pardes and the Conservative Yeshiva, she is now a rabbinical student. She reads Torah through disability, using feminist and halachic thought to confront exclusion and violence.

11890.name: Sophie Goorwich
11890.bio: Sophie Goorwich is the UK manager for Masa, connecting young Jewish people with meaningful experiences in Israel. After a decade running her own fitness business, Sophie took an unexpected turn into Jewish communal life. Her journey has left her curious about how Judaism, our values and the people we meet can shape the careers, and lives, we build.

12112.name: Daniel Gordon
12112.bio: Daniel A. Gordon is a historian of contemporary France, an associate member of the History Faculty at Oxford University and a fellow of the Royal Historical Society. His blog posts about previous French elections are the most-read pieces in the history of the French History Network Blog.

11891.name: Rivka Gottlieb
11891.bio: Rivka is a music psychotherapist/couples therapist in private practice working with adults and teens, with experience in schools, charities and the NHS. She’s developing the Shema Koleinu prayer skills website for Masorti Judaism and serves on the board of Covid-19 Bereaved Families for Justice UK, part of the Hillsborough Law Now coalition.

11889.name: Ayala Gottlieb Alter
11889.bio: Ayala is a singer, cellist, composer, Jewish educator and cantorial student at the Jewish Theological Seminary. After a year as cantor at the Great Synagogue of Stockholm, she studied at the Fuchsberg Jerusalem Centre Yeshiva before moving to New York to continue her training. She lends her voice to Masorti's Shema Koleinu tefillah skills resource.

12033.name: Sarah Grabiner
12033.bio: Sarah is a cantor and aspiring academic. While writing her PhD thesis at University College London on 'Prayer Book Jewish English', she works as a cantor across progressive communities in north London and teaches liturgy at Leo Baeck College.

12135.name: Avi Grant
12135.bio: Avi Grant is a filmmaker and freelance content creator. Avi is a member of Limmud's year-round Marketing Team, producing video content for social media.

11907.name: Natalie Grazin
11907.bio: Natalie is a former Limmud trustee, a serial charity start-upper and an avid Radio 4 listener. She has two teenagers with her partner Samantha, who she met at Limmud 25 years ago. Professionally, she is a coach and consultant, working with NHS organisations and Jewish charities and leaders on strategy, impact, change and development.

11855.name: Michael Green
11855.bio: Mike is inspired by how wild mushrooms and plants connect us with nature and our Jewish traditions. He founded the London Fungus Network to connect people with the urban fungal kingdom and is a ranger with London National Park City, an initiative that aims to make the city a wilder, greener – and more mushroomy – place.

12052.name: Reza Green
12052.bio: Reza Green reads Torah at egalitarian kehillot (communities) in Jerusalem, applying the graphical method of textual analysis she learned decades ago from Mechel Perlman. Whenever she has shared it with others, she's greatly enjoyed witnessing the ensuing 'light-bulb' moments. When not leyning, she practises law, science, photography, and quilting.

12116.name: Joanne Greenaway
12116.bio: Joanne Greenaway is a rabbanit (female Orthodox leader), writer, teacher, Sacks scholar and former London School of Jewish Studies CEO. She holds a halacha qualification from Midreshet Lindenbaum, hosts the Women’s Gallery podcast, is doing a PhD and finishing a book on get (Jewish divorce) refusal. She loves good questions and diverse voices.

11938.name: Alexandra Grisanti
11938.bio: Alexandra Grisanti is a strategist, entrepreneur and community builder working at the intersection of technology, business and people. She helps organisations turn ideas, networks and emerging technology into practical opportunities. At Limmud, she’ll explore how ChatGPT could help your synagogue unlock £50,000 in new value.

12122.name: Batsheva Haber
12122.bio: Batsheva is head of educational experiences at the United Jewish Israel Appeal. With over ten years’ experience in education, she specialises in Israel education, ed-tech and experiential learning. She has worked in consulting, at Teach First Israel, as ed-tech specialist at Mekif Gilo, on staff at Camp Moshava and at Appleseed.

12076.name: Jude Habib
12076.bio: Jude is a former BBC producer and charity director. She spent 20 years supporting marginalised communities to develop skills to influence public conversations. She now runs meet-ups for Jewish professionals to feel supported in the workplace, to share experiences so they don't feel alone, something she wishes she’d had access to after 7 October.

11913.name: Lara Haft Yom-Tov
11913.bio: Lara Haft Yom-Tov is a rabbi at New North London Synagogue. Originally from Washington, D.C., Lara received semichah from Beit Midrash Har’el and has studied at Pardes, Drisha, Hebrew College, and SVARA. They love connecting Jewish texts to the pressing questions of our times and teaching Talmud to people of all ages.

11875.name: Caroline Hagard
11875.bio: Caroline teaches Gan (kindergarten) at The Liberal Jewish Synagogue and Edgware and Hendon Reform Synagogue religion schools. She is a storyteller, writes Jewish songs for young children and writes/runs children's services for the High Holy Days/chagim (festivals). She is passionate about Judaism and her sessions are great fun.

12181.name: Daphna Haran
12181.bio: Daphna Haran is an educator at the Leo Baeck Education Center in Haifa and an expert in gifted and talented education and in teachers' professional development. For three years, with two rabbis, Ofek Meir and Oshrat Morag, she has led a beit midrash (house of study) for teachers, in which pedagogical questions are explored through Jewish texts.

12150.name: Nirit Harel
12150.bio: Nirit Harel founded Impact Manhattan/TLV/Portugal, bridging Israeli, US and Portuguese innovation. With 25+ years in global ventures, she was chief marketing officer of the Jewish Agency and CEO of Maccabi World Union North America. She also heads the Coimbra Jewish community, revived after 500 years of dormancy since the Inquisition.

11985.name: Paul Harris
11985.bio: Senior partner at criminal defence firm Edward Fail Bradshaw and Waterson having acted in many high-profile cases including Post Office appeals, Hillsborough and acting for numerous Jewish counter-protesters. Masorti Judaism trustee and Board of Deputies deputy for Masorti Judaism. Member of New North London Synagogue, father to Ava, Grace and BZ.

12205.name: Zev Harvey
12205.bio: Zev Harvey is a professor emeritus in the Department of Jewish Thought at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem, where he has taught since 1977. He is the author of many studies on medieval and modern Jewish philosophers, like Maimonides, Crescas and Spinoza. He is an EMET Prize laureate in the humanities (2009).

12000.name: Ariel Heller
12000.bio: Ariel Heller (he/they) is chair of Keshet Europe, the European network of Jewish queer individuals and organisations. A graphic designer, they have worked with Roma Pride and Jewish organisations, and developed Booking.com’s Proud Hospitality training on LGBTQIA+ inclusion.

11896.name: Vanessa Hidary
11896.bio: Vanessa Hidary is a spoken word artist, writer, educator and facilitator exploring Jewish identity, Zionism, antisemitism and belonging. A native New Yorker of Ashkenazi and Syrian Jewish heritage, she has performed on HBO’s Def Poetry and stages worldwide, using storytelling to challenge assumptions and amplify diverse Jewish voices.

11994.name: Michael Hilton
11994.bio: Veteran Limmudnik Michael Hilton worked as a congregational rabbi for 30 years, and has recently completed a book (not yet published) about the impact of Islam on Judaism over the centuries. The initial research was presented as a course ‘Judaism and Islam: A Shared History’ with Islamic scholar Harith Ramli.

12025.name: Kati Hoffmann
12025.bio: Kati is an ICU nurse and humanitarian aid worker, finishing her PhD in Global Mental Health at King's College London. Her research centres Ethiopian women's own accounts of resilience and coping with trauma in Addis Ababa through a decolonial, feminist, strengths-based lens. Next, she heads to Iraq as a Civil Peace Service advisor.

12013.name: Delphine Horvilleur
12013.bio: Delphine is a prominent figure in the realms of Jewish culture and religion and the author of several best-sellers. She was a rabbi of the Liberal Jewish Movement of France in Paris until 2026, and is the director of Tenoua, an independent online magazine and platform for Jewish thought. Since 2018, she has led the Tenoua study workshops.

12070.name: The Limmud House Band
12070.bio: The Limmud House Band is back for another year of music-making. Backing guest musicians from around the world, they’ll move effortlessly between folk, funk, pop, rock and jazz and of course the occasional niggun. Versatile, enthusiastic and chronically short of sleep, the House Band is your ever-present guide through Limmud.

11883.name: Robin Howard
11883.bio: Robin Howard is a senior physician based in London. He has extensive experience in treating neurological disability and a keen interest in the history of the neurosciences. He is a regular Limmudnik.

12081.name: Ernie Hunter
12081.bio: Ernie is second generation (a child of survivors) and a volunteer educator in the UK and Germany. He chairs the Northern Holocaust Education Group and is an accredited speaker for it and Generation 2 Generation. He is a member of the Education Advisory Group of the Manchester Jewish Representative Council. His best job? Being a grandpa!

11831.name: Jonathan Hunter
11831.bio: When not at Limmud events, Jonathan spends much of his leisure time at various modern jive dance events around the country, and is very much looking forward to sharing the joy of partner dancing again with all at Limmud Festival this year!

12120.name: Ilana Hutchinson
12120.bio: Ilana is the co-director of outreach and prevention at Jewish Women’s Aid, working with the whole Jewish community to reshape attitudes and challenge norms around domestic abuse and sexual violence. With over 30 years’ experience in education, Ilana is passionate about empowering young people to be positive drivers of change.

11905.name: Rivka Isaacson
11905.bio: Rivka is professor of Molecular Biophysics at King's College London. She grew up in the frum (Orthodox) community of Broughton Park and loves poetry, fiction and theatre. She gave the Royal Institution Christmas Lectures and writes for the Independent and Financial Times. Her husband is Nick Blain; their kids are lifelong Limmudniks so far.

11836.name: Judith Ish-Horowicz
11836.bio: Judith’s belief in the power of bringing generations together led her to open Apples and Honey Nightingale, the UK's first co-located nursery in a care home, to develop accredited training in intergenerational (IG) practice and to found Gen-All, England’s grassroots IG network. Her Judaism unlocked the spiritual power of IG relationships.

12027.name: Margaret Jacobi
12027.bio: Margaret Jacobi is the rabbi emerita of Birmingham Progressive Synagogue. Blessed by Lily Montagu as a baby, she was inspired by her passion for social justice. Margaret originally studied medicine, has PhDs in Physiology and Talmud and is now a magistrate. In her spare time she loves making music.

12199.name: Zoe Jacobs
12199.bio: Zoe Jacobs is a cantor and advocate for innovation in liturgical music. She was ordained at Hebrew Union College's Debbie Friedman School of Sacred Music, becoming Reform Judaism’s first ordained cantor. She leads the clergy team at Finchley Reform Synagogue and founded the biennial Shirei Chagigah conference to help others lead music and prayer.

11852.name: Nicole Jacobus
11852.bio: Nicole is an event producer and enthusiasm enthusiast from London. Stop her in the corridor anytime to talk about escape rooms, lino printing, or to arrange a chavruta in the bar. She will be co-chair of Limmud Festival 2027 along with Harry Lampert.

11998.name: Shoshana Jakobovits
11998.bio: Shoshana often says she has three lives: she is a Torah learner (graduate of Yeshivat Maharat), a software engineer at Google DeepMind, and a spouse and mother. Does she have a better command of Aramaic, Python, Swiss-German or baby language? It depends when you ask. What is consistent, however, is her love of texts, people and where the two meet.

12110.name: Lia Joffe
12110.bio: Lia is a youth worker, theatre maker and aspiring historian. She was a Noam movement worker, and currently lives in Moishe House Finsbury Park, but she does have non-Jewish friends.

12157.name: Sacha Johnstone
12157.bio: Sacha is a professional magician and mentalist with more than 15 years of experience performing at corporate and private events across the UK and worldwide. A trusted choice for leading blue-chip companies, he has entertained sports personalities and Hollywood stars. He is also a firm favourite at communal events and on the London simcha circuit.

12139.name: Leah Greenwald Jordan
12139.bio: Leah (she/they) is rabbi of Kehillah North London. Studied in the Pardes and SVARA kollels; sits on the advisory committee of the Center for Jewish Nonviolence (Jewish-Palestinian co-resistance). Enjoys speculative and fan fiction. Lives in Maida Hill with partner Benji Stanley, Azara’s director of learning, and children Jules and Marlowe.

12097.name: Mark Joseph
12097.bio: Mark was born in 1959 in Paignton, Devon, and grew up in Plymouth. He studied Philosophy, Politics and Economics at Balliol College, Oxford, and took up saxophone. He moved to Israel in 2000 and is an editor and translator. He found Jewish pathways and psychoanalysis in his 30s. He has just left Israel, for now, and is learning Palestinian Arabic.

12065.name: Itai Kagan
12065.bio: Itai Kagan is the Kennicott Fellow in Hebrew Studies at the University of Oxford, following completion of a PhD at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem. He is a philologist interested in the transformation of Jewish texts and languages from the Bible to the Middle Ages, give or take a millennium.

12064.name: Judith Kagan
12064.bio: Judith Kagan is a Hebrew fantasy writer, weaving magical strands from the Talmud, archaeology and Jewish folklore. Her bestselling novels 'Harashta' (2024) and 'Shagrirut HaSheidim' (2025) were selected for Israel's national school reading programme. Judith worked at the National Library of Israel, which she represents at this year's Limmud.

12178.name: Alexander Kahn
12178.bio: Alex is a painter at the Charles H. Cecil Studios in Florence. He studies literature, with a particular interest in Yiddish literature.

12036.name: Keith Kahn-Harris
12036.bio: Keith Kahn-Harris is a sociologist and writer. He is a senior lecturer at Leo Baeck College and a senior research fellow at the Institute for Jewish Policy Research. The author of nine books, he has published widely on Jewish issues, antisemitism, heavy metal, the warning messages inside Kinder Surprise Eggs, and much else besides.

11874.name: Jenny Kananov Shayo
11874.bio: Jenny has a background in educational and organisational psychology and previously founded a social impact start-up. She has been involved in activism and community organising and now works at Yachad, a British-Jewish organisation empowering the British-Jewish community to support a diplomatic resolution to the Israeli-Palestinian conflict.

12169.name: Slavyan Kanovski
12169.bio: Slavyan Kanovski is a Sofia tour guide who works with Bulgaria’s Jewish community. He teaches Israeli dance and organises SoDa – Sofia Dance. He loves Limmud and sharing the remarkable story of Bulgarian Jewry and its beautiful Sephardi heritage. Be sure to ask him about it when you see him!

12129.name: Elliott Karstadt
12129.bio: Elliott Karstadt is part of the clergy team at Alyth Synagogue in London. He is passionate about Jewish education at all levels, and in 2024 he launched 'All Else is Commentary: A Podcast of Jewish Ideas', which has now published over 100 episodes, covering Jewish texts from the Bible to the present day.

12174.name: Emily Kasriel
12174.bio: Emily wrote 'Deep Listening', developing the approach at King’s College London and the London School of Economics and Political Science. She led the BBC/British Council Crossing Divides project, bringing Deep Listening to 1,000+ young people from 119 countries, and has trained everyone from executives to communities in conflict.

11815.name: Noah Katz
11815.bio: Noah is the Board of Deputies’ workplace and inclusion officer, covering the workplace, health, universities and Commission on Disability Inclusion. They are the co-founder of the Yad Fellowship, a Jewish-Muslim student leadership incubator with UK government funding. In 2023, Noah was elected the youngest chair of a Jewish community in the world.

11830.name: Andrea Kelmanson
11830.bio: Andrea has always worked with charities. After 20 years running volunteering programmes for young people, she was deputy director of the National AIDS Trust; after that she was CEO of the National Centre for Volunteering. For the past 35 years she has been working as a voluntary sector management consultant.

11861.name: Maureen Kendal
11861.bio: Maureen Kendal is an artist, author, producer and director of dreamstudio.io and Cecile Elstein Studio Ltd. Current projects: framework for artists’ oeuvres, catalogues raisonnés for artists and artist collectives. Publications on virtual worlds, cyber-selves, artists and art practice.

12040.name: Clive Kennard
12040.bio: Clive is a second-year student at Leo Baeck College. His doctorate focussed on Simeon Solomon, a gay Victorian Jewish artist. He is learning the classical rabbinic elements of Jewish studies – with a view to merging rabbinic training with the Victorian receptions of Jewish antiquity.

12095.name: Adriana Kertzer
12095.bio: Adriana Kertzer is a cultural producer, lawyer, and advocate for psychedelic medicine in contemporary Jewish culture. She founded the Jewish Healing Society, which fosters a supportive environment for Jews in psychedelic science, and has been building Jewish psychedelic community since 2016 as a connector, organiser, and risk reduction advocate.

11856.name: David Kinshuck
11856.bio: Retired, David is slowly learning to draw and paint. He would particularly like to use art to illustrate social and environmental concerns.

12012.name: Joshua Koonin
12012.bio: Josh Koonin is an Israeli political analyst and founder of IPCS Travel Group. Raised in Sydney, he worked for Australian politicians before making aliyah in 2016. He designs geopolitical tours for politicians, diplomats, influencers, student leaders and journalists from leading organisations such as CNN and writes extensively about Israeli affairs.

12144.name: Miriam Kunin
12144.bio: Mim is a Talmud enthusiast from Leeds, living and working in Oxford. Mim has studied at Drisha, Hadar, Pardes, the Conservative Yeshiva, Yashrut and Azara, and participated in Svara's teshuva writing collective. In hir spare time, Mim can be found swimming in rivers, singing folksongs or having long conversations about religion and/or disability.

12021.name: Yahala Lachmish
12021.bio: Yahala, a Jerusalem Academy of Music and Dance graduate, is a paytanit (singer of liturgical poetry), cantor and composer. She performs solo, with her ensemble Tandu and with Israeli orchestras. She leads prayer and is musical director at Kehilat Zion, teaches at Schechter Institute, Mabua and Hebrew Union College, and is paytanit at Project 929.

11814.name: Harry Lampert
11814.bio: Harry is a podcast, TV and radio producer specialising in science. He’s produced content for channels and organisations around the world and will talk to anyone about anything – especially science, woodworking and cooking. Heston Blumenthal called a cake Harry made ‘heavy’. He will be co-chair of Limmud Festival 2027 along with Nicole Jacobus.

11933.name: Juliet Landau-Pope
11933.bio: Juliet is an International Coaching Federation Professional Certified Coach, author and productivity expert with an academic teaching background and specialist training in ADHD and chronic disorganisation. She coaches students and adults to develop executive functioning skills and leads time management workshops in corporate and community settings.

11842.name: Robin Lansman
11842.bio: Robin Lansman: osteopath, past president of the Institute of Osteopathy. 3rd-generation survivor; 1988 March of the Living pioneer. Interfaith singer, JW3 Generation X committee. Frankl-inspired.

11992.name: Clive Lawton
11992.bio: Clive co-founded Limmud and helped spread it globally. He was a high school head, Liverpool's education director, CEO of Chief Rabbi Sacks' 'Jewish Continuity' and of the Commonwealth Jewish Council, now its executive chair. He founded children's Holocaust education and was a magistrate, hospital board chair and Metropolitan Police governor.

11876.name: Samuel Lebens
11876.bio: Samuel Lebens is a professor of Philosophy at the University of Haifa and an Orthodox rabbi. He has written six books and many articles, on topics from Bertrand Russell to the Hasidic masters. Born in England, he lives in Netanya with his wife and three children. His sessions are dedicated in loving memory of Shaul Berkowitz z"l.

12184.name: Claire Lemer
12184.bio: Claire Lemer is a general paediatrician. She volunteers for a number of community charities. Teaching her dad to cook has been hugely rewarding and fun.

12078.name: The Leo Baeck Education Center Haifa
12078.bio: A group of students are representing the Leo Baeck Education Center (LBEC) in Haifa at Limmud Festival. LBEC is a leading school in Israel both academically and in its contribution to the community. The school proudly emphasises the values of Liberal Judaism, Zionism, democracy, social justice, tikkun olam, religious freedom and equality.

11973.name: Luke Levine
11973.bio: Luke Levine (he/they) is director of programmes at KeshetUK, working to create more inclusive Jewish communities for LGBT+ people. He has over a decade of experience in Jewish youth and community organisations and is passionate about belonging, inclusive practice and the intersections of LGBT+ and Jewish identity.

11825.name: Charlie Lewin
11825.bio: Charlie (they/them) is a multifaceted visual artist based in London, UK. They have studied Songwriting (BA) and Fine Art (BA) and completed a master's in Children’s Book Illustration and Graphic Novels. Charlie is currently working on their first graphic novel about their life growing up in an insular ultra-Orthodox Hasidic/Charedi community.

11968.name: Bracha Lieberman
11968.bio: Bracha Lieberman is a career counsellor. Bracha runs innovative, community-based mental health programmes and writes poems and ideas on parshah. Bracha likes songwriting and acting and thinks community counts. Start your day off with an act of kindness!

12108.name: Stuart Linke
12108.bio: Stuart is an NHS consultant clinical psychologist, researcher at University College London and advisor to Wellspring and Jami (Jewish Association for Mental Illness). He belongs to Ruach Chavurah and Finchley Reform Synagogue, and studied with Zalman Schachter-Shalomi z"l. He wrote 'Psychological Perspectives on Traditional Jewish Practices'.

11819.name: Asher Lovy
11819.bio: Asher is an abuse survivor and director of ZA'AKAH, which advocates for survivors of sexual violence in the Jewish community. He was raised in Boro Park and has taken a long journey to get not very far from home. When he's not in court reporting on sexual violence cases you can find Asher in the kitchen cooking for Shabbat.

12161.name: Daniel Mackintosh
12161.bio: South African and south London Jew, community organiser and institution builder. Dad of three lovely small people, partner to Charlotte, loves text and being challenged and believes in building Jewish life in the UK.

12032.name: Ilia Mainshlos
12032.bio: Ilia Mainshlos is an educator and Jewish history researcher based in Israel. At ANU – Museum of the Jewish People, he develops educational content, leads ConnectEd – the Jewish global educator network, and co-leads Identity Works, a fellowship for Jewish educators in Europe. His work focuses on Jewish peoplehood, identity, and memory.

11824.name: Robin Makin
11824.bio: Robin Makin is a regular Limmudnik. He produced Liverpool Old Hebrew Congregation’s six-month sesquicentennial Heritage Season, which ran from September 2024 to February 2025. In 2026 he organised the Jewish Culture Month concert at Princes Road Synagogue, celebrating Jewish religious and secular music.

11911.name: Claire Mandel
11911.bio: Claire Mandel leads strategic programmes at the Jewish Leadership Council, bringing people, organisations and ideas together to strengthen Jewish life across the UK. Previously CEO of New North London Synagogue, she has also held a variety of leadership roles within Limmud and is passionate about community innovation and engagement.

11944.name: Dagmara Manka-Wizor
11944.bio: Dagmara Mańka-Wizor works at the POLIN Museum in Warsaw. She brings Jewish history and culture to a wide audience, and leads anti-discrimination training for professionals. She is also a member of the Warsaw Jewish Community and the Renaissance HUB for Jewish Education. Privately, she is a sports freak and a hopeless fan of FC Polonia Warszawa.

12111.name: Ayana Maor Haver
12111.bio: Ayana Maor Haver is a social worker with a BA in Philosophy and Jewish Thought and an MA in Social Work. She has worked in therapy, education, healthy sexuality and community work. She is interested in the ways Jewish ideas meet everyday life, and in questions of identity, choice, relationships and meaning.

11967.name: Annette Margolis
11967.bio: Annette is a semi-retired mathematics and academic English teacher. She runs the monthly Italian conversation class at Cartlands Tea Room, Kings Heath, Birmingham.

12147.name: Maurice Markham
12147.bio: Maurice is a Limmud regular who is slightly too intrigued by how and why people think and feel the way they do. Now retired, his professional career was as a learning and development consultant, and a group facilitator. He's a parent of three and grandparent of two and a half so things haven't really changed since!

11910.name: Olivia Marks-Woldman
11910.bio: Olivia is the chief executive of the Holocaust Memorial Day Trust and vice chair of Kids, a charity for disabled young people and their families. She has three (young adult) children, including one with learning disabilities, one cat and one dog. She can occasionally be spotted at a Parkrun.

12017.name: Michael Marmot
12017.bio: Michael Marmot is one of the most influential figures in global public health. Professor of Epidemiology at University College London since 1985 and director of its Institute of Health Equity, he chaired the WHO Commission on Social Determinants of Health, led the landmark Marmot Reviews, and holds more than twenty honorary doctorates.

11920.name: Michael Marmur
11920.bio: Michael Marmur is professor of Jewish Theology, Hebrew Union College (HUC) – Jerusalem. Born in Britain, Michael has lived in Israel since 1984. He was previously dean of HUC in Jerusalem, provost of HUC, and chair of Rabbis for Human Rights. In 2025, 'Living the Letters: An Alphabet of Emerging Jewish Thought' was published by Palgrave Macmillan.

11996.name: Dmitry Maryasis
11996.bio: Since his repatriation to Israel in 2022, Dmitry Maryasis has worked at ANU – Museum of the Jewish People, coordinating educational projects for Russian-speaking Jewish communities. From 2007 to 2017, he headed the programme committee of Limmud Moscow. He is a former head of Israel and Jewish Communities Studies at the Russian Academy of Sciences.

12210.name: David Mason
12210.bio: Rabbi David Mason is executive director of the Jewish refugee charity HIAS+JCORE and a Sacks Scholar. His thinking connects Jewish ideas and scholarship to social responsibility. He was previously rabbi of two London synagogues. He studied Conflict Resolution at King’s College London and has expertise in interfaith work and social cohesion.

11970.name: Tamar Meir
11970.bio: Tamar Meir is head of Literature at Givat Washington College, specialising in midrash, piyyut (liturgical poetry) and Hasidic tales. She is an award-winning children's author ('Francesco Tirelli’s Ice Cream Shop'), poet and editor. She is on the board of Beit Hillel (an Orthodox rabbinic organisation) and founded the 'Kulana' Women's Beit Midrash.

11984.name: Simon Mendes
11984.bio: Simon Mendes is a New York-based director and producer. His debut 'The Darkest Light' won the inaugural Best First Feature Award at the 2026 San Francisco Jewish Film Festival. He co-produced 'Sabbath Queen' and was associate producer on the Oscar-shortlisted 'Dick Johnson Is Dead' and 'Becoming'. He is now producing 'Alliance'.

11859.name: Helena Miller
11859.bio: Helena is director of postgraduate degrees and senior research fellow at the London School of Jewish Studies. She has led, taught, researched and written widely. She runs the Jewish Lives longitudinal study in the UK. Helena co-chaired Limmud International 2009–12 and is an editor of the 'Journal of Jewish Education'.

11860.name: Steve Miller
11860.bio: Educator and facilitator with 40+ years at Limmud and worldwide. Steve sparks curiosity, asks bold questions, and seeks to uncover patterns of meaning across diverse topics including social justice, history, art, and spirituality. Professionally he builds cross-sector partnerships to create resilient and thriving communities across London.

11834.name: Joe Millis
11834.bio: 'Welcome back my friends to the show that never ends, I’m so glad you could attend, come inside, come inside…' Joe Millis is a supporter of lost causes – Tottenham Hotspur, Dulwich Hamlet, Israel-Palestine peace – a sceptic and a cynic. He has been there, done that, and has several T-shirts and scars to prove it.

12074.name: Carly Minsky
12074.bio: Carly is a writer with a background in academic philosophy and a passion for exploring new ways to engage with Jewish heritage and identity. She co-founded the Jewish Non-Parent Network in 2026 to build a community for Jewish people who do not have children, and to advocate for better inclusion in Jewish life for this underserved demographic.

12014.name: Shira Mirvis
12014.bio: Shira Marili Mirvis is the community rabbanit of Kehilat Shirat HaTamar in Efrat and CEO of the Honey Foundation in Israel. She works to strengthen women’s religious and communal leadership and serves as a casualty notification and intelligence officer in the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) reserves. Her sessions are dedicated in loving memory of Brenda and Russell Smith z"l.

12079.name: Oshrat Morag
12079.bio: Oshrat Morag is senior rabbi of the Leo Baeck Education Center in Haifa, overseeing the religious and spiritual life of 2,400 students from pre-kindergarten to 18, including those with special needs. Born in Haifa, she previously held rabbinic posts in Cincinnati, Ohio, where she pursued her PhD in Feminist Theology, and in Buenos Aires, Argentina.

12075.name: Joshua Moritz
12075.bio: Josh is a psychotherapist working in private practice. He previously worked as a youth and community worker in the Jewish community for over a decade. He co-founded the Jewish Non-Parent Network to build a community for Jewish people who do not have children, and to advocate for better inclusion in Jewish life for this underserved demographic.

11987.name: Abigail Morris
11987.bio: Abigail Morris is a keen – and chatty – runner. She has previously been the director of the Jewish Museum and artistic director of Soho Theatre. (She recently directed a show there with Maureen Lipman which caused a bit of a fuss!) She is a member of Finchley Reform and has been coming, with her family, to Limmud for the last 27 years.

12202.name: Benny Morris
12202.bio: Born in Israel in 1948, Benny Morris grew up in Jerusalem and New York. He served in the IDF (Nahal paratroops), studied at the Hebrew University and Cambridge, and was a professor at Ben-Gurion University. His books include 'Righteous Victims' (Knopf, 1999) and '1948: A History of the First Arab-Israeli War' (Yale University Press, 2008).

12130.name: Gaby Morris
12130.bio: Gaby Morris is a trustee of the Jewish Square Mile Foundation, dedicated to exploring London’s medieval Jewish community. She co-founded Greyscape, highlighting brutalist, modernist, and constructivist architecture, and has researched and written numerous oral history projects. She is a founder of Riverside Training Company.

12131.name: Howard Morris
12131.bio: Howard Morris chairs the Jewish Square Mile Foundation, uncovering the story of medieval London’s Jews, their contribution to the City and the journey from expulsion to civic inclusion, while exploding myths that persist today. With his wife Gaby, he founded Greyscape, a global modernist architecture platform. He is a lawyer, mediator and writer.

12183.name: Nina Morris-Evans
12183.bio: Nina's tagline is 'there's no one keener than Nina'. Whether co-chairing Limmud's Young Leaders Programme, working as head of sixth form in a London comprehensive, or winning the triathlon world championships this year, Nina is nothing if not enthusiastic. She’s also involved with V'Ahavta, a network of UK Jews countering the far right.

11835.name: Robin Moss
11835.bio: Robin is chief executive of Unitas Youth Zone, an amazing youth centre in Burnt Oak with more than 50,000 visits a year. He is also a Jewish and Israel educator. He has presented at Limmud events on five continents and invitations to South America and/or Antarctica are welcome. He is also chair of KeshetUK and a trustee of the Jewish Youth Fund.

11993.name: Naomi Munk
11993.bio: Naomi Munk (née Webber) is a lifelong Limmudnik and barrister specialising in employment, education and discrimination law. She has a particular interest in issues where religious practice and secular law collide – a topic which always promotes lively discussion!

11966.name: Simon Myerson
11966.bio: Simon chaired the Union of Jewish Students in 1985–86 and has led Leeds Jewish Representative Council since 2022. He taught Melton for 11 years. He was called to the Bar in 1986, took silk (became a Queen's Counsel) in 2003 and sat in civil and serious sexual crime for 23 years. He thinks he's on the sensible left and modern side of observance.

12197.name: David Neifeld
12197.bio: David Neifeld is a rabbi and director of the Sephardi Kashrut Authority in London, and director of special projects at the Maimonides Heritage Center in Tiberias, Israel. With a background in rabbinic leadership and communal engagement, he is passionate about making Jewish life accessible and strengthening Jewish identity.

12103.name: Daniel Nevins
12103.bio: Danny Nevins is senior rabbi of New North London Synagogue and is author of 'Torah and Technology: Circuits, Cells, and the Sacred Path' (Izzun Books, 2024). A member of the Rabbinical Assembly's Committee on Jewish Law and Standards since 1999, he writes responsa on topics of contemporary Jewish practice.

12107.name: Karen Newman
12107.bio: Karen Newman is the Board of Deputies of British Jews' vice-president for security, resilience and cohesion. A former Liberal Judaism chair, she helped create the Movement for Progressive Judaism of which she is a trustee and is also a Leo Baeck College governor, Liberal Jewish Synagogue trustee and Jewish LGBT+ Group committee member.

11833.name: Jacqueline Nicholls
11833.bio: Jacqueline is a London-based artist, Jewish educator, award-winning visual poet, and longtime Limmudnik. Founder of The Talmudic Drawing Studio, she teaches traditional Jewish texts using drawing. She was the creative director of Jewish Renaissance’s pilot Artist Development Scheme, and regularly teaches at the London School of Jewish Studies.

12010.name: Gary Ogin
12010.bio: Gary is a London-based scriptwriter and theatre practitioner specialising in comedy-drama for stage and screen. He has written seven plays for the BBC, creating character-led work that blends sharp social observation, emotional truth and humour.

12123.name: Stephen Ogin
12123.bio: Stephen Ogin chairs the Yiddish Café Trust which includes amongst its activities the Yiddish Open Mic Café, the UK Yiddish Sof-Vokh (weekend) and theatre (London Yiddish Shpilers). He is an active supporter of both Yachad and Standing Together, a member of Ealing Liberal Synagogue, and an emeritus professor in the field of engineering materials.

11864.name: Irwin Oppenheim
11864.bio: Irwin is a chazan with the Jewish community of Amsterdam. He is an expert on how Jewish ritual and music have evolved through the ages, and gives a weekly shiur (lesson) on this topic. In daily life, he serves as an IT manager at the dealing room of a Dutch bank.

12044.name: Esra Ozyurek
12044.bio: Esra Özyürek is the Sultan Qaboos Professor of Abrahamic Religions and Shared Values at the Faculty of Divinity, University of Cambridge, and the academic director of the Cambridge Interfaith Programme. Her book 'Subcontractors of Guilt: Holocaust Memory and Muslim Belonging in Postwar Germany' was published by Stanford University Press in 2023.

12128.name: Tal Paley
12128.bio: Tal is an artist and art historian whose work focuses on memory, memorials and storytelling, currently studying an MA in Museum Education. They have previously led workshops combining art history, Jewish culture and practical craft to engage audiences with the past and understand how it can shape what we create today.

11942.name: The Limmud Participant Care Team
11942.bio: The Limmud Participant Care Team looks after the wellbeing of everyone at the festival, running the Wellbeing Hub and its drop-in sessions. The team is co-chaired by Melanie Goldberg and Benjamin Smith.

11895.name: Leon Pein
11895.bio: Participating in, and running, campaign groups from a very early age. Life is one long campaign, especially if you're Jewish: you're guaranteed to have had to explain some quirk or other of Judaism many times.

11900.name: Joanna Phillips
11900.bio: Joanna co-founded the Queer Yeshiva, is a former Jewdas-nik and exchanged several emails with a well-known food publication this year about their use of the term 'bagel'. She loves beigels, matchmaking, the Talmud and when people ask to see a photo of her dog.

12186.name: The Pitbulls
12186.bio: Life is not a waste of time, and time is not a waste of life. So let's stop wasting time, get wasted, and have the time of our lives.

11923.name: Marcia Plumb
11923.bio: Marcia Plumb is co-founder of two Mussar (Jewish ethical practice) organisations, SoulBalanceMussar, UK and A Soul in Balance, USA. She teaches this ancient Jewish wisdom through groups, corporate training, art, workshops for managing polarising conversations, school curricula and individual coaching.

11886.name: Rebecca Posner
11886.bio: Rebecca grew up in Italy and north London. A lifelong feminist with a background in biomedical research, she has just completed a lab-based PhD in Women's Health, and has an active interest in women's roles and education in Judaism, alongside reproductive education generally. Her sessions are dedicated in loving memory of her father Keith Jeremy Posner z"l.

12057.name: Karen Prevezer
12057.bio: Karen has been leyning regularly since her bat mitzvah over 30 years ago. In that time, she has covered every single verse in the Torah, frequently leyning the full sidrah for a given week. Formerly a member of Kol Nefesh Masorti, Karen is now co-chair of the Assif minyan at New North London Synagogue.

12072.name: Marian Prinsley
12072.bio: Marian is the president of the Norwich Hebrew Congregation and a community leader who has successfully restored Norwich Synagogue and continues to build a growing and thriving Jewish community in Norfolk.

12073.name: Peter Prinsley
12073.bio: Peter Prinsley is the Labour member of Parliament for Bury St Edmunds and Stowmarket (elected 2024) and a former consultant ear, nose and throat surgeon at James Paget and Norfolk and Norwich University Hospitals. He sits on the Home Affairs Select Committee and is vice chair of Labour Friends of Israel and a deputy for Norwich.

12048.name: Eliana Pushett
12048.bio: Eliana Pushett is the United Jewish Israel Appeal and Jewish Agency community shlicha (emissary) in the north of the UK. Originally from Jerusalem, she holds degrees in Education and English Literature. Having worked with major Jewish organisations, she is passionate about connecting Israel and global Jewry and strengthening Jewish life.

12094.name: Hanna Radomski
12094.bio: Hanna is a licensed psychotherapist, supervisor and teacher in psychotherapy. Hanna also works as a facilitator at legal psychedelic retreats in the Netherlands. She has extensive experience in supporting participants through psychedelic experiences. Hanna found psychedelics helpful in her own personal connection with Judaism and Jewish identity.

12163.name: Harith Ramli
12163.bio: Harith teaches comparative religion and Islamic history at the Cambridge Muslim College and Usul Academy. He has had more than ten years of experience as a lecturer in various universities in the UK. His research focuses on the historical formation of Islamic intellectual traditions. He also works on curriculum development and game writing.

11881.name: Dov Raphael
11881.bio: Dov Raphael grew up in Liverpool. He immigrated to Israel in 1978, where he works as a consultant actuary, and is also an amateur musician and chorister. In 2022 he received an MA in Jewish music from the Schechter Institute of Jewish Studies, and is currently researching Anglo-Jewish liturgical music at Bar-Ilan University.

11854.name: Poppy Raskolnikoff
11854.bio: A student of the Middle East, Poppy is a trained peace worker and has spent time on the West Bank as a peace volunteer. Israeli-born and Hebrew-speaking, she is keen to spread the message of peace and justice.

12035.name: Alma Reisel
12035.bio: Alma is a systemic psychotherapist working with individuals, families, couples and groups. She's a long-term Limmudnik with a long history of advocacy, education and therapeutic support on topics such as LGBT inclusion, safeguarding and healing from abuse.

11845.name: Samantha Reuben
11845.bio: With an academic and professional background in literature and libraries, Sam manages the library and archives at the London School of Jewish Studies. A keen bibliophile, Sam enjoys literature, and books as physical art forms. Sam has written and performed stand-up comedy, and promises to bring a novel, entertaining voice to her presentations.

11958.name: Yael Roberts
11958.bio: Yael Roberts is a PhD candidate in Creative and Critical Practice at Sussex University where she has received the Morris and Bessie Emanuel Scholarship in Modern Jewish History and Culture for her practice-based research on 19th-century Hasidism and Jewish Diaspora. She has taught with Azara Yeshiva, Miknaf Haaretz and at synagogues across the UK.

12003.name: Jessica Robinson
12003.bio: Jessica is the nature and education lead with EcoJudaism. She engages Jewish adults and children in fun, empowering activities supporting people to understand their relationship to nature as fundamental to their Jewish identity. Jessica has degrees in Environmental Science and Sustainable Development and has worked in the field for over 20 years.

12053.name: Sam Robinson
12053.bio: By day, Sam is a 'Jewish Agent', connecting Jewish communities worldwide – training community leaders in emergency preparedness, crisis response and resilience. By night, Sam bartends and runs a community pub in Jerusalem. In between, Sam is usually bringing people together on a football pitch or over a Shabbat meal with eclectic guests.

12171.name: Jessica Roda
12171.bio: Jessica Roda is an anthropologist, ethnomusicologist, and associate professor of Jewish Civilization at Georgetown University. Author of two monographs, she explores religion, gender, media, and health, focusing on healing, collective trauma, breathwork, and psychedelics in North American Jewish life, including Orthodox and Sephardi communities.

11828.name: Elisa Rodenburg
11828.bio: Elisa Rodenburg has an MA in History and learns Talmud in a small study group with some (emphasis on some) regularity. She enjoys reading, Amsterdam’s monthly Historical Café, swimming, hiking, and visiting libraries at home in the Netherlands and abroad. She also enjoys chatting about all of the above.

12180.name: Rebecca Rogowski
12180.bio: Rebecca Rogowski (she/they) is the senior educator at Hillel Deutschland, holds a BA in Jewish Studies and Comparative Literature, is a Pardes alum, and is currently pursuing an MA in Jewish Education at Hebrew College. They are passionate about inclusive education, Jewish, queer and feminist history, Yiddish and their two cats.

11848.name: Nathan Rogut
11848.bio: Nathan is a behavioural economist at Clifford Chance, helping shape fee-earner behaviour through large-scale transformation aligned with the firm’s strategy. Beyond behavioural economics, he is passionate about Judaism and Jewish identity and enjoys spotting the hidden behavioural nudges shaping everyday life.

12018.name: Jonathan Roiser
12018.bio: Jonathan Roiser is professor of Neuroscience and Mental Health at University College London, where he leads research on the neuroscience of depression, particularly symptoms relating to motivation. He is a big Limmud fan, having attended (on and off) for over 25 years.

11843.name: Jonathan Romain
11843.bio: Jonathan Romain was rabbi of Maidenhead Synagogue before becoming convenor of the Reform Beit Din. A writer and broadcaster, he is chaplain to the Jewish Police Association, president of the Accord Coalition and chair of the Religious Alliance for Dignity in Dying. His latest book is 'A Better Death: The Case for Assisted Dying'.

12124.name: Micha'el Rosenberg
12124.bio: Micha'el Rosenberg is senior director for teen and campus strategy and faculty at Hadar. He has semichah from the Israeli Chief Rabbinate and a Talmud PhD from the Jewish Theological Seminary. He wrote 'Signs of Virginity: Testing Virgins and Making Men in Late Antiquity' and co-wrote 'Gender Equality and Prayer in Jewish Law' with Ethan Tucker.

12082.name: Phil Rosenberg
12082.bio: Phil Rosenberg is the 49th president of the Board of Deputies of British Jews. At 38, he became the youngest ever president in the Board’s 264-year history. Phil is the deputy for Brondesbury Park Synagogue. He is a consultant specialising in government relations, media, faith and diplomacy.

11862.name: Simon Rosenstone
11862.bio: Simon is severely visually impaired (almost from birth), but this does not stop him from enjoying life to the full. He has done several bungee jumps, skydiving and wing walking. He likes to play UNO – he has a braille set, which besides the braille markings is identical to a normal set – and he likes Jenga.

12099.name: Liat Rosenthal
12099.bio: Liat Rosenthal is currently the director of culture, education and communities at the Board of Deputies of British Jews, where she has launched the UK's first-ever Jewish Culture Month. Liat's work includes cultural programming, community engagement and audience development.

12152.name: Aleph Ross
12152.bio: Aleph is a writer and PhD student based at the University of Birmingham. Her research focusses on the history of sexuality, sexual health and medicine in 20th-century Jewish Britain. She is also the co-founder of the cultural non-profit Jargon, which organises events and sells second-hand books around the theme of Jewish Diaspora.

11807.name: Adam Rossano
11807.bio: Adam is a dad of two and a husband of one. While his kids are at school, he works for Limmud as executive director, empowering dozens of volunteers to create inspiring cross-communal Jewish learning gatherings across the UK. He has a BA in Philosophy and Hebrew, and no qualifications but a lot of love for gardening, hiking and playing the trumpet.

11930.name: Jordan Rothschild
11930.bio: Jordan Rothschild is a doctoral student of Sociology at the University of Oxford. His dissertation explores Jewish belonging and communal institutionalisation in Berlin, Germany, specifically on conversion as a site of boundary crossing, and religious affiliation under secularisation. Before academia, Jordan worked at the Foreign Office of Germany.

12119.name: Naomi Russell
12119.bio: Naomi is co-director of outreach and prevention at Jewish Women’s Aid, driving work towards a world without violence against women and girls. She’s led national mental health campaigns and is a qualified psychotherapist. She 'enjoys' watching Spurs and gardening messily with her daughter.
