12206.name: Sarah Sackman
12206.bio: Sarah Sackman is the member of Parliament for Finchley and Golders Green and a justice minister. Brought up in Hampstead Garden Suburb, she has been a Limmud regular over the years. Sarah is passionate about the power of cross-communal Jewish education and the importance of continuing to celebrate Jewish culture in challenging times.

12098.name: Matan Sacofsky
12098.bio: Matan Sacofsky is an English-Israeli visual artist and filmmaker based in Jerusalem. A Sam Spiegel Film School graduate, his work spans figurative oil painting, en plein air landscapes and documentary film. Projects include his Nightscapes exhibition at the Knesset, a Self Portrait series and co-directing the documentary feature Good Morning Gaza.

12114.name: Stephanie Saffer
12114.bio: By day Steph heads up fundraising at a women’s criminal justice charity. She also serves as a trustee of KeshetUK. As a passionate foodie she has previously run her own chocolate business, perfected the recipe for sourdough challah and maintains a stock of pickled, preserved and fermented treats at all times.

12061.name: Leon Saltiel
12061.bio: Leon Saltiel is director of diplomacy and representative at UN Geneva and UNESCO for the World Jewish Congress. He is also a scholar of the Holocaust, specialising in the Greek experience.

11877.name: Michael Samson
11877.bio: Michael Samson is a retired local government solicitor and retired mediator. Being a Jew, born in India, he speaks about the history, culture, heritage and ancestry of the different groups of the Jews of India.

12008.name: Jennifer Sandler
12008.bio: Jenny Sandler is an autism, ADHD and dyslexia specialist teacher and consultant. She supports children, families and schools, and is a governor at a Jewish primary school and a specialist autism school. She holds master’s degrees in literacy difficulties and autism and is writing a book for grandparents of autistic and ADHD children.

12007.name: Jonathan Sandler
12007.bio: Jonathan Sandler is the author of the graphic memoir 'The English GI' and founder of the GraphicMEMOIRBlog, where he has interviewed over 100 graphic novel creators around the globe. Based in London, he also works with Mensch Publishing to develop new graphic memoir projects and nurture emerging visual storytellers.

11887.name: Dahlia Scheindlin
11887.bio: Dahlia Scheindlin is a public opinion expert who has advised nine national campaigns in Israel and in 15 other countries over 25 years. She is a senior analyst for Haaretz, a policy fellow at Century International, and the author of 'The Crooked Timber of Democracy in Israel: Promise Unfulfilled'. She is a longtime member of A Land for All.

11991.name: Nikki Scheiner
11991.bio: Nikki Scheiner is a consultant psychologist specialising in functional neurological disorders (formerly medically unexplained symptoms). Her interest in the health legacy of Jewish persecution and migration is informed by her work on the intersection of psyche and soma, and her previous career as a historian of Enlightenment Spain.

12083.name: Astrid Schmetterling
12083.bio: Astrid Schmetterling is an art historian and author. She was senior lecturer in Visual Cultures at Goldsmiths, University of London until 2026. Her writing focuses on the relation between history, culture, and memory, and is informed by the insights of Diaspora, postcolonial and transcultural memory studies.

12104.name: Avi Schneebalg
12104.bio: Avi is a 71-year-old (they say he looks younger, though) retired lawyer, mediator, civil judge and lecturer based in Brussels, Belgium, a father and a grandfather. Fifty years ago, he was secretary-general of the Union of Jewish Students in Belgium and co-founder of the European Union of Jewish Students.

12190.name: Amos Schonfield
12190.bio: Amos is a community builder and charity leader. He helped to convene V'Ahavta: Jews Against the Far Right after having seen the impact of the far right on our communities and neighbours. He is the founder and CEO of Our Second Home, the UK's refugee youth movement, and has worked, volunteered, and been a trustee in the Jewish community since 2009.

12208.name: Daniel Schwammenthal
12208.bio: Daniel Schwammenthal edits The Jewish Chronicle. Previously, he headed the American Jewish Committee’s EU office in Brussels and was an editorial writer and op-ed editor at The Wall Street Journal Europe. Born in Germany, he studied in Aachen, Boston and Manchester, earning degrees in Political Science, International Relations and European Law.

11873.name: Aaron Joseph Seitler
11873.bio: Aaron Seitler is an educator living in Jerusalem. A first-class History graduate of University College London, he served as an IDF paratrooper and developed a course on Rabbi Sacks' thought. He writes for the Jewish Chronicle, Jerusalem Post and Times of Israel. Aaron is completing an MA in Jewish Thought and serves as an IDF reservist.

12188.name: Carlos Johanan Seynave
12188.bio: Johanan Seynave is managing director at Schwartz and Lumbrozo, a Brussels-based EU affairs consultancy. He is a jurist, researcher and policy expert who has held several positions at Jewish organisations, where he has contributed to shaping the policy landscape with regard to combating antisemitism and fostering Jewish life.

11939.name: The Limmud Shabbat Team
11939.bio: The Limmud Shabbat team is co-chaired by Avital and Eden, who are so excited to be at festival and to share their favourite parts of Shabbat with you. They love exploring new traditions and new tunes, and bringing together the Shabbat-mosphere from all corners of the globe. If you see them sprinting round the Hilton, come say hi!

12101.name: Janine Shalev
12101.bio: Janine Shalev is a conflict transformation trainer, mediator and coach working with Nonviolent Communication (NVC), a needs-centred approach to conflict. Her recent work has focused on the polarising impact of the Israel/Palestine conflict, helping people and communities navigate difficult conversations and move beyond entrenched positions.

11823.name: Marvin Shaw
11823.bio: Marvin J Shaw has recently designed three new wellbeing courses which you can taste here at Festival. Marvin is absolutely delighted to launch his eighth book, '200 Poems To Boost Your Mood – and other stories', here at Limmud and will accept any offers of a l'chaim (coffee of course!) to help him celebrate.

11844.name: Sybil Sheridan
11844.bio: Sybil Sheridan has been a rabbi serving many Progressive Jewish communities in a career spanning 45 years. Currently living in Oxford, she continues to teach and preach, engaged in Bible study, women’s studies, interfaith and social action. She is a founder of the charity Meketa, supporting Jews in Ethiopia.

11922.name: Michael Shire
11922.bio: Michael Shire teaches at Hebrew College Boston and is rabbi at Central Reform Temple Boston. He is a trustee of The Pursuit of History which organises a Limmud-type event annually in Boston named 'History Camp'. He is the founder of Torah Godly Play, a Torah storytelling methodology.

11839.name: Liubov Sigalova
11839.bio: Liubov Sigalova is a professional organiser based in the Netherlands. Previously, she worked in Jewish education and community projects with Taglit, Hillel Moscow and ORT, as an educator and project manager. Today, she brings these two worlds together, exploring how our homes can support the lives, traditions and memories that matter to us.

12051.name: Moshe Silver
12051.bio: Moshe Silver is a rabbi on the faculty at Jerusalem's Pardes Institute, where he teaches Maimonides and leads prayer workshops, connecting the ancient texts to contemporary life. He is active in interfaith work, and in Jerusalem social justice initiatives. His book is 'The Weight of Gold'.

12172.name: Yosef Silver
12172.bio: Wherever Yosef has lived, in the UK, Israel or the US, people end up around his table. Now it’s his job: he leads marketing, brand and data at Brighton and Hove Jewish Community, bringing fresh energy to Jewish Brighton. He splits his time between Brighton and Kansas City, home to his three kids and agency. He’s happiest on a plane or in a kitchen.

11837.name: Paul Silver-Myer
11837.bio: Having spent his working life in accountancy, Paul Silver-Myer retrained as a psychotherapist and now combines preparing tax returns for therapists with a private therapy practice. He is also a financial coach and mediator. Paul is a former treasurer of Liberal Judaism and a past chair and now president of Finchley Progressive Synagogue.

11937.name: Zoe Silverman
11937.bio: Zoe is an award-winning chartered architect (Royal Institute of British Architects) with over two decades of experience delivering exceptional building projects across the residential, education, and commercial sectors. She leads the successful practice ZED Architect and regularly presents at Limmud on architectural history, theory, and design.

12093.name: Claire Silverstone-Bright
12093.bio: Claire Silverstone-Bright is a criminologist, writer and advocate with lived experience of the criminal justice system. A proud shammas (synagogue warden) at New London Synagogue, she participated in the Masorti mission to Israel. Her work explores rehabilitation, identity, belonging and what Jewish ideas of teshuvah (repentance) mean in practice.

12088.name: Yishai Simansky
12088.bio: Yishai Simansky is an Israeli educator and Jewish communal professional, leading the Jewish Agency’s aliyah team for the UK and Western Europe. A former World Zionist Organisation shaliach (emissary) in London and Vienna, he lives with his family in Leshem, Israel, and is currently writing a book based on the testimony of a Holocaust survivor.

11919.name: Anna Simons
11919.bio: Anna Simons is a charity sector consultant specialising in organisational change projects and leadership development. She is currently working with the Jewish Leadership Council and the Jewish News to build The JQ – an AI-powered online HQ designed to bring the richness of UK Jewish life together in one welcoming digital home.

11999.name: Gershom Sizomu
11999.bio: Gershom Sizomu is the chief rabbi and spiritual leader of the Abayudaya Congregation in Uganda. He was ordained at the Ziegler School of Rabbinic Studies in May 2008. In February 2016, he was elected as a member of the Ugandan parliament, and in August 2025 was elected as the first Ugandan delegate to the World Zionist Congress.

11954.name: Peter Slowe
11954.bio: Peter Slowe has written many books including 'Geography and Political Power' and the biography of Manny Shinwell. His latest is 'Projects Abroad and the Invention of Mass Overseas Volunteering', explaining how he founded Projects Abroad and gave hundreds of thousands of young people the opportunity to volunteer in the developing world.

11853.name: Jeremy Smilg
11853.bio: Jeremy Smilg enjoyed a career in the City before eventually escaping and earning a PhD in the reaction of the Jewish community of England to the French Revolution.

11995.name: Josh Smith
11995.bio: Josh Smith is one of the Limmud volunteer co-chairs, who are responsible for the organisation of all Limmud volunteering, including the Yad programme and ad-hoc volunteering, as well as the experience and wellbeing of all volunteers.

11940.name: The Limmud Social Programming Team
11940.bio: Consider Miki Friend and Annie Whiteson your social maestros, cruise directors, harbingers of chaos, for Limmud '26. Whether you're here to make some friends, meet a lover, or uncover the mysteries the Hilton Metropole has to offer, social programming is for you. Come and visit us at the kiosk in the back of the bar to get socially programmed!

12137.name: Jessica Spencer
12137.bio: Jessica Spencer is a co-founder of Azara and visiting rabbi for Leeds Masorti. She was ordained by Hebrew College and by Yashrut, and is currently studying for a PhD in Talmud at Columbia University. Jessica co-wrote 'Poem haShavua', a collection of poems on the weekly Torah portion. She likes eating bread and longs for a Kenwood mixer of her own.

11846.name: Sophia Spiegel
11846.bio: Sophia Spiegel is the lay leader of the Cork Jewish Community, Ireland. She is a Jewish educator and her passion for education is reflected in the classes she teaches. Sophia is a board member and co-chair of Limmud Europe and co-chair of Limmud Ireland.

12138.name: Benji Stanley
12138.bio: Benji is director of learning at Azara, a non-denominational beit midrash (house of study). He was rabbi of Westminster for eight years before serving as rabbinic fellow at Pardes. He loves reading closely and communally. He lives in London with his partner, Leah, their daughter Jules, and baby Marlowe. He studied at Oxford and Leo Baeck College.

11975.name: Janine Stein
11975.bio: Janine Stein is a writer, advertising copywriter and communications professional. In between working and studying Talmud, she wrote a book tracing her family from a shtetl in Eastern Europe across the world. Using archives, memoirs and interviews, she uncovered what happened to two brothers and six sisters scattered by history.

11961.name: Peter Stein
11961.bio: Peter W. Stein leads Temple B’rith Kodesh in Rochester, New York. He was ordained at the Hebrew Union College-Jewish Institute of Religion. Peter teaches at the Colgate Rochester Crozer Divinity School and is a member of the North American board of the Central Conference of American Rabbis.

11847.name: Josi Steinfeld
11847.bio: Josi Steinfeld is a London-based opera specialist, lecturer and critic for playstosee.com. A professional lawyer and opera singer, she obtained an opera degree at Rose Bruford College 20 years ago and has since given illustrated opera talks, combining her insights as a singer with live singing.

11863.name: Sharon Stiefel
11863.bio: Sharon Stiefel was ordained at the Reconstructionist Rabbinical College and is rabbi of Mayim Rabim, the only Reconstructionist congregation in Minneapolis, Minnesota. A rabbi and licensed graduate social worker, she brings Jewish tradition and pastoral care together. She and her wife, Davida Alperin, live in St Paul and have two adult children.

11925.name: Andrew Stone
11925.bio: Andrew Stone is a father, husband and solicitor who has lived in south Manchester for over 17 years. Having trained in karate for much of his youth, after an extended gap, he started again with his daughter, Eliana, about four years ago. Eliana loves nothing more than showing how she has progressed by seeing if her dad can take one of her punches.

11926.name: Eliana Queen Esther Stone
11926.bio: Eliana has been practising karate for over four years, and is currently a 1st kyu (senior brown belt). This is her sixth Limmud, and her second time presenting. She is looking forward to showing you some of the kihon, or basics, of Shotokan karate.

11867.name: Helen Stone
11867.bio: Helen Stone is a founder member of the Holocaust charity Generation 2 Generation. She is a retired secondary teacher and is one of Generation 2 Generation's 46 presenters. She has presented her mother Emmy Golding's story to countless schools and other organisations and also teaches English to refugees and asylum seekers.

11977.name: Maurice Stone
11977.bio: Maurice is chairman of the Israeli Dance Institute (IDI). He has been teaching dance for many years at Limmud in the UK, Russia and Ukraine. He believes that Israeli dance is a fundamental educational tool promoting Jewish identity and a connection with Israel. So, let’s dance!

11866.name: Robert Stone
11866.bio: Robert Stone is a historian and political economist with a lifelong fascination with how people of different religions and cultures relate to each other, developed during a career advising governments on how to fight poverty, particularly in the wake of conflicts. He is the author of 'The Golden Bell', a novel set in the medieval Mediterranean.

11964.name: Claire Straus
11964.bio: Claire is a career coach and workshop facilitator involved in Limmud’s constructive disagreement work. She’s interested in how we talk, listen and connect, and increasingly troubled by the way we disagree. An off-the-scale introvert, she’s curious about conversation: what gets in the way and what helps. Preferably over coffee.

11929.name: Abbie Strauss
11929.bio: Abbie Strauss is a cantor, composer and recording artist whose work is enjoyed worldwide. She co-founded Tamid Palm Beach and founded the music school The Institute of Jewish Rock, driven by a desire to bring people together in joy through music. She is a proud member of the Grammys' Recording Academy and an advocate for the arts.

11858.name: Pavlina Sulcova (Schultz)
11858.bio: Pavlína Šulcová (Schultz) is a creative producer and co-author of 'Talmud Digest' and other comics. She founded Judaism Fun Again to make Jewish heritage more accessible. She is an alumna of Paideia in Stockholm and Pardes in Jerusalem where she fell in love with Talmud and its tradition of debate, interpretation, and storytelling.

11898.name: Roni Tabick
11898.bio: Roni Tabick is the rabbi of New Stoke Newington Shul, a fun and vibrant Masorti community in east London. He was ordained in New York by the Jewish Theological Seminary where he spent much of his time developing his deep interest in myths, monsters and mysticism. Roni's first book is a Jewish fantasy novel called 'Radiance'.

12056.name: Andres Tassara
12056.bio: Continental shaliach (emissary) of the World Betar Movement and the Jewish Agency for Israel.

12105.name: Maryanne Taylor
12105.bio: Maryanne is a sleep consultant and founder of The Sleep Works. For over 15 years she has helped children, teens and adults get better sleep. She combines sleep science with practical advice for getting to bed, overloaded minds and those 3am wake-ups. Since teaming up with Miriam Berger, she’s discovered the rabbis knew quite a bit about sleep too!

11850.name: Lindsey Taylor-Guthartz
11850.bio: Lindsey is a teaching associate at the Faculty of Divinity, Cambridge University, and is writing a biography of Limmud. In 2021 she received semichah from Maharat, and published her book 'Challenge and Conformity: The Religious Lives of Orthodox Jewish Women'. She's a co-founder of Azara, an initiative creating Jewish text learning for everyone.

12063.name: Avihud Tidhar
12063.bio: Avihud Tidhar is a theatre-maker, educator, and programme coordinator at KeshetUK, leading on the Belonging in Ritual project. An actor, director, dramaturg, and play translator into Hebrew, his creative practice centres on storytelling, living text, and the intersection of Jewish and LGBT+ lives.

12006.name: Luz Toff
12006.bio: Luz takes a holistic approach to everything she does, from learning and teaching Torah to healthy living. Luz is a graduate of Yeshivat Maharat, having had the opportunity to learn and teach in a range of Jewish educational settings. She is passionate about making Jewish learning and practice meaningful, relevant and accessible.

12201.name: Gilad E. Troy
12201.bio: Senior fellow in Zionist Thought at the Jewish People Policy Institute, a global Jewish think tank, and distinguished scholar in North American History at McGill. An award-winning American presidential historian and leading Zionist thinker, he is the author of nine books on American history and nine on Zionism, including 'The Zionist Ideas'.

11946.name: Persephone Tsebelis
11946.bio: Persephone is a sudoku and mahjong enthusiast.

12084.name: Dan Turek
12084.bio: Dan is a musical supervisor, musical director and conductor. He recently supervised four new shows in The Bazaar, an immersive space on Celebrity Cruises' latest ship, Xcel. He was musical director for the Olivier Award-winning production of Fiddler on the Roof at Regent's Park Open Air Theatre and the Barbican Theatre.

11820.name: Lester Max van Ravenswade
11820.bio: Physician in daily life at a plastic/reconstructive surgery department. Founder of the Jewish Medical Initiative Foundation. Overall a passionate (Modern Orthodox) Jew with a love for people, learning and understanding.

12022.name: Yona Verwer
12022.bio: Yona Verwer is a Dutch-born, New York-based artist who turns ancient stories into a lens on today’s biggest questions: Who are we? Where do we belong? And how do we care for a changing world? Drawing on heritage, spirituality, migration, and ecology, her work has been exhibited in more than 35 museums worldwide.

12166.name: Julia Vogl
12166.bio: Julia Vogl is an international printmaker and public artist focused on community engagement. Her commissions reflect the individual and collective aspects of humanity through colour, play and contemplation. Commissioned by Tate, ITV, Facebook, Hull City of Culture, Jewish Arts Collaborative in Boston USA, and currently the JW3 in London.

12086.name: Adam Wagner
12086.bio: Adam Wagner is a King's Counsel (KC) and barrister at Doughty Street Chambers and a visiting professor of Law at City St George's, University of London.

12087.name: Julia Wagner
12087.bio: Julia Wagner is a lecturer and writer specialising in film. She is the author of 'Hester Street' (BFI Film Classics, Bloomsbury 2025). She also loves to sing.

11894.name: Michael Wahnon
11894.bio: Long-time attendee, first-time presenter, incredibly tired, Michael Wahnon is a PhD researcher in the field of Nuclear and Chemical Engineering at the University of Leeds. To find out more, go and find him, he's fairly easy to spot.

11871.name: Lewis Warshauer
11871.bio: Lewis is a long-time Limmudnik and presenter. Based in New York, he's a graduate of Jewish Theological Seminary Rabbinical School and an independent Jewish studies teacher for adults. His particular interests include midrash and the arts.

11840.name: Ben Webber-Lewis
11840.bio: Ben is a long-time Limmud volunteer, having co-chaired Festival in 2019. He holds a PhD in Chemical Biology from Imperial College London and currently works as a civil servant.

12058.name: Chaim Weiner
12058.bio: Chaim Weiner heads the European Masorti Bet Din and works with over 50 Jewish communities around Europe. He is part of the rabbinical team at New North London Synagogue. His Jewish Journeys tours bring Jewish history to life through studying traditional sources in the places they were written.

12060.name: Daniel Tal Weininger
12060.bio: Danny is head of professional development (North America) at the National Library of Israel, building global educational partnerships around the library's vast collections. He holds an MA in Jewish Thought and rabbinic ordination, with extensive experience of designing and delivering learning programmes across Israel, Europe, and the US.

12126.name: Lilach Nofar Weiss
12126.bio: Lilach is a sociologist and anthropologist (Hebrew University) and certified dance movement therapist, experienced in activism, group facilitation and community organising. A graduate and co-facilitator of Seeds of Partnership Jewish–Palestinian co-leadership programmes, she is active in Standing Together, advocating for peace and social justice.

11893.name: Jonathan Weissbart
11893.bio: Jonathan has presented many sessions over the years drawing on his knowledge and experience of Jewish and liturgical music. More recently he has been broadening his knowledge to cover music composed by Jews, but not necessarily in the Jewish sphere.

11882.name: Andrew Winter
11882.bio: Andrew Winter has been playing the violin since early childhood. He has led many orchestras and ensembles. Andrew's performances at Princes Road Synagogue in Liverpool have included concerts celebrating Jewish music and musical heritage. His violin was made in 1802 in France by Nicolas Lupot who was one of the greatest violin makers of his time.

12193.name: Irene Wise
12193.bio: Artist Irene Wise was senior lecturer in Media and Culture at the University of Roehampton, where she ran courses in art, literature and film. She is an Imperial War Museum fellow in Holocaust Education and has worked and advised on Holocaust films. Irene writes blogs and reviews for Jewish Renaissance. Irene’s artwork can be viewed on her website.

12146.name: Jonathan Wittenberg
12146.bio: For 40 years rabbi at the New North London Synagogue, which he loved, now senior rabbi of Masorti Judaism. Loves people, animals, trees and plants. Cares about refugees, environment, compassion and justice. Founder of EcoJudaism. If possible, goes nowhere without his dog Nessie. Loves his family.

11912.name: Gabriel Yom-Tov
11912.bio: Gabriel Gendler Yom-Tov is a London-based mathematician and rebbetzin. He has taught at the Fuchsberg Center, Yeshivat Hadar, and Azara. He tries to teach one serious shiur and one silly shiur every Limmud. Can you tell which is which?

12191.name: Yossi Zabari
12191.bio: Yossi Zabari is a comedian and spoken-word artist who has performed for over two decades across Israel, Europe and the US. His work blends stand-up, storytelling and spoken word. He has also appeared on Israeli television. His new English-language solo show, 'A Jew on the Run', is currently touring internationally.

12136.name: Levona Zarum
12136.bio: Raphi is president of the Union of Jewish Students for 2026/27. Passionate, committed and open-minded, Raphi’s time at the University of Warwick, where he studied Philosophy, was dedicated to building thriving Jewish student communities.

11832.name: Raphael Zarum
11832.bio: Dean, London School of Jewish Studies, where he also holds the Rabbi Sacks Chair in Modern Jewish Thought. A rabbi and Physics PhD, his book 'Questioning Belief' won a Yeshiva University Prize. Hosts the 'Big Questions of Jewish Belief' podcast. Wildly creative international lecturer. His new book, 'Big Questions, Brief Answers', is out soon.

12028.name: Yonatan Zeigen
12028.bio: Yonatan Zeigen is a social worker and father of three. After losing his mother, Vivian Silver, on 7 October and being heartbroken by the war in general, he decided to dedicate himself to co-resistance, peace and reconciliation. He is on the board of the Parents Circle–Families Forum and a candidate for the party 'A Place for Us All'.

11986.name: Ariella Zeitlin
11986.bio: Ariella Zeitlin is an award-winning Israeli violinist, singer and storyteller who creates joyful, moving experiences rooted in Jewish music and identity. Through concerts, workshops and her Inner Circle community, she brings people together to find courage, connection and a renewed sense of Jewish pride.

12002.name: Amir Ziv
12002.bio: Amir Ziv grew up in Jerusalem and served in the IDF as a combat soldier and commander before becoming active with Breaking the Silence in 2013. As director of pedagogy, he shapes the organisation’s educational content and engagement strategy, connecting testimony to broader questions of equality, accountability and the moral costs of military rule.

12091.name: Omer Zonenshine
12091.bio: Omer Zonenshine is an educator and community leader with over 15 years of experience in the field of non-formal education. Omer is a graduate of the Israeli Rabbinical Seminary at the Hartman Institute.
